Article.Title: A GIS-based multi-criteria decision analysis for identifying optimal geothermal power plant sites: a case study of the Gulf of Suez, Egypt
Article.Authors: Gomaa S.; Eissa M.; Abo Khashaba S.; Mostafa W.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Gulf of Suez is a geologically significant rift basin, characterized by Miocene-age formations that formed through extensional tectonics during the Tertiary period, ultimately facilitating the divergence of the Arabian Peninsula from the African continent. This region has considerable geothermal potential, making it a strategically valuable asset for developing clean, sustainable energy infrastructure. The present study proposes an integrated spatial suitability framework employing Geographic Information Systems (GIS) coupled with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to delineate optimal sites for geothermal power plant development within the study area. In the context of escalating global energy demands, geothermal energy, defined as terrestrial heat extracted from the Earth’s crust through deep drilling and surface fluid transport, represents a viable pathway toward energy transition. The analytical framework was constructed from subsurface thermal data derived from 52 hydrocarbon wells, enabling the computation of geothermal gradients at varying depths and heat flow assessments. The Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was applied to nine (geothermal gradient, heat flow, fault density, geology, seismic activity, proximity to the electricity grid, proximity to roads, land use, and slope) spatially explicit criteria encompassing thermal, geological, topographic, environmental, and infrastructural parameters, each assigned relative weights commensurate with its significance. A robust correlation (R= 0.975) was established between subsurface temperature and depth, yielding a mean geothermal gradient of 48.5 °C/km (R² = 0.9509) and affirming the reliability of the thermal model. The resulting suitability analysis demonstrates that the Gulf of Suez region possesses favorable conditions for the deployment of both Flash Steam and Binary Cycle power plant technologies. Along the eastern coastal corridor, localities including Hammam Faraun, Ras Sudr, and Abu Zenima were identified as suitable for Flash Steam systems at drilling depths of 3,000–4,000 m, corresponding to reservoir temperatures of 140–210 °C, while Binary Cycle systems are applicable at depths of 2,000–3,000 m with temperatures ranging from 100 to 160 °C. On the western coast, sites encompassing Ras Gharib, Ras Shukeir, Jabal al-Zeit, and Jabal Ataqa are technically viable for Flash Steam technology at depths of 3,000–4,000 m and temperatures of 140–210 °C, with supplementary Binary Cycle suitability observed at depths of 2,000–3,000 m and temperatures of 100–180 °C. Zones exclusively suited for Binary Cycle applications include Ayoun Moussa, Wadi Baaba, Wadi Feiran, and Wadi El-Tor to the east, and Zaafarana, Wadi Dara, and Wadi Araba to the west, at depths of 3,000–4,000 m with temperatures ranging between 100 and 160 °C and 100–155 °C, respectively. Northern portions of the study area, characterized by comparatively subdued geothermal gradients, are deemed appropriate for direct-use applications, including space heating, light industrial operations, and residential thermal supply.

Article.Title: Exploratory QSPR analysis of physicochemical properties of selected antifungal agents using topological indices
Article.Authors: Asim M.; Mufti Z.; Almehizia A.; Assiri A.; Ganati G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe structural-property relationships are key in the study of the physicochemical behavior of pharmaceuticals. The degree-based topological indices available through molecular graph theory are used to investigate the structure-property analysis of selected antimycotic agents in a quantitative way in this work. The molecular graphs of ten antimycotic agents were constructed, and several degree-based indices including$$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$F^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$Y^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$S^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$G^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$P^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$HM^\alpha _1(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$HM^\alpha _2(\Upsilon ^o)$$, and$$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$were computed to describe their structural characteristics. To enhance descriptive reliability, this study introduces a novel integration of degree-based topological descriptors with comprehensive multivariate statistical techniques—combining linear regression, correlation profiling, and dimensionality reduction to evaluate structural-property dependencies. Statistical methods were applied to examine the connection between molecular structure and various physicochemical properties, including density, boiling point, enthalpy of vaporization, refractive index, molar refractivity, polarizability, molecular volume, surface tension, and atomic mass. The strength of the associations between topological descriptors and physicochemical parameters were analyzed using regression analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson analysis, and Spearman analysis of correlation. The accuracy of the fitted regression models was quantitatively evaluated for all parameters and showed to be property-dependent. The range of the standard model error metrics were:$$\textrm{MAE} = 0.0234$$–161.7920 and$$\textrm{RMSE} = 0.0298$$–262.6852 which scale directly with the magnitude of the target physicochemical properties. Furthermore, Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation yielded cross-validated performance metrics spanning$$Q^2_{\textrm{LOO}} = -2.1417$$to 0.3514, with associated errors bounded by$$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}MAE} = 0.0320$$to 191.2633 and$$\mathrm {LOOCV\text {-}RMSE} = 0.0371$$to 304.5087. Moreover, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to reduce data dimensionality and identify the most informative descriptors. These findings indicate that a number of topological indices have strong positive correlations with significant physicochemical characteristics, especially those of boiling point, molar refractivity, molecular volume, and atomic mass. Among descriptors that were examined, the most consistent correlations with physicochemical properties of antimycotic agents are observed in$$M^o_1(\Upsilon ^o)$$,$$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$, and$$HF^o(\Upsilon ^o)$$, where$$M^o_2(\Upsilon ^o)$$achieved strong descriptive performance for polarizability ($$R^2 = 0.989$$,$$\textrm{RMSE} = 22.8565$$,$$\textrm{MAE} = 17.7267$$).. The analysis of the results of PCA indicates that the first two principal components cover about 82 percent of the total variance and, therefore, the cumulative structural and physicochemical descriptors are effective in distinguishing the targeted compounds. Overall, the results indicate that degree-based topological indices are reliable descriptor of the physicochemical behavior of antimycotic agents and serve as effective tools in computational drug development and structure-property prediction.

Article.Title: Establishing a reflective-formative higher-order measurement model for the Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF)
Article.Authors: Wong B.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGiven that model misspecification threatens the validity of constructs and distorts statistical findings, in the context of Smartphone Addiction Inventory-Short Form (SPAI-SF), this study investigates whether smartphone addiction construct should be modelled using reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) or reflective-formative approach (Type II model). Drawing on theoretical criteria such as (1) direction of causality, (2) interchangeability of the indicators, (3) correlation/covariation among the indicators, and (4) the relationship of indicators with other constructs, this study has specified smartphone addiction as a second-order reflective-formative construct. To verify this model specification, data was collected from undergraduate students at a Chinese university and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), confirmatory tetrad analysis (CTA-PLS), and several recently developed model fit indices (SRMR, d_ULS, d_G). The results have not only determined that reflective-formative approach (Type II model) is more appropriate than reflective-reflective approach (Type I model) for modelling smartphone addiction construct but also provided strong evidence for construct validity. This study makes a significant theoretical and methodological contribution to the smartphone addiction literature by emphasizing the importance of considering the formative nature of the smartphone addiction construct when designing research frameworks.

Article.Title: Analysis of building seismic damage characteristics and topographic amplification effects of the 2026 Diebu Ms5.5 earthquake
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang J.; Wang P.; Wang Q.; Su W.; Zhang X.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractOn January 26, 2026, an Ms5.5 shallow-focus earthquake occurred in Diebu County, Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, Gansu Province. The affected area lies within the alpine gorge of the Bailong River on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau, a region characterized by rugged topography and complex geological conditions that are typically prone to topographic amplification of ground motion. To address how topographic and site conditions control ground-motion amplification and the resulting spatial distribution of seismic damage, this study selected Dianga Town in Diebu County—the area covered by the earthquake damage survey—as the study area. Field damage surveys, seismic station monitoring data, and FLAC3D three-dimensional numerical simulations were integrated to systematically reveal the relationships among ground-motion amplification, building damage, and slope deformation. Results indicate that the seismic intensity in the study area reached VI–VII on the Chinese seismic intensity scale. Ground-motion amplification was closely associated with the spatially non-uniform distribution of seismic damage: at steep cliffs, slope shoulders, and high-elevation sites, peak ground acceleration (PGA) amplification factors approached 2.0, and buildings at these locations experienced significantly more severe damage than those at other sites. Seismic loading also altered the shear strain distribution pattern of the slope, causing the zone of concentrated shear strain to redistribute and extend toward the residential area. Topographic relief, excavation-induced free faces, and elevation differences were identified as the primary factors contributing to topographic amplification in the studied alpine gorge; in particular, an elevation difference of only about 100 m produced pronounced differences in seismic damage. These findings qualitatively reveal the mechanism of ground-motion amplification and provide a scientific basis for seismic fortification and geological hazard mitigation in villages and towns within alpine gorge areas on the eastern margin of the Tibetan Plateau.

Article.Title: HSP90AA1 induces M2 macrophage polarization via stabilizing ITGB1 and promoting CCL2 secretion in nasopharyngeal carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ding M.; Wang C.; Cao X.; Zong D.; Mao Y.; Wang W.; Ni X.; He X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractNasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) presents a major treatment challenge, largely due to immunotherapy resistance. The molecular mechanisms that drive the remodeling of the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in NPC are still not well understood. This study explored how heat shock protein 90 alpha family class A member 1 (HSP90AA1) regulated the NPC immune microenvironment. A total of 54 NPC patients receiving first-line immunotherapy were analyzed by immunohistochemistry (IHC). High HSP90AA1 expression predicted shorter progression-free survival (PFS). According to the TIMER database, HSP90AA1 expression positively correlated with M2 macrophage infiltration. Additionally, we established an indirect co-culture model containing NPC cells and THP-1-derived macrophages and found that HSP90AA1 facilitated macrophage M2 polarization. According to the results of co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and cycloheximide (CHX) chase assays, HSP90AA1 associated with integrin β1 (ITGB1) and stabilized its protein expression, subsequently increasing C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 (CCL2) secretion. HSP90AA1 knockdown suppressed CCL2 secretion and M2 polarization, and ITGB1 overexpression partially reversed this effect. Taken together, our in vitro models and retrospective clinical correlation suggest that the HSP90AA1-ITGB1-CCL2 axis may drive immunosuppressive TME remodeling in NPC, highlighting HSP90AA1 as a promising predictive biomarker and therapeutic target against immunotherapy resistance.

Article.Title: Feasibility and expert evaluation of a medical large language model in an interdisciplinary clinical board
Article.Authors: Ronicke M.; Sollfrank L.; Sagonas I.; Atreya R.; Grieshaber-Bouyer R.; Hoerning A.; Jefremow A.; Kowalski I.; Krickau T.; Lermer J.; Meidenbauer N.; Rech J.; Rothhammer V.; Schley G.; Sondermann W.; Sticherling M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractInterdisciplinary clinical boards (ICB) on chronic inflammatory diseases discuss complicated and multidisciplinary cases with inflammatory conditions among experts in their discipline. Medically specialized large language models (LLMs) are finding increasingly widespread use among physicians to answer clinical questions. LLMs offer the potential to close the gap between rapidly expanding medical knowledge and limited time of physicians by providing evidence-based summaries to clinical questions and enable “real-time” literature search. However, it is unclear if LLMs can be implemented in clinical routine of ICB. In this prospective study, 100 consecutive real-world cases were discussed in our ICB. Each case was first discussed independently of the LLM and a preliminary recommendation was documented. The clinical question was then entered in the LLM “OpenEvidence”, the answer was reviewed by the board with the opportunity to add aspects not previously raised, and the recommendation was subsequently confirmed as final. Each participating expert evaluated the answer of the LLM using a questionnaire comprising eight Likert scale (1–5) items and one free-text item. Two physicians, blinded to each other, additionally evaluated outputs for their agreement with the board’s decision. The same cases were evaluated after prompt optimization at two different time points. The 100 discussed cases resulted in 759 rater-case evaluations. A mean of 2.3 specialties were directly involved in each case. The highest score was achieved by the item “OpenEvidence provided clinically relevant information for this case.” (4.06). Recommendation for future use achieved a mean score of 3.95. Complete agreement of the LLM answer with the final recommendation of the ICB was rated in 40.2% and 50.5% of all evaluable cases (n= 97) by the two raters. When restricted to consensus cases, i.e. cases rated identically by both raters (n= 62 of 97), complete agreement was 51.6%. Outputs after prompt optimization tended to be associated with higher agreement, but did not reach statistical significance. Outputs were not stable over time. The integration of OpenEvidence into an ICB was feasible and was perceived as useful by the participating specialists, with partial or complete concordance with the final board recommendation in the majority of evaluable cases. As the study did not assess patient outcomes, clinical harm or hallucinations, no conclusions on patient safety can be drawn. The LLM was naturally limited by the information provided in the prompt. Inadequate questions or missing information led to suboptimal answers, highlighting the importance of identifying and including relevant information beforehand. Expert oversight remains essential. Model drift of LLMs may outweigh prompt optimization.

Article.Title: Enhanced anti-ESKAPE pathogen and antibiofilm activities of Korean red ginseng-derived silver nanoparticles via membrane deformation: LC/HRMS profiling and dynamic correlations
Article.Authors: Aati S.; Bahr H.; Aati H.; Rajan S.; Shari F.; Sayed A.; Hassan H.; Basyony A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRed Ginseng is widely recognized for its diverse pharmacological activities, which are largely attributed to its ginsenoside content. A commercial processed Korean Red Ginseng extract product (HO3), hereafter referred to as “HO3 extract”, was used throughout this study. HO3 extract was analyzed using LC-HR-MS to evaluate and profile its ginsenoside content. LC-HR-MS analysis tentatively identified six major ginsenosides, namely Rh1, Rh2, Rg1, Rg2, Rg3, and Rb1. Subsequently, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) incorporating HO3 extract were synthesized and analyzed using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), spectroscopy ultraviolet–visible (UV–Vis) spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), zeta potential measurements, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited a characteristic absorption band at 420 nm, indicating nanoparticle formation, while FTIR analysis revealed the presence of functional groups involved in nanoparticle stabilization. The antibacterial and antibiofilm activities of HO3 extract and HO3-mediated AgNPs were subsequently evaluated. Antibacterial assessment demonstrated that AgNPs significantly outperformed HO3 extract, exhibiting higher inhibition percentages and lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive pathogens. Furthermore, biofilm inhibition assays revealed markedly greater suppression by AgNPs (55–75%) than by HO3 extract (7–16%), with the highest activity observed against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Time-kill assays further demonstrated that the antibacterial efficacy of AgNPs was both dose- and time-dependent. Moreover, the identified major ginsenosides were subjected to molecular dynamics (MD) simulations against microbial membrane models to predict their potential antimicrobial mechanisms. Notably, ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 exhibited the strongest membrane-disruptive effects, inducing substantial bilayer thinning and reducing local membrane thickness, thereby supporting their potential antimicrobial role.

Article.Title: Segmentation of brain tumors using a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model on MRI
Article.Authors: Kazemi M.; Farsi H.; Ghaffari A.; Mohamadzadeh S.; Barati A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAccurate segmentation of brain tumors in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is crucial for effective treatment planning and post-treatment monitoring. However, challenges such as intensity inhomogeneity, low-contrast boundaries, and highly irregular tumor morphology significantly complicate this task. In this work, we introduce a two-stage hybrid framework that integrates a convolutional U-Net for coarse tumor localization with a morphological Laplacian-enhanced active contour model for precise boundary refinement. While the U-Net is trained using bimodal input (FLAIR + T1ce) to generate reliable initial masks, all refinement steps and final performance evaluations are conducted exclusively on single-modality FLAIR images—ensuring clinical simplicity and robustness. The proposed active contour incorporates a novel local fitting term based on morphological Laplacian operators, which capture structural transitions and enhance edge sensitivity. An adaptive weighting function dynamically balances the influence of local and global intensity information during contour evolution, improving resilience to noise and intensity variations without compromising computational efficiency. When evaluated on the BraTS 2020 dataset, the proposed method achieves a Dice coefficient of 96.48% ± 1.57%, a Jaccard index of 93.43% ± 2.92%, and a sensitivity of 97.01% ± 1.69%. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms both classical active contour models and contemporary deep learning architectures in whole-tumor segmentation from FLAIR-only MRI. The source code will be made publicly available upon acceptance.

Article.Title: Hour-scale response of low-Earth-orbit satellite altitude to extreme geomagnetic storms revealed by the NinjaSat CubeSat during the 2024 solar maximum
Article.Authors: Tanaka H.; Nakagawa T.; Nozawa S.; Tamagawa T.; Enoto T.; Kitaguchi T.; Iwakiri W.; Mihara T.; Takeda T.; Ota N.; Aoyama A.; Iwata S.; Takahashi T.; Yamasaki K.
Article.Abstract: AbstractExtreme geomagnetic storms accelerate low-Earth-orbit satellite decay by inflating the thermosphere, yet the hour-scale pathway from solar-wind energy to atmospheric heating is poorly understood. Using the GNSS receiver of the NinjaSat CubeSat ($$\sim 500$$km,$$97^\circ $$sun-synchronous), we tracked orbital altitude through solar-maximum 2024 and cross-correlated the storm-time altitude-change rate with geomagnetic indices during the two largest storms of the year. The EUV-corrected residual correlates with the polar-cap (PC) index at$$r\gtrsim 0.8$$, PC leading or coincident with the response by up to$$\sim 3$$h, as do the auroral electrojet indices AE and AL. It also correlates with the Dst index ($$r\approx 0.82 - 0.84$$), but the altitude dropprecedesthe Dst minimum by$$\sim 3$$h, attributing this to a common solar-wind driver rather than ring-current heating. XRISM ($$31^\circ $$,$$\sim 560$$km) shows the storm-induced density enhancement reached low latitudes in May 2024 but not in October 2024, consistent with a shorter electrojet duration despite comparable peak intensity. Polar Joule heating, indexed by PC, is thus the dominant storm-time drag driver, providing a natural forecasting window of up to$$\sim 3$$h.

Article.Title: Adsorption of hazardous Acid Violet 17 on Vachellia nilotica biochar: experimental and statistical physics modelling
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Al Shayeb A.; Naidu R.; Fegade U.; Jethave G.; Alluqmani A.; Martuza M.; Shatnawi Z.; Haque M.; Arifuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractInadequate management of chemical industrial effluents necessitates the development of high-capacity, sustainable wastewater treatment technologies. This study investigates the adsorptive removal of hazardous Acid Violet 17 (AV17) dye using a novel biochar derived fromVachellia niloticastems (VNBB). Characterization via HRTEM and BET analysis revealed a mesoporous, sponge-like architecture with a surface area of 50.92 m2g− 1and an average pore diameter of 8.02 nm. Batch experiments demonstrated that VNBB is highly effective, achieving a maximum removal efficiency of 97.94% at pH 6. Equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir isotherm, yielding a superior maximum adsorption capacity (Qmax) of 333.33 mgg− 1. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second order model, (R² = 0.995), implying strong correlation with the experimental results. From thermodynamic and statistical physics study, it was found that the adsorption mechanism followed mainly physical interaction. To provide deeper mechanistic insights, advanced statistical physics modeling was applied. A double-layer model with five parameters successfully described the adsorption isotherms. The steric parameternranged from 0.39 to 0.42, indicating a multi-docking mechanism where AV17 molecules maintain a horizontal orientation on the VNBB surface. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed the process is endothermic and spontaneous, with adsorption energies (E1) between 22.16 and 24.48 kJmol− 1, signifying a physical component to the binding. Furthermore, the biochar exhibited excellent stability, maintaining high performance across five regeneration cycles with less than a 2% loss in capacity. These findings position VNBB as a high-performance, cost-effective, and reusable adsorbent for the remediation of dye-contaminated industrial wastewater.

Article.Title: Molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus in chigger mites
Article.Authors: Lee H.; Kim S.; Kim H.; Lim H.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSevere fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging tick-borne viral disease with high case-fatality rates in East Asia. While hard ticks are recognized as the primary vectors of SFTS virus (SFTSV), the detection of SFTSV RNA in chigger mites suggests their involvement in viral maintenance in natural conditions. In this study, wild rodents were captured at 17 sites across the Republic of Korea in 2019, and spleen tissues and mites were collected and tested for SFTSV RNA using RT-PCR. To evaluate transovarial transmission,Leptotrombidiumsp. collected from an endemic area were reared under laboratory conditions. Among 56 rodents and 3,402 mites, SFTSV RNA was detected in 3.6% of rodents and 2.3% of mite pools (minimum infection rate of 0.09%). Phylogenetic analysis revealed that all viral sequences clustered within genotype B. SFTSV RNA was detected in both parental mites and their F1 larvae, providing molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission. This study provides the first molecular evidence suggestive of transovarial transmission of SFTSV in chigger mites under laboratory conditions and indicates that chigger mites may contribute to the natural maintenance of the virus. Further animal model-based studies are needed to clarify their vector competence.

Article.Title: Development of a prediction model for occupational satisfaction among cancer patients following counseling in German psychosocial cancer counseling centers
Article.Authors: Lange H.; Kurth T.; Roth R.; Sibert N.; Breidenbach C.; Schellack S.; Ernstmann N.; Heidkamp P.; Hiltrop K.; Rother J.; Heier L.; Kowalski C.
Article.Abstract: AbstractA prognostic model was developed and internally validated to predict satisfaction with the occupational situation among cancer patients receiving psychosocial counseling regarding return to work (RTW). Data were collected from outpatient cancer counseling centers in Germany and included individuals who had sought counseling on work-related issues at different stages of their illness. Satisfaction with the occupational situation was measured using a single-item scale. LASSO regression with cross-validation and bootstrapping was applied for predictor selection. The final model (n= 259) identified satisfaction with life, baseline satisfaction with the occupational situation, and higher household and personal income as positive predictors, while workplace conflicts and psychological distress were negative predictors. The model showed moderate predictive accuracy (R2= 0.29, RMSE = 2.55) and good calibration-in-the-large (predicted: 5.45; observed: 5.45). The model may support the identification of cancer survivors likely to report low satisfaction with the occupational situation following psychosocial counseling. External validation is required to assess generalizability. A web-based tool was developed to support application in counseling settings.

Article.Title: A single-user feasibility study demonstrating real-time raycast-based stair and elevation-change detection on consumer smartphone LiDAR hardware
Article.Authors: Herdt N.; Braun T.; Bell T.; Russell S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractFor individuals who are blind or visually impaired (BVI), undetected stairways, curbs, and sudden elevation changes represent a leading cause of fall-related injury. Herein we present a preliminary, single-operator feasibility evaluation of a computationally efficient geometric algorithm for detecting stair and elevation changes in real time, implemented entirely on an LiDAR-equipped consumer smartphone (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.2). The algorithm uses a set of eight downward- and forward-facing raycasts projected into an ARKit (Artificial Reality developer Kit)-reconstructed mesh and performs line-segment angular analysis at 60 Hz within a 16.7 ms per-frame budget, without requiring cloud processing, GPU inference, or custom hardware. A single trained operator conducted 120 trials spanning eight real-world hazard locations, five step heights (4.5 to 7.5 in; 11.4 to 19.1 cm), four stair grades (22 to 33 degrees), varied lighting conditions (indoor artificial, outdoor daytime, and outdoor nighttime), and both ascending and descending approaches, yielding an overall detection rate of 92.5% (95% CI 86.4–96.0%) and a mean alert distance of 2.31 ft (0.70 m; SD = 0.91 ft). No false-positive alerts were observed during the hazard-approach or traversal segments of these trials, although dedicated hazard-free control trials were not conducted, so this should not be read as a validated false-positive rate across general non-hazard environments. Detection rate and alert distance both tended to increase with step height, with the smallest steps and one specific indoor location accounting for most missed detections; however, pairwise differences across step-height, lighting, and approach-direction categories did not reach statistical significance at the sample sizes tested (Fisher’s exactp> 0.05 in all cases), and step geometry covaried with test location in this design, so these patterns should be treated as preliminary and hypothesis-generating rather than as an established reliability threshold. Descending approaches produced numerically lower detection rates and shorter warning distances than ascending approaches, consistent with a geometric limitation intrinsic to depth-based sensing of hazards that only become visible at close range. These results indicate that low-latency elevation-hazard detection is technically feasible on commodity mobile hardware under controlled, single-operator conditions; confirming this feasibility finding for real-world use by BVI individuals will require larger, multi-participant studies incorporating natural scanning behavior and dedicated negative-condition testing.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning and hybrid transformer-based proteochemometric modelling for breast cancer molecular subtyping and multi-target natural product discovery
Article.Authors: Jakkula B.; Perugu S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractBreast cancer comprises five intrinsic molecular subtypes with distinct transcriptomic programs, prognoses, and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Yet, accurate subtype discrimination remains limited by boundary-overlap and poor cross-cohort generalisability, while single-target agents often fail against pathway redundancy and acquired resistance. We developed an integrated computational framework linking transcriptomic-classification, explainable target prioritisation, and multi-target natural-product discovery. Three transcriptomic cohorts (METABRIC-BRCA-2016, TCGA-BRCA-2012, and TCGA-BRCA-2018; n = 2512 after quality-control and ComBat-correction) were integrated. Differential-expression analysis and PCA-based feature selection yielded a 50-gene signature that retained more than 90% of the subtype-associated variance. Among the six evaluated classifiers, XGBoost achieved the best performance and generalised to an independent cohort of 3,409 samples (accuracy: 85.70%; ROC-AUC: 0.95–0.99). SHAP-analysis identified 30-candidate genes associated with Basal-like and HER2-enriched subtypes, which were cross-referenced against ChEMBL to retain 11 targets for proteochemometric (PCM) modelling. A hybrid PCM multilayer-perceptron integrating ProtBERT and ChemBERTa embeddings with molecular fingerprints and chemical descriptors achieved a balanced-accuracy of 0.9140 and mean ROC-AUC of 0.9696. Screening of 30,898 NPASS natural products identified 292 pan-active compounds. Independent binding- and safety-prioritisation strategies converged on three leads: NPC139056, NPC196231, and NPC471997. This reproducible pipeline provides computationally prioritised leads for experimental validation in clinically challenging breast cancer subtypes.

Article.Title: Proteomics characterization of muscle-invasive bladder carcinoma identifies molecular subtypes and subtype-specific biological processes
Article.Authors: Pedregosa-Barbas J.; Trilla-Fuertes L.; García-Fernández E.; Becerril-Gómez F.; Lalanda-Delgado P.; Zambrana F.; Martínez-Salas I.; Gajate P.; Dittmann A.; López-Vacas R.; Kunz L.; Rubio G.; Nieto-Torrero S.; Pertejo A.; Vara J.; González-Peramato P.; Gámez-Pozo A.; Pinto-Marín Á.

Article.Title: User-focused faceted aggregated exploratory multimedia search results framework
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Saadia A.; Rashid U.; Khan T.; Jan T.; Khalil R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSearch engines have become a ubiquitous platform for finding information, yet web users still struggle to browse and filter retrieved results in exploratory search environments with ill-defined information needs. While search engines retrieve relevant results for keyword queries, users struggle to browse, filter, and comprehend disorganized, media-diverse, disjointed verticals. Existing research on vertical aggregation has mainly focused on aggregating heterogeneous verticals, thereby undermining crucial aspects such as organization, annotation, and personalization to support exploratory search. This research proposes an aggregated, personalized exploratory search framework that organizes search results into Named Entity Recognition (NER)-derived, domain-independent facet categories and ranks them using a modified Best Matching 25 Fielded (BM25F) ranking algorithm. The facets are linked to the user query as implicit pseudo-relevance feedback to personalize search results based on the user’s category-specific intent. We empirically validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm on standardized benchmarks (SciFact, TREC-COVID, NFCorpus, FiQA, SCIDOCS, ArguAna). The results show that the proposed ranking algorithm provides, on average, 12.59% superior data exploration performance while preserving lexical relevance. The algorithm’s efficacy in real-world exploratory search was further validated through a user study (N=23) that evaluated users’ exploratory search outcomes using system usability and behavioral metrics. An independent user study with 23 participants further indicates higher perceived usability and task satisfaction compared with a Google baseline, with a 17.72-point improvement in system usability and a 25.3% relative improvement in satisfaction with exploratory task completion. Behavioral analysis additionally shows shorter queries and substantially fewer query reformulations, indicating reduced query-formulation effort during exploratory search. These findings show that aggregating, annotating, organizing, and personalizing search results can substantially improve exploratory search effectiveness, reduce cognitive load, and enhance user satisfaction.

Article.Title: Spatial variability of TEC perturbations and ROTI during the 3 october 2024 X9.0 solar flare: a multi-station GNSS analysis
Article.Authors: Data E.; Setegn G.; Okoh D.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study investigates the spatially heterogeneous low-latitude ionospheric response to the 3 October 2024 X9.0 solar flare using GNSS observations from seven equatorial and low-latitude stations. TEC, quiet-time differential TEC ($$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$), and ROTI were analyzed under relatively quiet geomagnetic conditions ($$K_p=1$$–3). The flare peaked at 12:18 UT, and comparison with quiet-time conditions revealed$$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$perturbations of approximately 6–14% at several stations, with pronounced spatial differences. YKRO showed the largest positive perturbation at the flare peak, reaching 12.75 TECU (14.21%), whereas MBAR and CUSV exhibited negative perturbations of$$-10.98$$TECU ($$-10.77\%$$) and$$-6.14$$TECU ($$-9.29\%$$), respectively. However, substantial and sometimes larger$$\Delta \textrm{TEC}$$variations occurred outside the flare interval, indicating that their magnitude alone cannot establish a flare-driven response. ROTI remained generally below 0.04 TECU min$$^{-1}$$during the flare, with stronger irregularity activity occurring predominantly after sunset. The results indicate a measurable and spatially heterogeneous ionospheric response temporally associated with the X9.0 flare, while highlighting the substantial contribution of intrinsic low-latitude variability. These findings emphasize the importance of multi-station observations and quiet-time normalization for robustly assessing solar-flare-associated ionospheric disturbances.

Article.Title: Unravelling the roles of redox homeostasis and antioxidant system in facilitating adaptive responses during Pb induced hormesis in Brassica juncea
Article.Authors: Dhiman S.; Naresh R.; Bhardwaj R.; Singh R.; Kapoor N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis research explores the role of the antioxidant-prooxidant balance in eliciting the hormesis effect inBrassica junceaseedlings exposed to mild Lead (Pb). Excessive Pb doses in plants causes oxidative stress, which damages plant cells, stunts growth, and reduces agricultural yield. Conversely, mild Pb doses induce a hormetic effect inside plants system, leading to beneficial adaptive changes at cellular, molecular, and physio-biochemical levels. The plant's antioxidant defence network often relieves Pb metal stress. Antioxidants, both enzyme-based and non-enzyme-based, neutralize reactive oxygen species (ROS) created by Pb stress, protecting cellular structures and promoting plant resilience. Also, the idea of hormesis, which describes how modest doses of toxins like Pb metals cause plants to adapt, helps us understand how plants protect themselves and enhance stress tolerance to handle stress by raising antioxidant activity. In the present study, mild Pb exposed 10 days oldB. junceaseedlings were tested for antioxidant activity and gene expression. Moderate Pb exposure increasedB. junceaseedling protein content, antioxidant enzyme activity, and gene expression. The results suggest the possible role of antioxidants in inducing hormetic responses inB. junceaseedlings exposed to Pb, laying the foundation for understanding how these mechanisms cooperate to minimize Pb impact and improve seedling resilience.

Article.Title: A physics guided hybrid modeling framework for rainfall runoff forecasting in data scarce regions
Article.Authors: Molajou A.; Tajbakhsh A.; Shokatian-Beiragh M.; Variani H.; Aram S.; Brysiewicz A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRainfall-runoff (R-R) forecasting in data-scarce regions remains challenging due to limited hydrometeorological observations, uncertainties in satellite-based precipitation products (SPPs), and the inability of individual modeling approaches to fully represent complex watershed dynamics. To address these challenges, this study develops a physics guided hybrid modeling framework that integrates bias-corrected satellite precipitation products, signal decomposition techniques, process-based hydrological modeling, and deep learning (DL) for improved runoff simulation and forecasting. In the proposed framework, physical knowledge is incorporated through the soil and water assessment tool (SWAT), which provides physically meaningful representations of watershed processes, while a long short-term memory (LSTM) network learns residual nonlinear relationships between physically simulated and observed runoff responses. Three widely used SPPs, including CHIRPS, IMERG, and PERSIANN-CDR, were evaluated against available rainfall observations, and a PDF-based additive bias correction approach was applied to improve precipitation estimates. Wavelet transform (WT) and variational mode decomposition (VMD) were further investigated within a time consistent feature construction framework to extract hydrologically relevant temporal patterns from corrected precipitation inputs and SWAT-simulated runoff outputs. The framework was evaluated in two hydroclimatically contrasting watersheds in Iran, namely the semi-arid Tabriz Basin and the humid Ghaem Shahr Basin. Results indicated that CHIRPS provided the most reliable precipitation estimates among the tested SPPs, while VMD outperformed WT in extracting temporal characteristics relevant to runoff generation. The proposed VMD-SWAT-LSTM framework generally achieved superior or comparable performance compared with standalone SWAT, LSTM, and conventional SWAT-LSTM models during training, validation, and testing periods under a temporally consistent evaluation framework. During the training phase, the proposed framework achieved CC = 0.99, NSE = 0.96, and RMSE = 2.61m3.s− 1in Tabriz Basin, and CC = 0.98, NSE = 0.97, and RMSE = 0.58m3.s− 1in the Ghaem Shahr Basin. The proposed approach also demonstrated improved robustness in multi-step-ahead forecasting (up to 7 days), although predictive performance decreased with increasing lead time, and maintained robust performance under uncertainty according to Monte Carlo (MC) analysis. The findings demonstrate that combining physically based watershed representation with decomposition assisted data-driven (DD) error learning within a physics-guided framework can improve R-R forecasting accuracy and robustness in data-scarce regions. The proposed methodology showed robust performance in the two investigated hydroclimatically contrasting basins, suggesting its potential for hydrological prediction in data-scarce regions. However, its transferability to other basins and broader hydrological and climatic conditions requires further evaluation.

Article.Title: An international multilocation trial reveals genotype-by-environment interactions in Arabica coffee across climate gradients
Article.Authors: Gautron R.; Berny Mier y Teran J.; Delgado Muñoz L.; Lemus S.; Rahn E.; Castro Llanos F.; Bunn C.; Gezan S.; Pruvot-Woehl S.; Maina C.; Cheserek J.; Alonso Castillo J.; López Morgado R.; Alpízar E.; Alvarado J.; Arevalo J.; Banda B.; Baudry D.; Bordeaux M.; Castro E.; Devasia J.; Gichuru E.; Gimase J.; Alunga C.; Kachiguma N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractClimate change makes the future of Arabica coffee (Coffea arabicaL.) uncertain, a crop supporting Coffee is produced on approximately 12.5 million farms worldwide, predominantly family-run smallholdings. Identifying varieties that combine high productivity with disease resistance across diverse environments is critical for climate adaptation, yet global empirical evidence remains limited. We leveraged a dataset from an international multi-environment trial evaluating 32 varieties for yield and coffee leaf rust severity across a total of 30 sites in 17 countries. Genotype-by-environment interactions were analyzed using factor analytic mixed-effects models, and latent environmental factors were linked to climatic gradients through partial least squares regression. Yield stability was associated with thermal gradients, distinguishing varietal adaptation between cooler environments with high diurnal temperature variation and warmer, thermally stable conditions. In contrast, rust severity and its interactions were associated with joint gradients of temperature, precipitation, humidity, and thermal variability. Among the evaluated genotypes, the F1 hybrids H1 Centroamericano and EC16, followed by the introgressed line Parainema, showed the strongest combined performance for yield and rust resistance, although with distinct climatic preferences and trade-offs in yield stability. Overall, introgressed varieties consistently outperformed pure Arabica varieties, which exhibited lower yields and greater rust susceptibility. These findings provide a robust empirical basis for climate-informed variety deployment and breeding strategies in Arabica coffee.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of mental health literacy and associated factors among older adults with cataracts
Article.Authors: Tang X.; Li X.; Li J.; Long L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMental health literacy may shape how older adults with cataracts recognize psychological distress and seek support, but variation within this population remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study surveyed 209 hospitalized adults aged 60 years or older with cataracts using validated measures of mental health literacy, anxiety, perceived social support and sleep quality. Latent profile analysis identified three mental health literacy profiles: low-MHL/negative-attitude (16.7%), limited-recognition/moderate-attitude (33.5%) and high-MHL (49.8%). Multinomial logistic regression showed that diagnosis duration, anxiety level, living arrangement and primary caregiver were associated with profile membership. These findings highlight different patterns of recognition and attitudes within this hospitalized sample. They support examining these dimensions separately in nursing assessment research. Independent validation is required before using the profiles to guide nursing assessment or select educational support.

Article.Title: Coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and leached plastic-derived additives during magnetite-assisted water treatment
Article.Authors: Kida M.; Dytłow S.; Pochwat K.; Strojny W.; Ziembowicz S.; Gruca-Rokosz R.; Koszelnik P.; Radoń M.; Bester K.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe coupled interactions between particulate microplastics and dissolved plastic-derived additives were investigated using magnetite (Fe₃O₄). The investigated materials included tire wear particles (TWP), poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) pipe particles, and reference polymers. Magnetite rapidly induced heteroaggregation and enabled efficient magnetic separation of the investigated MPs. Simultaneously, dissolved plastic-associated organic compounds were scavenged from model solutions, with removal depending on their physicochemical properties. SEM, FTIR, and magnetic analyses confirmed attachment of Fe₃O₄ particles to microplastic surfaces, the formation of Fe₃O₄–MP aggregates, and the absence of detectable chemical modification of the investigated polymers. Magnetic measurements further demonstrated that the magnetic response of the heteroaggregates depended on polymer type, pH, and aggregate organization. Statistical analysis and exploratory Random Forest modelling were used to examine relationships among the investigated variables and to identify their relative contributions within the experimental dataset. Phthalate release from TWP continued after rapid magnetite-induced aggregation and separation of the microplastic particles, indicating that removal of the particulate fraction did not immediately terminate additive release from the polymer matrix. The simultaneous presence of MPs and magnetite therefore involved coupled processes associated with particulate aggregation, additive release, and scavenging of dissolved compounds. These findings demonstrate that physical removal of microplastic particles alone does not necessarily eliminate the dissolved fraction of plastic-derived contamination. The study provides an experimental assessment of these coupled processes under controlled conditions and highlights the importance of considering both particulate and dissolved plastic-related contaminants when evaluating magnetite-assisted treatment strategies.

Article.Title: Deep reinforcement learning-based adaptive FOPID tuning for power system stability enhancement: A twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient approach
Article.Authors: Kumar S.; Singh M.; Singh M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3)-based adaptive fractional-order proportional-integral-derivative (FOPID) controller for joint load-frequency and voltage regulation in a renewable-rich power system. The proposed controller adaptively tunes five FOPID parameters, namely$${K_p}$$,$${K_i}$$,$${K_d}$$,λ, and µ, through a multi-objective reward formulation that simultaneously minimizes frequency integral time-weighted absolute error (ITAE), terminal-voltage ITAE, maximum frequency deviation, and tie-line power error. A curriculum-based training strategy is employed to progressively expose the TD3 agent to increasing disturbance severity. The proposed framework is evaluated on a modified IEEE 14-bus system incorporating 46% renewable penetration, comprising DFIG-based wind generation and photovoltaic generation under low-inertia operating conditions. Under the standard 0.10 p.u. step-load disturbance, the proposed TD3-FOPID controller achieves an ITAE of 0.0612, a settling time of 1.48 s, and an overshoot of 1.82%. Across four nominal disturbance scenarios, the obtained damping ratios range from 0.74 to 0.78, while the broader tested operating-envelope analysis gives a minimum damping ratio of 0.72. The maximum system-level ROCOF observed at disturbance inception across the evaluated scenarios is 0.82 Hz/s, below the 2 Hz/s reference threshold adopted in this study. Statistical evaluation over ten independent training/evaluation runs with different random seeds further demonstrates consistent performance of the proposed approach. Numerical Lyapunov verification using the linearized closed-loop model provides numerical evidence of stable closed-loop behaviour within the tested operating envelope. The results demonstrate the potential of TD3-based five-parameter FOPID adaptation for robust frequency and voltage regulation in renewable-rich power systems.

Article.Title: Initiation mechanism of irrigation-induced retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Tableland, China
Article.Authors: Ma P.; Chen L.; Xue Y.; Wang J.; Mu Q.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRepeated sliding disturbs the slope structure and degrades soil mechanical properties, promoting the progressive development of retrogressive loess landslides on the South Jingyang Plateau, China. These landslides progressively encroach upon the plateau surface and have caused substantial casualties and property losses. Field investigations revealed that two subsequent retrogressive failures caused the landslide crown to retreat by approximately 8 and 7 m, respectively, suggesting that the near-crown zone formed after the initial failure underwent sustained disturbance and structural readjustment. Accordingly, undisturbed loess samples were collected from a sliding-disturbed zone approximately 5 m from the current crown (No.1) and a relatively undisturbed zone approximately 50 m from the crown (No.2). Consolidated undrained triaxial tests, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) infiltration tests, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analyses were conducted to systematically compare the strength, water-migration characteristics, and microstructural damage of the soils from the two zones, thereby elucidating the triggering mechanism of retrogressive landslides. The results indicate that: (1) The soil in the sliding-disturbed zone exhibited pronounced mechanical weakening. Under natural conditions, the average shear strength of No. 1 was approximately 20% lower than that of No. 2; under saturated conditions, its shear strength was only 71.9–90.0% of that in the relatively undisturbed zone. The disturbed soil was characterized by a higher proportion of large pores, weaker interparticle bonding, and more irregular pore geometries, making its mechanical behavior more sensitive to variations in water content. (2) The sliding-disturbed zone exhibited more pronounced water migration. The average signal intensity of the second peak in the NMR T₂ spectrum was approximately 1.97 times that of the relatively undisturbed zone, indicating a stronger water-filling response within the larger-pore domain. During water infiltration, pore-structure readjustment and changes in pore morphology occurred in the disturbed zone, further promoting structural weakening of the soil. (3) The subsequent evolution of retrogressive landslides can be summarized as follows: the initial failure disturbs the slope and alters its stress state and pore structure; sustained water infiltration subsequently promotes further structural readjustment and degradation of the soil’s mechanical properties, thereby reducing slope stability and increasing the likelihood of renewed failure. This process ultimately produces a cascading “sliding–disturbance–re-sliding” evolution pattern.

Article.Title: Metagenomic insights into viral community restructuring and microbial interactions in waste stabilization ponds
Article.Authors: Rizk N.; Marouf M.; Ahmed N.; El-Gayar M.; Kamel M.; El-Khateeb M.; Sedhom R.; Elfeky E.; El-Liethy M.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractWaste stabilization ponds (WSPs) operate as sequential ecological compartments in which physicochemical gradients, microbial succession, and trophic interactions increase toward the final polishing stage. Among these units, the maturation pond represents the terminal control point for pathogen attenuation and effluent quality; however, its role in shaping viral community structure remains insufficiently resolved. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics to characterize DNA viral communities across the full treatment train of a full-scale WSP system in Giza, Egypt, with particular emphasis on maturation-stage restructuring. Viral community composition was strongly structured by treatment stage (PERMANOVA R² = 0.53,p< 0.05), with the most pronounced compositional turnover occurring between upstream ponds and the maturation pond. Relative abundance changes were highly taxon dependent. Human-associated viral families, includingAdenoviridaeandPoxviridae, were detected in the inlet but fell below detection in the maturation pond, whereas other groups such asMicroviridaeshowed partial persistence. In contrast, several bacteriophage-associated signals increased in relative abundance in the maturation pond, suggesting stage-associated restructuring of viral DNA profiles that may be linked to host community shifts, environmental filtering, or particle-associated DNA dynamics. Notably, the maturation pond virome displayed differentiation from upstream stages, including the emergence of eukaryote-associated viral signals, consistent with potential co-variation with locally established microeukaryotic communities. Cross-domain network analysis further revealed that the maturation pond was characterized by tightly connected virus–bacteria–microeukaryote modules dominated by positive associations, indicative of coordinated responses to shared environmental filtering. Together, these findings position the maturation pond as a distinct ecological compartment associated with downstream virome restructuring under combined environmental filtering, treatment-stage conditions, and host-community-associated processes.

Article.Title: Effect of Bacillus sp. N188 application on turf quality and functional value
Article.Authors: Radkowski A.; Szpytma M.; Radkowska I.; Bujak H.; Dobrzyński J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMaintaining high-quality functional and recreational turfgrass requires effective management practices that support turf performance under field conditions. One promising strategy involves the use of plant growth-promoting microorganisms. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect ofBacillussp. N188 on turf quality and functional performance. A field experiment was conducted in 2024–2025 under the conditions of southern Poland on Haplic Phaeozem soil. The study included two lawn mixtures differing in species composition and intended use: “Uniwersalna U-1” and “Super Trawnik”. The experimental design comprised control treatments and variants with annual application of a preparation containingBacillussp. N188. Turf quality was assessed according to the COBORU methodology, including visual traits (overall appearance, turf density, leaf colour and structure, and disease susceptibility), as well as physiological indices (NDVI, LAI, SPAD) and selected indicators of functional value. The application ofBacillussp. N188 significantly improved turf quality compared to the control treatments. An increase in sward density and uniformity, more intense leaf coloration, improved structural characteristics, and reduced incidence of fungal diseases were observed. The physiological indices confirmed improved plant condition in plots treated with the bacterial preparation. The positive effects ofBacillussp. N188 were observed in both lawn mixtures, although the magnitude of the response varied depending on species composition. The results indicate thatBacillussp. N188 has potential as a plant biostimulant for improving the aesthetic and functional properties of turfgrass under temperate climatic conditions.

Article.Title: Antioxidant treatments combined with refrigerated storage, modified atmosphere packaging, and precooling improve postharvest quality of red cabbage
Article.Authors: Abo Elmakarem A.; Mostafa N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPostharvest deterioration of red cabbage involves water loss, oxidative imbalance, membrane damage, and loss of structural and sensory quality. This study evaluated the effects of four food-grade antioxidants—ascorbic acid, citric acid, glutathione, and α-tocopherol—together with an untreated control under three refrigerated storage strategies: conventional refrigeration, modified atmosphere packaging (MAP), and pre-cooling followed by MAP. A 5 × 3 factorial experiment was conducted to assess treatment effects and interactions on physiological, biochemical, oxidative, structural, and quality-related attributes after 12 weeks of storage. Antioxidant treatment, storage condition, and their interaction significantly affected several measured attributes, indicating that treatment responses varied with the storage environment. The combination of citric acid and pre-cooling followed by MAP resulted in the lowest weight loss (8.96%), representing a 69.6% reduction compared with the untreated control under the same storage condition (29.46%). Under this combination, SOD activity reached 49.08 units mg⁻¹ protein compared with 25.69 units mg⁻¹ protein in the corresponding control. Antioxidant treatments also influenced phytochemical retention, membrane stability, firmness, texture, and oxidative-stress-related responses, although the magnitude and direction of effects varied among antioxidant–storage combinations. Multivariate analyses supported associations among oxidative status, antioxidant defense, structural attributes, and postharvest quality. The results indicate that antioxidant application can complement refrigerated MAP-based storage, with citric acid combined with pre-cooling and MAP providing the lowest weight loss among the tested combinations. These findings support the potential of integrating food-grade antioxidant treatments with established refrigerated handling practices, while further studies are needed to evaluate their performance under commercial-scale conditions.

Article.Title: Prevalence of ocular allergy among children in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Ismail M.; Khalafalla I.; Dirie A.; Alemayehu C.; Zalwango C.; Isse S.; Farah F.; Sheck Z.; Mire A.; Herow A.; Ahmed A.; Abdi F.; Mohamed I.; Jayte M.; Mumin B.; Hakizimana T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractOcular allergy ranges from seasonal and perennial allergic conjunctivitis to chronic, potentially sight-threatening vernal keratoconjunctivitis (VKC). African prevalence studies use heterogeneous terminology and case-ascertainment methods, and their estimates have not previously been synthesized. To synthesise published prevalence estimates of ocular allergy among African children, quantify uncertainty around summary estimates, and describe between-study variation. PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, African Journals Online and African Index Medicus were searched for observational studies published from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2025. Disease-specific terms were supplemented with broader ocular-morbidity terminology, reference-list screening and citation verification to identify studies reporting ocular allergy as a secondary outcome. Eligible studies enrolled African children and provided an extractable numerator and denominator. Logit-transformed proportions were pooled using a random-effects restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) model in Stata 17. Heterogeneity, 95% prediction intervals, diagnostic and setting subgroups, and sensitivity analyses were reported. Fourteen studies from five countries included 18,681 children, of whom 1,911 had ocular allergy, allergic conjunctivitis or VKC/vernal disease. The pooled prevalence was 9.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] 5.4%–15.6%), with extreme heterogeneity (τ2 = 1.23; I2 = 99.19%; Q(13) = 1844.38, p < 0.001) and a 95% prediction interval of 0.8%–55.9%. The pooled estimate was 14.5% (95% CI 5.5%–33.0%; k = 6) for allergic conjunctivitis and 6.6% (95% CI 3.8%–11.2%; k = 8) for VKC/vernal disease; the subgroup difference was not statistically significant (Qβ(1) = 1.99, p = 0.158). School/community studies yielded 8.9% (95% CI 5.0%–15.4%; k = 13), whereas the single clinic study reported 17.6% (95% CI 15.8%–19.6%). Substituting a narrower VKC case definition gave 8.4% (95% CI 4.9%–14.2%), and leave-one-out estimates ranged from 8.0% to 10.2%. Published studies consistently report ocular allergy among African children, although the available evidence is too heterogeneous to support a reliable continental prevalence estimate. Variation in case definition and ascertainment is a plausible and likely substantial contributor, but could not be quantified formally. The findings support consideration of ocular allergy within school eye-health and primary eye-care programmes while underscoring the need for standardised diagnostic and reporting methods.

Article.Title: Effect of extraction temperature on the fatty acid composition, metabolic profile, and bioactivity-related properties of Lepidium sativum seed oil
Article.Authors: Abdo M.; Elnaggar M.; Elissawy A.; Gad H.; El-Ahmady S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLepidium sativumL. (garden cress) seeds are a valuable source of oil rich in unsaturated fatty acids. This study examined the effect of extraction temperature on the yield, fatty acid composition, metabolic profile, and functional properties ofL. sativumseed oil. Fixed oils were obtained by maceration in n-hexane at room temperature (cold-extracted seed oil, CSO) and by Soxhlet extraction in n-hexane at 70 °C (hot-extracted seed oil, HSO). Chemical characterization by GC–MS revealed marked differences between the two oils. α-Linolenic acid was the major fatty acid in CSO (36.04%), whereas oleic acid predominated in HSO (24.73%). The influence of these compositional changes on functional properties was assessed using DPPH radical-scavenging and α-amylase inhibition assays. CSO showed higher antioxidant activity (IC50= 138.47 ± 2.87 µg mL−1) and stronger α-amylase inhibitory activity (IC50= 123.46 ± 2.48 µg mL−1) than HSO. The results demonstrate that extraction temperature significantly affects the lipid composition of L. sativum seed oil and is associated with changes in its functional properties.

Article.Title: Knowledge attitudes and practices regarding toothbrush hygiene and disinfection among dental students in a multicenter cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Demircan B.; Çamgöz A.; Çalışkan A.; Selen M.; Aydogdu H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study aimed to evaluate dental students’ knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding toothbrush contamination and disinfection, and to assess differences according to clinical training level and gender. A total of 1206 dental students (years 1–5) from three dental faculties in Turkey were included. Data were collected through an online questionnaire covering demographic characteristics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices. Chi-square test, independent samples t-test, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) were used for statistical analysis. Of the participants, 767 were preclinical and 439 were clinical students. Mean knowledge, practice, attitude, and total scores were 3.87 ± 0.76, 3.45 ± 1.32, 2.83 ± 0.61, and 10.14 ± 1.86, respectively. Disinfection knowledge was higher in the clinical group (p= 0.010), whereas disinfection practice was lower (p= 0.001). The practice rate was significantly higher among students with disinfection knowledge (70.8% vs. 46.2%;p< 0.001) and among those who considered disinfection necessary (57.1% vs. 14.7%;p< 0.001). The most common source of information was social media, and the most frequently reported disinfection method was tap water. Knowledge and positive attitudes do not consistently translate into evidence-based practice among dental students. Although clinical training improves knowledge, it does not independently enhance disinfection behavior. Toothbrush hygiene should therefore be addressed through practice-oriented learning outcomes from the preclinical years.

Article.Title: A comprehensive study on multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis of machine learning models in diabetes detection
Article.Authors: Mumenin N.; Pranto M.; Yousuf M.; Monowar M.; Hamid M.; Alotaibi F.; Alassafi M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractHigh discrimination performance is often interpreted as evidence of model reliability in clinical machine learning (ML). However, strong predictive accuracy does not guarantee safe decision behavior. In safety-critical domains such as healthcare, miscalibrated probabilities, ineffective uncertainty estimation, and overconfident errors can lead to harmful decisions despite high area-under-curve metrics. This study presents a comprehensive multi-dimensional predictive safety analysis demonstrating that models with comparable discrimination performance can exhibit substantially different reliability and risk characteristics. We conduct a rigorous benchmarking evaluation across two heterogeneous diabetes risk datasets, a large population-scale BRFSS cohort and a small-sample early-stage clinical dataset. A diverse set of classical, ensemble, and deep tabular models are evaluated under a strict leakage-free cross-validation protocol with dedicated calibration splits. Beyond conventional discrimination metrics (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC), we assess probabilistic calibration (ECE, Brier score, NLL), epistemic uncertainty using a unified bootstrap-based framework, uncertainty–error correlation, selective prediction safety, high-confidence error rates, subgroup fairness across age and sex, and conformal prediction with finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees under the standard exchangeability assumption. Our results reveal a consistent accuracy–safety gap that models achieving near-identical PR-AUC display markedly different calibration quality, uncertainty effectiveness, subgroup reliability, and overconfidence behavior. On the early-stage clinical dataset, near-ceiling discrimination performance is observed across models, but due to the limited sample size, these results should be interpreted cautiously, as variability across folds may affect the stability of comparative performance across models. The findings demonstrate that discrimination metrics alone are insufficient to characterize reliable clinical decision-making. A comprehensive evaluation incorporating calibration, uncertainty quality, subgroup fairness, and formal coverage guarantees is essential for the trustworthy pre-deployment assessment of machine learning in healthcare. Rather than introducing a new predictive algorithm, this work contributes a unified empirical audit of safety-relevant model behavior, addressing reliability dimensions that are commonly evaluated separately or omitted in conventional diabetes prediction benchmarks.

Article.Title: Coordinated integration of renewables, STATCOMs, and V2G for hosting capacity improvement under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Ali Z.; Aleem S.; Aldawsari F.; Zenhom Z.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAlthough incorporating renewable energy sources (RESs) into electric distribution networks (EDNs) offers significant sustainability and environmental benefits, improper management of RESs may threaten the technical performance of the network. To assess the safe integration of distributed generation (DG), the hosting capacity (HC) concept is employed. Plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), through coordinated charging and discharging, can further support RES integration. Moreover, reactive power compensation using devices such as static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) remains a key strategy for mitigating voltage violations under high RES penetration. This article proposes a novel stochastic multi-objective optimization framework, from the distribution system operator’s (DSO) perspective, to optimally coordinate the dispatch of PEV aggregators, wind-based DGs, PV-based DGs, and STATCOMs. The model accounts for uncertainties in load demand, solar radiation, wind speed, and PEV demand using stochastic programming. The objectives are to maximize HC while minimizing voltage deviation and power losses. The feasibility of employing a recent optimization technique, Tianji’s Horse Racing Optimization (THRO), to solve the proposed multi-objective problem is demonstrated and benchmarked against three other optimization algorithms on both the IEEE 33-bus system and a real 59-bus network in Cairo, Egypt. Results of IEEE 33-bus EDN show that optimal coordination of V2G-enabled PEVs and reactive power support via STATCOMs can enhance HC by 37%, reduce voltage deviation by 74%, and decrease power losses by 15%. In addition, the Cairo 59-bus EDN system exhibited similar trends, achieving an approximately 83% increase in hosting capacity, accompanied by nearly a 39% reduction in voltage deviation.

Article.Title: A train-once, evaluate-twice protocol for cross-lingual depression detection with large language models
Article.Authors: Abdalla A.; Parvez M.; Alam T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractDepression affects more than 280 million people worldwide, and social media text provides a large-scale resource for automated mental health assessment. Large language model (LLM)-based approaches have shown promising performance for social media-based depression detection; however, their cross-lingual robustness for underrepresented languages such as Arabic remains insufficiently explored. We proposed the “train once, evaluate twice” protocol to evaluate the cross-lingual robustness of eight LLMs for detecting depression in both English and Arabic. For six open-source LLMs, we used QLoRA-based parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) to adapt them; for two closed-source GPT models, we fine-tuned them with the OpenAI supervised fine-tuning (SFT) API. To provide context for understanding transfer performance, we also evaluated a translation-based pipeline (MarianMT + XLM-R) and a bilingual fine-tuning ablation using data-mixing techniques. The models performed nearly at ceiling in their monolingual evaluation (English), with the best Macro-F1 score of 0.990 in GPT-4.1 Mini, and moderately well in Arabic (best Macro-F1 of 0.800 in Qwen2). Cross-lingual evaluation revealed significant directional asymmetry. The strongest transfer performance was observed in AR → EN (Macro-F1 = 0.793 for GPT-4.1 mini), whereas EN → AR remained considerably more challenging (best Macro-F1 = 0.638 for GPT-3.5 Turbo). The MarianMT + XLM-R translate-then-classify baseline achieved consistently lower cross-lingual performance than the fine-tuned generative LLMs evaluated in this study. The results of a bilingual fine-tuning ablation experiment conducted using Qwen2-7B-Instruct suggested that bilingual data mixing is sufficient to preserve English performance at near-ceiling levels. However, bilingual data mixing did not improve Arabic performance relative to monolingual Arabic fine-tuning. Thus, for this family of models, simple bilingual exposure appears insufficient to address the cross-lingual performance gap. Error analysis showed that EN→AR transfer predominantly increased false negatives, whereas AR → EN transfer exhibited more balanced precision–recall degradation profiles. Notably, the two Arabic-specialized models evaluated did not consistently outperform the strongest general-purpose multilingual models under cross-lingual transfer settings. PEFT produced compact adapters with low local inference latency, whereas API-based GPT inference exhibited substantially higher end-to-end latency. These findings support the notion that standard single-language fine-tuning does not afford much robustness when models are deployed across languages, especially in the EN → AR direction; thus, providing impetus for further research into new methods for adapting LLMs across multiple languages. Trial registration: Not applicable.

Article.Title: Assessment of the appropriateness of the selection for radiotherapy intensity from a quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30) perspective in older patients with cancer
Article.Authors: Murofushi K.; Kuribayashi S.; Ohnishi K.; Hayakawa S.; Tsuchida K.; Inoue Y.; Ohkawa A.; Ishida T.; Machitori Y.; Murakami M.; Takizawa D.; Saito M.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Testosterone exposure shifts female baseline phenotypes toward a male-associated tear-nerve-epithelial state in mice
Article.Authors: Feret N.; Megido A.; Pernot S.; Girard M.; Decoudu M.; Kindermans J.; Fichter L.; Llorens S.; Attina A.; Vialaret J.; David A.; Daien V.; Loulier K.; Hirtz C.; Michon F.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSex and hormonal status are clinically relevant determinants of ocular-surface physiology, but whether adult androgen exposure shifts multiple components of the ocular surface in parallel remains poorly defined. We compared vehicle-treated female mice with testosterone-treated females and used intact males as a physiological reference rather than as a procedure-matched control. Modified-nucleoside profiling, tear proteomics, corneal and trigeminal ganglion RNA sequencing, corneal flat-mount nerve volumetry, von Frey aesthesiometry, phospho-histone H3 labelling and single-endpoint Krt14-CreERT; CAG-Cytbow lineage tracing were combined to examine the tear-nerve-epithelial system at baseline. Tear collection rate was unchanged, whereas total tear protein concentration and proteomic composition differed between vehicle-treated and testosterone-treated females and shifted toward the intact male reference; 1,052 of 3,125 identified tear proteins were modulated in at least one pairwise comparison. Testosterone-treated females also showed lower central βIII-tubulin-positive nerve-fibre volume and mechanical sensitivity and fewer mitotic epithelial cells than vehicle-treated females, while lineage-labelled epithelial foci showed a qualitatively concordant distribution. Corneal transcriptional responses were substantially broader than those in the trigeminal ganglion. These findings show that adult testosterone exposure is associated with coordinated plasticity across several baseline ocular-surface phenotypes. They establish endocrine status as an important biological variable for experimental design while leaving its consequences for injury and disease to future functional studies.
