Article.Title: Differences in competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH4 and CO2 in mylonitic and primary structure coal
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Chen X.; Li J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTectonically deformed coal exhibits significantly different gas adsorption-desorption characteristics from primary structure coal due to intense coal mass deformation, making it a research hotspot in coalbed methane development and gas disaster prevention and control. To explore the differences in the competitive adsorption mechanisms of CH4and CO2between mylonitic coal and primary structure coal, this study took No. 8 coal from the Zhuxianzhuang Mining Area as the research object. Based on experimental results, molecular models of mylonitic coal (C214H159N3O20) and primary structure coal (C208H152N2O18)were constructed respectively. Isothermal adsorption simulations of single-component and mixed gases of CH4andCO2at different ratios were carried out using molecular dynamics methods. The results show that the adsorption of CH4and CO2in both types of coal belongs to physical adsorption, with stronger adsorption capacity under low temperature and high pressure. Under the same conditions, the adsorption capacity and adsorption heat of CO2are higher than those of CH4, and the adsorption advantage of CO2in mylonitic coal is more prominent. This is closely related to the more complete aromatic ring conjugated π-electron system, abundant oxygen-containing functional groups and a higher proportion of ultramicropores in mylonitic coal. With strong polarity and small kinetic diameter, CO2molecules are more prone to interact with π-electrons and produce the “pore-filling effect”. In mixed gas adsorption, the total adsorption capacity and interaction energy of both coal types increase with the rise of CO2molar fraction. Although the adsorption selectivity coefficient of CO2to CH4decreases, it is always greater than 1, and the selectivity coefficient of mylonitic coal is higher. The energy distribution curve of CO2shifts to adsorption sites with low interaction energy, while that of CH4shows the opposite trend, and the shift amplitude of gas molecular curves in mylonitic coal is larger. In addition, the interaction energy of mylonitic coal is dominated by van der Waals force, accounting for a higher proportion than that of primary structure coal. Its CH4adsorption heat also has a larger fluctuation range, reflecting a stronger competitive adsorption capacity for CO2. The research findings provide a theoretical basis for mine gas prevention and control and efficient coalbed methane development.

Article.Title: Differentiating acute from chronic pulmonary thromboembolism: a preliminary study using dual-layer CT
Article.Authors: Bae K.; Cho M.; Jeon K.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe aim of this study was to evaluate the actual values and ranges of conventional and spectral parameters in pulmonary thromboembolism (PE) and assess their potential for distinguishing acute PE (APE) from chronic PE (CPE) using dual-layer CT (DLCT). This retrospective study included 52 patients with central PE diagnosed with CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) using DLCT. Patients were categorized into APE and CPE groups. Conventional and spectral parameters including Hounsfield unit (HU) and electron density (ED) values were measured at the thrombus and pulmonary trunk on both pre- and post-contrast images. Additionally, in vitro experiments were conducted to generate clots of varying compositions. Apart from D-dimer levels, no significant clinical differences were found between APE and CPE groups. APE showed significantly higher mean HU and ED values than CPE on both unenhanced and enhanced images (bothp< 0.001). Thrombus enhancement, using true non-contrast (TNC) values as a reference, was similar between groups. APE showed greater variability in HU and ED values, whereas CPE consistently demonstrated lower values across all imaging phases. Unenhanced HU and ED values provided better discrimination than post-contrast values, with high AUCs (p< 0.05). The in vitro findings were consistent with these observations and may provide a plausible explanation for the compositional differences between APE and CPE. APE showed higher HU and ED values than CPE. Conventional and spectral CT parameters could help differentiate APE from CPE, reflecting distinct thrombus compositions.

Article.Title: Cognitive and affective drivers of VR adoption in heritage tourism: Integrating UTAUT and Anticipated emotions
Article.Authors: Lorandi M.; Mandolfo M.; Di Dalmazi M.; Noci G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractWhile the potential of Virtual Reality (VR) in destination marketing is recognized, tourists’ motivations to adopt it remain underexplored. This paper investigates cognitive and affective factors influencing intentions to use VR in heritage tourism contexts. Integrating the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with Anticipated Emotion, an online survey was conducted on 626 respondents. Structural Equation Modelling-Partial Least Squares was employed to test the effects of cognitive and emotional predictors. Results reveal that Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Attitude, Positive and Negative Anticipated Emotions significantly predict VR adoption intentions. Findings further show that combining cognitive and affective antecedents enhances explanatory power. For practitioners, the study offers strategies to promote VR in heritage sites by addressing both rational and emotional motivations, fostering pre-visit engagement and enriching on-site experiences. This represents the first integration of UTAUT and Anticipated Emotion in heritage destination marketing, offering a perspective on VR adoption among visitors.

Article.Title: DuSR-Net: a statistical- and optimization-prior-guided deep-unrolled network with cross-scale manifold alignment for hyperspectral image classification

Article.Title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of immunosuppressive regimens and immune-related outcomes in adeno-associated virus-based gene therapy
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Wu N.; Fu D.; Zhao Q.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSignificant progress has been made in adeno-associated virus (AAV)-based gene therapy. However, host immune responses remain a major challenge to its widespread clinical application, making immunosuppressive regimens an important component of clinical management. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to characterize immunosuppressive regimens and immune-related outcomes in clinical AAV gene therapy. The primary outcomes were the proportions of humoral immune responses, gene therapy-associated uveitis (GTAU), elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and elevated creatine kinase (CK). A total of 73 studies involving 1773 participants were included and categorized as ocular (n = 31), liver (n = 22), muscle (n = 12), or central nervous system (n = 8) according to the primary target organ. Primary subgroup analyses were restricted to studies in which immunosuppression was used prophylactically. The pooled proportions of humoral immune responses were 27.7%, 75.8%, 35.2%, and 42.6% for ocular-, liver-, muscle-, and central nervous system-directed AAV gene therapy, respectively. The pooled proportions of GTAU in ocular-directed studies, elevated ALT in liver-directed studies, elevated CK in muscle-directed studies, and elevated ALT in central nervous system-directed studies were 24.2%, 49.5%, 5.1%, and 16.5%, respectively. Statistically significant regimen-based subgroup differences were observed for GTAU in ocular-directed studies and for humoral immune responses in muscle-directed studies. However, the current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific immunosuppressive regimen. These findings highlight variation in immune-related outcomes across target organs and the need for more clinical studies with standardized outcome reporting to better inform immunosuppressive strategies in AAV gene therapy.

Article.Title: EIDrive: an efficient and interpretable visual-language framework for low-level control signal prediction in autonomous driving
Article.Authors: Dong W.; Cai Y.; Sun X.; Liu Z.; Wang H.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIn recent years, end-to-end autonomous driving models have shown promising potential by directly generating waypoints or control signals from sensor data. In particular, low-level control signals, such as steering angle and vehicle speed, directly determine vehicle motion, making their prediction accuracy and interpretability important to the safety and reliability of autonomous driving systems. However, existing methods mainly regress control signals from visual inputs and lack explicit semantic characterization of the basis underlying control generation, making it difficult to establish a traceable link between scene understanding and control outputs. To address this issue, we proposeEfficient andInterpretable Driving (EIDrive), an efficient visual-language framework for low-level control signal prediction in autonomous driving. Given monocular driving videos, EIDrive jointly performs control signal prediction and natural-language explanation generation. Specifically, a sparse orthogonal subspace projection mechanism is introduced to improve feature compactness and structural expressiveness. A lightweight fine-tuned BERT model is employed as a shared semantic backbone, together with a structured control prediction head to model structured correlations among control-related features. On the BDD-X dataset, EIDrive achieves a turning-angle RMSE of 6.1 and a speed prediction accuracy of 88.2% under the$$1.0\,\mathrm {m/s}$$threshold. It also demonstrates competitive language-generation performance while maintaining a compact computational profile.

Article.Title: Automated SSIM regression for detection and quantification of motion artefacts in brain MR images
Article.Authors: Sciarra A.; Chatterjee S.; Dünnwald M.; Placidi G.; Nürnberger A.; Speck O.; Oeltze-Jafra S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMotion artefacts in magnetic resonance brain images can have a strong impact on diagnostic confidence. The assessment of MR image quality is fundamental before proceeding with the clinical diagnosis. Motion artefacts can alter the delineation of structures such as the brain, lesions or tumours and may require a repeat scan. Otherwise, an inaccurate (e.g. correct pathology but wrong severity) or incorrect diagnosis (e.g. wrong pathology) may occur. “Image quality assessment” as a fast, automated step right after scanning can assist in deciding if the acquired images are diagnostically sufficient. An automated image quality assessment based on the structural similarity index (SSIM) regression through a residual neural network is proposed in this work. Additionally, a classification into different groups - by subdividing with SSIM ranges - is evaluated. Importantly, this method predicts SSIM values of an input image in the absence of a reference ground truth image. The networks were able to detect motion artefacts, and the best performance for the regression and classification task has always been achieved with ResNet-18 with contrast augmentation. The mean and standard deviation of residuals’ distribution were$$\mu =-0.0009$$and$$\sigma =0.0139$$, respectively. Whilst for the classification task in 3, 5 and 10 classes, the best accuracies were 97, 95 and 89%, respectively. The results show that the proposed method could be a tool for supporting neuro-radiologists and radiographers in evaluating image quality quickly.

Article.Title: Prevalence and risk of colorectal adenomas and colorectal cancer among Thai population aged under 50 years
Article.Authors: Kotchanan N.; Kositamongkol C.; Auesomwang C.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe rising global incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) has prompted re-evaluation of screening strategies. This retrospective cross-sectional study aimed to determine the prevalence of colorectal adenoma and CRC and associated clinico-metabolic risk factors among 500 patients younger than 50 years who underwent colonoscopy at Siriraj Hospital between January 2022 and December 2023. The cohort was stratified into three age groups (20–29, 30–39, and 40–49 years), with a secondary analysis comparing the 20–39, 40–44, and 45–49 age subgroups. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent associated factors for colorectal adenoma and CRC. The prevalence of colorectal adenoma and CRC increased significantly with age: 0% (0/35) in the 20–29 age group, 13.1% (14/107) in the 30–39 age group, and 20.7% (74/358) in the 40–49 age group (p< 0.001). Secondary analysis revealed a sharp increase in prevalence starting in the early 40s, with 22.7% (30/132) in the 40–44 age group, which was higher than the 9.9% (14/142) observed in the 20–39 age group (p= 0.004) and similar to the 19.5% (44/226) in the 45–49 age group (p= 0.463). Multivariable logistic regression model revealed that each 1-year increase in age (aOR 1.06; 95% CI 1.01–1.10;p= 0.018) and male sex (aOR 1.95; 95% CI 1.17–3.25;p= 0.010) were independently associated with a higher prevalence of early-onset colorectal adenoma and CRC. These findings underscore the critical need for prompt diagnostic evaluation and early colonoscopy in adults under 50-particularly males and those in their early 40s-rather than informing average-risk screening guidelines.

Article.Title: Deep-learning-enabled distributed acoustic monitoring of bird activity on overhead transmission lines
Article.Authors: Fan X.; Wu B.; Gui J.; Xue B.; Xu J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTo address the mismatch between the urgent need for bird-hazard prevention on transmission lines and the spatiotemporal limitations of existing monitoring approaches, and to support operation and maintenance (O&M) units in implementing targeted mitigation strategies, we propose a distributed acoustic sensing-based method for bird-call event detection and bird-call classification on overhead transmission lines. To resolve the difficulty of detecting bird calls under complex noisy conditions, we develop a bird-call event detection model that integrates time-frequency feature extraction with time-frequency joint attention. Using log-Mel spectrograms as input, the model achieves a detection accuracy of 97.48 ± 0.12%, with a detection latency of 7.3 ms for a single 0.5 s window. The detected signals are then further transformed into MFCC heatmaps, from which time-cepstral features are extracted using a multi-scale convolutional backbone. Combined with denoising autoencoder (DAE)-based feature enhancement, this framework enables bird-call classification under severe environmental noise. Ablation experiments show that each module contributes substantially to the overall classification performance. Across five independent runs on the fixed independent test set, the full classification model achieved a mean accuracy of 95.67 ± 0.16%, outperforming the adapted TSAM-Net by 5.61% points. These results demonstrate the feasibility, accuracy and robustness of the proposed method under simulated transmission-line conditions with complex noise, and provide a promising technical basis for future monitoring of bird activity along long-distance transmission lines.

Article.Title: Development of a PLS-SEM-ANN hybrid model for predicting college students’ academic achievement from physical exercise through social support and psychological resilience
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; Lyu C.; Zhu Y.; Guo H.; Zhang Q.; Fan Y.

Article.Title: Subsurface basin structure, seismic site conditions and earthquake damage: case study of the Gölbaşi basin, Türkiye
Article.Authors: Büyüksaraç A.; Bektaş Ö.; Pamuk E.; Fırat S.; Işık E.; Işık N.; Çetin K.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGölbaşı (Adıyaman) Town, located within a basin along a left-stepping segment of the East Anatolian Fault Zone in Türkiye, experienced severe damage during the 6 February 2023 Mw 7.8 and Mw 7.6 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. Widespread liquefaction, ground subsidence, lateral spreading, bearing capacity failures and building collapses occurred, with their spatial distribution suggesting a strong association between basin geometry and ground motion amplification. This study investigates the subsurface geometry and sediment thickness of the Gölbaşı Basin using an integrated approach combining microgravity measurements and Spatial Autocorrelation (SPAC) analyses. A total of 120 microgravity measurements were conducted to delineate the lateral and vertical extent of low-density alluvial deposits, and two-dimensional gravity models were constructed along four profiles. Additionally, SPAC measurements at 20 locations yielded deep shear-wave velocity (Vs) profiles, from which Vs30 values were derived. Basin-depth proxies (Z1.0and Z2.5) were subsequently estimated from Vs30 using empirical relationships. The basin contains up to approximately 700 m of unconsolidated sediments. Variations in sediment thickness and basin geometry produce significant lateral heterogeneity in seismic velocity and impedance contrasts across the basin. Areas underlain by the thickest sediments experienced the most severe structural damage. The results demonstrate a strong spatial association between sediment thickness, basin geometry, seismic site conditions, and the observed distribution of structural damage. A neighborhood-based Pearson correlation analysis revealed a very strong positive relationship between the severe-damage ratio and sediment thickness (r= 0.905,p< 0.001), a strong positive correlation with Z2.5(r= 0.763,p= 0.017) and a strong negative correlation with Vs30 (r= − 0.698,p= 0.037). Although the correlations with Z1.0and the gravity anomaly did not reach the 5% significance level, they exhibited similarly strong spatial trends. Given the limited number of neighborhoods analyzed (n= 9), these results are interpreted as exploratory spatial associations rather than evidence of causal relationships. Nevertheless, the agreement among the gravity-derived basin geometry, SPAC-derived site parameters, and the damage analysis indicates that sediment thickness and subsurface basin structure were significant contributors to the spatial distribution of earthquake damage.

Article.Title: Accelerometer-derived ‘weekend warrior’ physical activity, genetic susceptibility, and the associated risk of osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Wei S.; Yu S.; Chen G.; Zhang Z.; Lei Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPhysical activity is important for health, but the association between the temporal distribution of weekly moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and incident osteoarthritis (OA) remains uncertain. This observational cohort analysis included 70,608 UK Biobank participants. Physical activity exposure was based on UK Biobank processed accelerometer variables derived from wrist-worn Axivity AX3 devices. Participants were classified as inactive (< 150 min/week MVPA), regularly active ( > = 150 min/week with < 50% accumulated during the two most active days), or weekend warriors (WW; >=150 min/week with > = 50% accumulated during the two most active days). The two most active days were not required to be Saturday and Sunday. Cox proportional hazards models estimated associations with incident overall, knee, hip, and hand OA after covariate adjustment; associations were also examined across OA polygenic risk strata. Compared with inactivity, both the WW and regularly active patterns were associated with lower overall OA risk. A direct comparison of the WW and regularly active groups showed no statistically significant difference in overall OA hazard. Site-specific associations differed: the two patterns showed similar associations with knee OA, while the WW group had a 21% higher risk of hand OA than the regularly active group. For hip OA, an inverse association was observed for the WW group, whereas the estimate for the regularly active group was not statistically significant. Associations between activity patterns and OA were observed across polygenic risk strata. The WW pattern defined by the two most active days was associated with lower overall OA risk compared with inactivity, and the direct comparison with regularly distributed activity was not statistically significant. Site-specific findings should be interpreted cautiously. Because this was an observational analysis of processed wrist-accelerometer variables, the results do not establish causality or identify joint-level mechanisms.

Article.Title: Infrared intensity-aware feature learning for robust target detection in infrared images
Article.Authors: Yu J.; Liu S.; Li Q.; Zhang C.; Qiu J.; Li Z.; Wan J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractInfrared target detection is challenging because of strong background noise, weak foreground–background intensity contrast, blurred boundaries, and limited target pixels. Motivated by the challenges observed in infrared inspection scenarios, this paper proposes YOLOv11-IR-TSD, an infrared-adaptive detector for improving feature representation and localization accuracy. In the backbone, a lightweight DnCNN-Lite module is introduced to suppress infrared imaging noise, while the original spatial pyramid pooling structure is replaced with an infrared-intensity-aware spatial pyramid pooling–fast (IIA-SPPF) module to enhance multi-scale feature representation. In the neck, a DINOv2-assisted self-supervised contrastive guidance mechanism and an infrared-intensity-gradient-weighted fusion strategy are employed to improve feature discrimination under complex backgrounds. In addition, a feature alignment constraint, an infrared-intensity-adaptive activation function, and a lightweight bounding-box refinement module are incorporated into the detection head to improve cross-stage feature consistency and localization accuracy. Experiments on the public FLIR and LLVIP infrared detection benchmarks show that YOLOv11-IR-TSD achieves mAP@0.5 values of 91.0% and 89.5%, respectively, while maintaining inference speeds of 64 and 62 FPS. Compared with existing infrared detection approaches, the proposed detector achieves improved detection accuracy while maintaining efficient inference, and exhibits enhanced robustness under noise interference, weak intensity contrast, and complex background conditions. Additional analyses under different target scales and contrast conditions further indicate the effectiveness of the proposed feature-learning strategy for challenging infrared scenes. Further evaluation on dedicated real-world infrared insulator datasets is required to investigate its applicability to abnormal-heating inspection.

Article.Title: Development and reliability test of the work stress questionnaire for cancer survivors after returning to work (WSQ-CS)
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Zhong Y.; Dai J.; Shen P.; Ma L.; Peng P.; Guo Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTo develop and conduct an initial psychometric evaluation of a context-specific questionnaire measuring perceived work-related stress among cancer survivors after returning to work. A descriptive phenomenological study was conducted with 20 cancer survivors, and the interview data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step method to generate the initial item pool. The Transactional Model of Stress served as a sensitizing framework for developing the interview guide. Two rounds of Delphi expert consultation were conducted between May and July 2022, followed by pilot testing in July 2022. Independent samples of 252 and 200 cancer survivors were recruited from two tertiary hospitals in Nanjing and Taizhou, China, for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, respectively. The final WSQ-CS comprised 24 items across five dimensions: physiological load, psychological load, economic load, obstruction of self-development, and social support deficit. The I-CVI values ranged from 0.83 to 1.00, and the S-CVI was 0.966. The overall Cronbach’s α was 0.914. EFA identified a five-factor structure accounting for 63.44% of the total variance. CFA showed that most fit indices met recommended thresholds, providing preliminary support for the five-factor structure. The questionnaire has undergone rigorous development and psychometric testing, and the findings support its reliability and validity. It can serve as an important assessment tool for the psychosocial rehabilitation of cancer survivors and provides a reliable measurable instrument for related research.

Article.Title: Application optimization of visual-verbal cue learning in image search system
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Hong J.; Luo X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIn modern image retrieval systems, effective alignment between visual and language modalities and efficient retrieval are critical for enhancing system performance. However, traditional prompt learning methods struggle to achieve good generalization. This paper proposes a visual–language prompt learning method, MaPLeMeta, designed to improve the overall performance of image retrieval systems. MaPLeMeta combines dual-modal prompt learning techniques by introducing learnable prompts in both the visual and text encoders, enabling deep alignment between visual features and textual descriptions. Additionally, MaPLeMeta optimizes visual and textual prompts through an asymmetric contrastive learning objective, improving the semantic consistency and retrieval accuracy of cross-modal features. After representation learning, a standard HNSW index is employed only as an engineering component to accelerate approximate nearest-neighbor search; it does not participate in prompt optimization or visual–language alignment. Experiments on DeepFashion show consistent improvements over the evaluated baselines: compared with the strongest baseline, MaPLeMeta increases Recall@1 by 1.3 percentage points (81.5% versus 80.2%) and NDCG@10 by 0.01 (0.89 versus 0.88). These results indicate competitive performance in cross-domain, cross-category, and few-shot retrieval, while the HNSW backend separately improves query efficiency.

Article.Title: Conflict-guided feature filtering for efficient exact decision trees
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Zheng S.; Pan S.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: AbstractExact decision-tree search is sensitive to the number of candidate predicates, motivating efficient front-end mechanisms for controlling the optimization space. We study conflict-guided feature selection (CGFS), in which discretized conflict relevance (DCR) ranks features by the fraction of sampled opposite-label pairs that they distinguish, and introduce joint conflict coverage (JCC) to reduce redundant selections. On five datasets spanning 569–45,222 instances and 14–500 original features, depth-3 PyDL8.5 experiments with a 60-s solver limit show that DCR at$$K=10$$reduces end-to-end time by$$2.74$$–$$348.60\times $$on completed full-feature runs, while the all-timeout Madelon configuration yields a$$>397.78\times $$lower bound. Direct MurTree validation independently reproduces substantial reductions on the harder Hill–Valley and Madelon representations. JCC further recovers complementary signal groups under controlled redundancy. Together, these results establish conflict coverage as an auditable front-end criterion for reducing candidate-predicate burden before exact decision-tree optimization, with predictive effects characterized explicitly across datasets.

Article.Title: Temporal soil nitrogen dynamics with stand age of Betula platyphylla forests in the permafrost region of Northeast China
Article.Authors: Wei H.; Chen X.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractNitrogen (N) is a key nutrient regulating plant growth, forest productivity and ecosystem functioning in permafrost regions. Despite the critical role of succession in modifying soil N processes, how soil N dynamics respond to mid-successionalBetula platyphyllaforest development remains poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize soil N transformations across a 25- to 61-year stand-age gradient in permafrost forests of Northeast China. We determined soil inorganic nitrogen concentrations and net nitrogen mineralization (ammonization + nitrification) using in‑situ incubation experiments in 25-, 40- and 61-year-old mid-successionalBetula platyphyllaforests. Ammonium N increased significantly with stand age, whereas nitrate N concentration exhibited a decreasing trend. Generalized least‑squares (GLS‑AR1) modelling detected no significant main effect of stand age on soil inorganic N or net N mineralization rate (Rm). Mean Min-N remained stable across stands (8.39, 8.15 and 8.49 mg·kg⁻¹ for the 25-, 40-, and 61-year-old stands, respectively). Rm showed a numerical increase along the age gradient (0.11, 0.46, 0.67 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹). Soil N dynamics were driven by significant stand‑age × soil‑depth and stand‑age × sample‑month interactions rather than stand age main effects. Inorganic‑N and mineralization rates were higher in topsoil (0–10 cm) than subsoil (10–20 cm). Ammonification dominated net N mineralization across all stands, contributing on average 3.88% (0–10 cm) and 4.18% (10–20 cm). Hierarchical partitioning analysis identified stand age as the primary driver of soil‑N variation, followed by sampling month, soil chemical properties and microbial biomass. Mid‑successionalBetula platyphyllaforest succession accelerates soil N turnover and modifies inorganic‑N composition without expanding total mineral‑N pools. These findings inform vegetation restoration and sustainable management of permafrost forest ecosystems.

Article.Title: Psychological pathways associated with gamified physical education and perceived learning in adolescents and young adults
Article.Authors: Wang D.; Duanmu S.; Yao L.; Liu Y.; Xiao T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGamified technology is increasingly used in physical education (PE), but evidence remains fragmented across motivation, engagement, and learning-related outcomes. This study proposed and empirically tested an integrated model linking students’ perceptions of gamified PE with psychological need satisfaction, motivation, multidimensional engagement, and perceived learning outcomes. A cross-sectional survey was completed by 500 secondary and tertiary students (mean age = 18.90 years, SD = 3.77; 51.4% female) from five institutions across three countries. Participants had experienced institution-approved gamified PE platforms sharing points, badges, feedback, challenges, progress indicators, meaningful choice, and cooperative activities, with limited teacher-level variation. A 43-item questionnaire measured 11 reflective constructs; 42 indicators were retained. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Gamified Technology Use and Perceived Enjoyment were positively associated with autonomy, competence, and relatedness satisfaction. Need satisfaction was positively associated with intrinsic and extrinsic motivation; motivation was positively associated with behavioral, emotional, and cognitive engagement; and all engagement dimensions were positively associated with perceived learning outcomes. The model explained 58.9% of PLO variance. Direct GTU–PLO and PE–PLO associations were nonsignificant, whereas the specified sequential indirect associations were significant. The findings support a cross-sectional pattern consistent with the proposed framework but do not establish causal or temporal mediation. Mastery-oriented feedback, meaningful task choice, progress tracking, and cooperative missions warrant further experimental evaluation, while public ranking should be used cautiously.

Article.Title: A national propensity score-matched analysis of simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplantation from donation after circulatory death and brain death donors
Article.Authors: Lim T.; Crichton E.; Baselious E.; Ketsan T.; Jurkovich A.; Cui Y.; Nissen N.; Kosari K.; Voidonikolas G.; Todo T.; Steggerda J.; Wisel S.; Kim I.; Brennan T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIncreased use of donation after circulatory death (DCD) organs can lessen the ongoing organ shortage in transplantation. While DCD donor utilization has increased in other types of organ transplantation, with outcomes comparable to donation after brain death (DBD) donors, DCD use in pancreas transplantation is declining. To rigorously define the risk of DCD pancreas donors and control for confounding variables, we performed a propensity score-matched analysis of adult simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) transplantations. Using data from the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) registry, we examined 1036 propensity-matched pancreas transplant recipients of 777 DBD and 259 DCD donor organs between 2010 and 2022. In univariable Cox proportional hazards models fitted in the propensity score-matched cohort, with robust variance estimates clustered by matched set, SPK recipients of DCD donors had post-transplant patient and graft survival outcomes comparable to those of DBD donors at 1 and 3 years. DCD recipients experienced similar rates of treatment for graft rejection at 6 months and 1 year, comparable rates of postoperative complications, and similar renal function at 1 year compared with DBD recipients. SPK recipients of DCD donors benefited from significantly shorter wait times for organs than recipients of DBD donors. The use of DCD donors in pancreas transplantation can safely increase organ availability.

Article.Title: Lake Urmia desiccation drives building heating and cooling energy demand in northwestern Iran
Article.Authors: Maboudi Reveshti A.; Maroofiazar R.; Ebrahimpour A.; Fatourehchi M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe progressive desiccation of terminal lakes under global climate change represents an emerging environmental challenge with significant implications for regional climate and building energy demand. This study investigates the impact of Lake Urmia desiccation on building energy consumption across 13 cities in the Lake Urmia Basin in northwestern Iran during 2001–2023. Using MODIS land surface temperature, Landsat water-extent monitoring, MERRA-2 reanalysis, and GPM precipitation data, we generated 299 year-specific weather files for 13 cities across the Lake Urmia Basin. Year-by-year EnergyPlus simulations of representative residential and commercial building archetypes were conducted to quantify the progressive impacts of drought-induced climatic changes on heating and cooling demand. Results show that the 90% reduction in lake surface area coincided with a 1.8–2.4 °C rise in summer temperatures and a 0.8–1.2 °C increase in annual mean temperatures. A control-city analysis indicates that the majority of these temperature changes can be attributed to lake-desiccation-driven mesoscale forcing rather than generic urban or regional warming. Annual cooling energy increased by 18–35% for residential and 22–42% for commercial buildings, while heating demand declined by 8–15%, resulting in a net HVAC energy increase of 12–23%. Cities within 30 km of the former lakeshore experienced impacts 40–60% greater than those in more distant areas, confirming the spatial attenuation of lake-related climatic effects. Strong negative correlations between lake surface area and cooling energy (r = − 0.82 to − 0.91,p< 0.001) further demonstrate a robust association between lake desiccation and increasing cooling demand. The cumulative additional annual energy cost across the basin was estimated at $127–218 million, while peak cooling demand increased by 15–25%, potentially placing additional pressure on electricity-grid stability. These findings have important implications for regional energy-infrastructure planning, climate-adaptive building design, urban cooling strategies, and lake-restoration policies in semi-arid regions undergoing large-scale environmental degradation.

Article.Title: Comparative characterization of the mucosal eukaryotic virome across independent whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing cohorts
Article.Authors: Na H.; Park J.; Kim T.; Choi N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe human mucosal eukaryotic virome remains incompletely characterized because methodological heterogeneity limits direct comparisons across independent whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing (WMS) datasets. To address this limitation, we reanalyzed publicly available DNA-based WMS datasets representing healthy body-site samples together with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated disease, and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) using the same ViromeScan-based analytical approach. Viral count profiles were converted to within-sample relative abundances for Bray–Curtis analyses, host-unmapped read depth was included as a covariate in PERMANOVA, and alpha-diversity findings were evaluated using repeated rarefaction. Anatomical site remained associated with eukaryotic virome diversity and community structure in the HMP cohort after accounting for sequencing depth, and site-associated differences were also observed in the independent NPC cohort analyzed using the same approach. HPV infection status was also associated with viral community structure after depth adjustment, whereas DOI-defined OSCC groups showed no significant global differences in alpha diversity, normalized viral recovery, or community structure and yielded only exploratory taxon-level signals. Across datasets, viral recovery varied with host-unmapped sequencing depth, with substantial between-sample heterogeneity. Together, these findings show that consistent application of publicly available analytical tools can support comparative characterization of eukaryotic virome profiles from existing WMS datasets, while also highlighting the importance of sequencing depth and cautious interpretation of taxon-level associations.

Article.Title: Isolation and phenotypic characterization of bacteriophages targeting multidrug-resistant biofilm-forming uropathogenic Escherichia coli from hospital sewage
Article.Authors: Tamrat E.; Derbie A.; Mekonnen F.; Asmare Z.; Geteneh A.; Kassa T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUropathogenicEscherichia coli(UPEC) is a major cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), with multidrug resistance (MDR) and biofilm formation complicating treatment. This study isolated and phenotypically characterized bacteriophages targeting MDR and biofilm-forming UPEC from hospital sewage in Ethiopia. Twenty-three archived MDR UPEC isolates were screened for biofilm formation, and phages were characterized by host range, efficiency of plating, multiplicity of infection (MOI), adsorption kinetics, one-step growth, environmental stability, and biofilm biomass reduction. Eight isolates (34.8%) formed biofilms, including 3 strong, 1 moderate, and 4 weak biofilm formers. Two phages, ΦET-3175 and ΦFETA-207, were isolated with titers of 1.35 × 10⁹ and 1.12 × 10⁹ PFU/mL, respectively. ΦET-3175 showed broader activity, with detectable activity against 6/23 (26.1%) isolates, an optimal MOI of 0.1, > 95% adsorption within 20 min, a latent period of approximately 30 min, and a burst size of 147 ± 4.6 PFU per infected cell. Both phages retained detectable activity across pH 4–10 and at temperatures up to 50 °C. ΦET-3175 reduced biofilm biomass by 3.2–39.5% among four susceptible biofilm-forming isolates, but the paired difference was not statistically significant (Z = − 1.826,p= 0.068). These findings provide preliminary in-vitro phenotypic evidence and support further genomic, structural, and biological characterization.

Article.Title: Dynamically tunable anisotropic Rabi model in circuit QED
Article.Authors: Tabatabaei S.; Zare Rameshti B.; Akbari M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractWe propose a circuit QED architecture that realizes the full anisotropic Rabi model (ARM) with in-situ tunability of its interaction symmetry. The circuit comprises a superconducting qubit coupled to a resonator through two simultaneous channels: a direct inductive path and a flux-tunable capacitive path mediated by a transmon coupler. By controlling the external magnetic flux, the destructive and constructive interferences between these paths continuously tune the ratio of the Jaynes–Cummings (JC) and anti-Jaynes–Cummings (AJC) couplings, sweeping the system across the entire ARM parameter space from pure JC, through the standard Rabi regime, to pure AJC without requiring rotating-wave approximations or external parametric drives. Furthermore, we identify a coherence sweet spot where the dispersive shift and photon shot-noise dephasing are suppressed. In the pure AJC regime, we demonstrate that the vacuum Rabi splitting vanishes and the Purcell decay rate is strongly mitigated while preserving high qubit readout contrast.

Article.Title: Environmental and personal BTEX exposure and inhalation health risks in healthcare-waste treatment units
Article.Authors: Shojaei A.; Khazaei M.; Rostami R.; Bahrami A.; Samarghandi M.; Samadi M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study investigated spatial and operational variations in airborne benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylenes (BTEX), personal exposure, and inhalation health risks in eight healthcare-waste treatment units in Hamadan, Iran. A total of 64 area air samples were collected, with 16 samples for each location–condition combination (indoor inactive, indoor post-treatment, perimeter inactive, and perimeter post-treatment), and personal breathing-zone samples were obtained from 16 workers. BTEX was analyzed by gas chromatography, and health risks were estimated using the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency framework. Risk estimates were based on 4 h/day of exposure, 300 exposure days/year, and the selected toxicity values. Monte Carlo simulation with 10,000 iterations characterized risk variability and sensitivity. Mean total BTEX increased significantly from 178.50 ± 15.56 to 307.57 ± 19.45 µg/m3indoors and from 34.54 ± 3.18 to 64.22 ± 6.69 µg/m3at perimeter locations. Post-treatment concentrations were positively associated with temperature and the number of autoclave cycles and inversely associated with time since the last cycle and relative humidity (RH). Post meridiem (PM)-shift workers had higher total BTEX exposure, hazard index (HI), and daily inhalation dose than ante meridiem (AM)-shift workers. Aggregate HI remained < 1 in observed and simulated estimates under the specified exposure assumptions. In contrast, benzene and cumulative carcinogenic risks exceeded 1 × 10–6but remained below 1 × 10–4. Exposure time was the dominant contributor to non-carcinogenic risk variability. These findings support continued occupational monitoring and control of autoclave-related BTEX exposure, particularly during post-treatment activities and prolonged exposure.

Article.Title: Cloud-deployable deep learning for smartphone-based body fluid cytology: a multi-architecture evaluation of YOLO and RT-DETR models
Article.Authors: Chomean S.; Khemtonglang N.; Mukda E.; Sittiphokkhasap N.; Changtrakul Y.; Wongphat K.; Mungmai A.; Tanantong T.; Kaset C.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAccurate cytological evaluation of body fluid specimens is essential for diagnosing inflammatory and malignant conditions, yet manual interpretation remains labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. This study developed and deployed a smartphone-based deep learning framework for multi-class body fluid cell classification integrating object detection, ROI-based classification, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Three hundred Wright–Giemsa–stained cytospin slides, one per patient, were used to generate 7149 smartphone-acquired images, which were annotated and curated into seven predominant cell classes. To reduce data leakage, images were partitioned at the source-photograph (slide-field) level. Five detection architectures (YOLOv8n, YOLOv10n, YOLOv11n, YOLOv11n-seg, and RT-DETR) were trained and evaluated on a held-out test set. YOLOv11n-seg achieved the highest mAP@50 (0.840), mAP@50–95 (0.757), and precision (0.772), while YOLOv11n achieved the highest recall (0.823). For YOLOv11n-seg, confusion-matrix macro-F1 and weighted-F1 were 0.720 and 0.730, respectively. Eosinophils, lymphocytes, and neutrophils were among the better-recognized classes, whereas errors were more frequent among monocytes, macrophages, and mesothelial cells. Grad-CAM++ analysis showed that model activation was predominantly centered within cell regions but was interpreted only as supportive model-inspection evidence. A Streamlit web application demonstrated browser-based inference with detection overlays, cell counts, differential composition, and data export. The system should currently be regarded as research, educational, and decision-support prototype rather than a standalone diagnostic device. External validation with patient-level separation, multiple imaging configurations, and broader cell populations is required before clinical application can be considered.

Article.Title: Assessment of information quality and reliability on lumbar disc herniation in short videos from Douyin
Article.Authors: Shen T.; Gong Q.; Hu Y.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLumbar disc herniation is a common cause of neurological symptoms and is associated with substantial decreases in health-related quality of life. Douyin has emerged as a leading social media platform, and an increasing number of users seek information on lumbar disc herniation there. However, the quality of such content remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the informational quality of Douyin short videos related to lumbar disc herniation. Using a cross-sectional design, we retrieved the top 100 videos related to lumbar disc herniation from the Douyin platform on October 17, 2025, using the default ranking. Video quality and reliability were evaluated with the Global Quality Scale (GQS) and the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) tools. Videos were compared across uploader categories, and correlation analyses were conducted to examine factors potentially associated with video quality. Among the 96 videos related to lumbar disc herniation ultimately included in the analysis, the median duration was 71 s. The median counts were 17,240 likes, 9,749 collections, 1,041 comments, and 6,830 shares. Overall information quality was modest, and reliability was low. Differences in GQS and mDISCERN scores across uploader groups were not statistically significant. Correlation analyses indicated that the numbers of likes, comments, collections, and shares were not associated with video quality. The quality of Douyin videos related to lumbar disc herniation warrants improvement. Establishing minimum quality standards for health education videos is essential to ensure that the public receives trustworthy information.

Article.Title: Numerical analysis of hydrodynamic responses to bed roughness in vegetated open channels under subcritical flow conditions
Article.Authors: Mumtaz M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractVegetation is widely recognized as an effective nature-based solution for flood mitigation because it increases hydraulic resistance and promotes flow energy dissipation. Although numerous studies have investigated vegetation-induced flow resistance and the influence of bed roughness independently, the coupled effects of vegetation and varying bed roughness under subcritical flow conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a validated computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model based on the standard k-epsilon (k-ε) turbulence closure to investigate roughness-vegetation interactions in a vegetated open channel. The numerical model was validated against experimental streamwise velocity profiles under three subcritical flow conditions (Froude number (Fr) = 0.40, 0.44, and 0.48), yielding good agreement with laboratory measurements (correlation coefficient (R) = 0.91–0.96 and root mean square error (RMSE) = 0.0152–0.0259). Following validation, the model was applied to seven subcritical flow conditions (Fr = 0.40–0.65) and four equivalent sand-grain roughness heights (Ks = 0, 7.22, 14.32, and 24.47 mm) to evaluate their influence on velocity distribution, turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), turbulent eddy dissipation (TED), and bed shear stress (BSS). The results showed that increasing bed roughness enhanced flow resistance and significantly modified turbulence characteristics within the vegetated channel. Relative to the smooth-bed condition, the maximum velocity decreased by 6%, based on the validated velocity field and the associated k–ε turbulence closure, TKE was found to decreased by 31.4%, and the maximum BSS increased by 70% at the highest roughness height (Ks = 24.47 mm). These findings demonstrate that bed roughness substantially alters vegetation-controlled flow behavior and provide new insight into roughness–vegetation interactions for the design and optimization of sustainable nature-based flood mitigation systems.

Article.Title: Mammalian recombinant production of mature peptide hormone insulin-like 3 (INSL3)
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Metivier R.; Fischer E.; Kruse A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractInsulin-like 3 (INSL3) is a peptide hormone important for regulating male reproductive physiology. INSL3 belongs to the insulin/relaxin family of peptide hormones, which are synthesized in cells as prohormones containing B-C-A chains. These hormones mature following proteolytic processing by prohormone convertases to remove C chain and yield mature hormones containing B-A chains that are stabilized by two inter-chain and one intra-chain disulfide bonds. It has been a challenge in the field to produce recombinant active mature INSL3 in large quantities because the enzymes that process INSL3 are unclear. Here we report prohormone convertases PCSK1 and PCSK3, and carboxypeptidase E together process INSL3 prohormone into mature INSL3 and established a simple method to produce recombinant active mature INSL3 in a mammalian expression system using an engineered Fc-fusion approach with co-expression of processing enzymes. Furthermore, we confirmed the molecular weight of the recombinant INSL3 matches the native hormone by intact mass spectrometry, and the recombinant mature INSL3 display full activity (EC50= 360 pM) in signaling assays of its cognate receptor RXFP2. Notably, the Fc-fusion INSL3 is also fully active (EC50= 609 pM) and has a much higher yield and a simpler production method. Lastly, peptide hormones of this family are conserved prohormone convertase substrates, therefore this method can potentially be applied to the expression and purification of other peptide hormones within this family with some optimization.

Article.Title: Determinants of multidimensional child health outcomes among infants in an urban poor setting in Makassar, Indonesia
Article.Authors: BaharuddinNur R.; Wijaya E.; Irmayanti I.; Wahyuni A.; Ansariadi A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractChild malnutrition remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia. However, the factors associated with multidimensional child health outcomes (MCHO), defined as the coexistence of anthropometric failure and infectious morbidity, remain poorly understood. Examining these conditions jointly is important because undernutrition and infection are biologically interconnected, frequently coexist, and together impose a greater burden on child health than either condition alone. This study examined maternal and child determinants of MCHO in a cross-sectional analysis nested within an ongoing birth cohort of 142 mother–child pairs (children aged 6–13 months) participating in an ongoing birth cohort in an urban poor setting in Makassar, Indonesia. Nutritional status was assessed using World Health Organization anthropometric indicators, and associations were estimated using Firth penalised-likelihood logistic regression with sensitivity analyses based on modified Poisson regression and E-values. MCHO affected 14.79% of children, while stunting, wasting, underweight, and recent infectious morbidity affected 23.94%, 19.72%, 11.97%, and 30.99%, respectively. Caesarean delivery was independently associated with MCHO, though estimated from a model with a modest events-per-variable ratio (AOR 3.09, 95% CI 1.18–8.10,p= 0.022; adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 2.60, 95% CI 1.17–5.77; E-value 5.63). Recent infectious morbidity was independently associated with wasting (AOR 2.57, 95% CI 1.07–6.16,p= 0.034; aPR 2.01, 95% CI 1.03–3.93; E-value 4.58). Unimproved drinking water showed consistent positive associations with MCHO, stunting, and wasting (allp< 0.10). These findings highlight the associations of maternal, infectious, and environmental factors with child health and underscore the need for integrated interventions that address nutrition, infection prevention, maternal and child health, and household environmental conditions simultaneously.

Article.Title: Pulse duration and pulse repetition frequency shape cavitation dynamics and volumetric liquefaction by histotripsy in a fibrous tissue-mimicking phantom
Article.Authors: Nanda Kumar Y.; Wang Y.; Kreider W.; Han Q.; Liu J.; Vlaisavljevich E.; Schade G.; Maxwell A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractHistotripsy is a focused ultrasound technique that mechanically liquefies tissue through cavitation bubble activity and has shown promise for noninvasive tumor ablation. However, treating fibrous, mechanically robust tissues remains challenging, and the influence of pulse parameters on cavitation dynamics and liquefaction efficiency in these tissues is not well understood. Here, we systematically investigated the combined effects of pulse duration and pulse repetition frequency (PRF) on cavitation behavior and lesion formation in a fibrous tissue-mimicking double-network hydrogel. Pulse duration and PRF were varied over four orders of magnitude while maintaining a constant 1% duty cycle. High-speed photographic imaging, shear wave elastography (SWE), B-mode ultrasound, and open-top light-sheet (OTLS) microscopy were used to relate cavitation behavior to phantom damage and liquefaction. The 1-cycle condition produced the largest bubble cloud area at longer exposure times, while the 1 and 10-cycle conditions exhibited higher frame-to-frame correlation and greater spatial persistence. In contrast, longer-pulse, low-PRF exposures (≥ 100 cycles) produced more localized cavitation and contiguous lesion formation. Among the tested parameters, 1,000 -cycle pulses at 10 Hz yielded the highest volumetric liquefaction rates. In contrast, short-pulse, high-PRF conditions generated substantial total damage but little to no fully liquefied volume. These findings show that pulse duration and PRF shape cavitation behavior and liquefaction in this fibrous tissue-mimicking model.

Article.Title: PPO-based QoS-aware resource management for multi-class URLLC and eMBB slices in NR/NR-U HetNets
Article.Authors: Elmosilhy N.; Elmesalawy M.; El-Haleem A.; Ibrahim I.
Article.Abstract: AbstractExploiting new radio (NR) and NR-unlicensed (NR-U) technologies within a multi-RAT heterogeneous network can leverage traffic congestion and enhance overall capacity. thus, an optimization problem is introduced and formulated to maximize users’ quality of service (QoS) satisfaction by maximizing data rates while satisfying critical latency requirements. To accommodate heterogeneous URLLC services, multiple traffic classes with different delay requirements are considered, and a scalable numerology mini-slot technique is employed to satisfy the QoS requirements of each traffic class. An iterative framework is presented that combines regret matching learning for user association considering coexisting Wi-Fi users and a proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm which determines the optimal resource distribution based on a predefined numerology value for each slice. A logarithmic utility function is presented to enforce proportional fairness while satisfying each user’s service requirements. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an overall QoS satisfaction rate of 74% significantly outperforming benchmark architectures including NR-only, NR-Wi-Fi, NR-NR-U, and LWA. Furthermore, comparative evaluations against other reinforcement learning algorithms—such as Q-network, deep Q-network (DQN), double DQN, dueling DQN, and actor-critic confirm stability and performance of the proposed PPO-based approach.

Article.Title: Decomposing deep neural network-brain representational similarity reveals distinct sources across the human visual hierarchy
Article.Authors: Li X.; Zhang F.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractDeep neural networks predict neural responses across the visual hierarchy, yet published alignment scores do not reveal whether this correspondence reflects learned representations, architectural inductive biases, low-level image statistics, or categorical structure. We decompose DNN-brain alignment into four sources using variance partitioning on representational similarity analysis, applied to 7T fMRI from eight participants viewing approximately 10,000 natural images. The composition of alignment shifts systematically along the cortical hierarchy: in primary visual cortex, architecture and low-level statistics account for 46% of total explained variance, whereas in high-level visual cortex model-specific learned representations dominate, reaching 68% in the parahippocampal place area. The same framework applied to language models processing image captions reveals that alignment is strongly model-dependent: a sentence embedding model contributes 51% unique variance in higher visual cortex, whereas an autoregressive model contributes only 4%, with the remainder attributable to surface text statistics and category structure. Across nine models, alignment scores varied substantially in composition. Decomposing alignment into its sources is necessary before a score can be interpreted as evidence for convergent processing.

Article.Title: Assessing urban water consumption dynamics using machine learning and spatial variables under normal and pandemic conditions: A case study
Article.Authors: Sabzchi-Dehkharghani H.; Majnooni-Heris A.; Fakherifard A.; Safari M.; Shakouri B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study developed a spatially explicit framework to estimate household water consumption (HWC) and the number of household water subscribers in each consumption class (NHWSCC) using land surface temperature (LST), land value, and elevation. Three machine-learning (ML) models were applied: symbolic regression (SR), an extreme learning machine (ELM), and an ELM hybridized with the artificial bee colony algorithm (ELM-ABC). The spatial predictors supported the generation of HWC maps for normal and pandemic-period conditions in Tabriz, Iran. Model performance was generally more stable at grid resolutions of 600–700 m, although the achievable resolution varied among consumption classes. The models captured spatial patterns for many low- and intermediate-consumption classes but performed less well for the highest-consumption categories. SR sensitivity analysis identified LST as the most influential predictor of NHWSCC. Differences in predictor sensitivity between the study periods suggest changes in the relationships between spatial characteristics and household water use. Observed annual consumption increased in lower-land-value areas and decreased in higher-land-value areas during the pandemic period. These findings support the use of readily available spatial proxies for within-city water-consumption mapping, while recognizing the limitations of the predictors and validation design.

Article.Title: On the use of machine learning in damage identification of offshore jacket wind turbine: a virtual case study
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Pugliese F.; Christie J.; Titurus B.; De Risi R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study presents a high-fidelity, simulation-based Finite Element – Operational Modal Analysis – Machine Learning (FE–OMA–ML) framework for damage diagnosis of a jacket-type offshore wind turbine support structure. Finite-element-simulated acceleration responses are processed using Enhanced Frequency-Domain Decomposition (EFDD) to identify modal frequencies and damping ratios, which are then used as machine-learning input features. A progressive stiffness-degradation dataset covering 13 structural conditions and multiple sensor configurations is constructed to represent the gradual nature of in-service deterioration. The proposed approach is evaluated in terms of exact component-level classification, binary damage detection, layer-level localisation, ensemble-vote-based ranking, response-noise robustness, and sensor-layout optimisation. The reliability of the extracted modal features is further examined through FE–EFDD consistency checks of natural frequencies and mode shapes. The results show that the workflow retains useful hierarchical and ranked diagnostic information across different degradation levels, sensor layouts, and noisy-response conditions. However, exact component localisation becomes more sensitive as data complexity and measurement noise increase. The analysis also supports identifying efficient sensor configurations that preserve useful diagnostic performance. The proposed framework therefore provides a structured numerical strategy for evaluating modal-feature-based damage diagnosis of offshore jacket support structures.

Article.Title: Machine learning prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement after TAVI
Article.Authors: Shan Y.; Liu P.; Zhao Z.; Wang H.; Lai J.; Qiu X.; Li X.; Wang S.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe fate of mitral regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve implantation is highly heterogeneous, and accurate preoperative prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based predictive model for regurgitation improvement following transcatheter aortic valve implantation. This single-centre retrospective study included 324 patients with moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation who underwent transcatheter aortic valve implantation between 2019 and 2024 (development cohort) and 120 patients in 2025 (temporal validation cohort). Eleven machine learning algorithms were compared. Feature selection was performed using a dual-screening strategy combining the Boruta algorithm and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis was used to interpret predictor contributions to model predictions. Six variables were identified as robust predictors: functional mitral regurgitation, interventricular septal thickness, atrial fibrillation, left ventricular ejection fraction, surgical approach, and left atrial diameter. In temporal validation, logistic regression achieved an AUC of 0.788 (95% CI 0.694–0.883), followed by Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression (AUC, 0.787; 95% CI 0.693–0.882) and CatBoost (AUC, 0.778; 95% CI 0.683–0.872). Interventricular septal thickness showed a significant nonlinear association with mitral regurgitation improvement, with approximately 1.1 cm suggested as a provisional breakpoint in an exploratory analysis. This machine learning model enables individualized prediction of mitral regurgitation improvement after transcatheter aortic valve implantation using readily available preoperative parameters. The identification of interventricular septal thickness as a nonlinear predictor with a potentially clinically relevant threshold suggests promise for preoperative risk stratification. Nevertheless, because both the development and temporal validation cohorts were derived from a single centre, these findings are preliminary and require prospective multicentre validation before any clinical implementation.

Article.Title: Integrated classical/quantum–classical neural networks, DFT, and experiments for predicting bandgap and color of CrxSbxTi1−2xO2 yellow-orange pigments
Article.Authors: Vaselnia S.; Aminian M.; Banadaki R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe accurate prediction of the bandgap ($$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$) and color of ceramic pigments is of considerable importance in materials science research. In this work, we investigate the$$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$and color of Cr$$_x$$Sb$$_x$$Ti$$_{1-2x}$$O$$_2$$rutile pigments by combining experimental, density functional theory (DFT and DFT+U) calculations, and neural network approaches. The main novelty of this study is the application of classical/hybrid quantum–classical neural networks to the prediction of pigment color and$$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$. Cr/Sb co-doped rutile pigment was synthesized and characterized, and the electronic structures of undoped and doped$${\textrm{TiO}}_{2}$$were analyzed using first-principles calculations. In parallel, classical and hybrid quantum–classical neural network models were developed and trained on datasets compiled from the Materials Project database and literature-reported rutile-based pigments. The models successfully captured the trends in$$\text {E}_{\text {g}}$$and chromaticity, with the hybrid architectures providing slightly improved predictive performance and more consistent agreement with experiment. Overall, this work demonstrates an effective framework that links experiment, first-principles calculations, and classical/quantum–classical neural networks for predicting key properties of ceramic pigments, and it points toward the future use of fully quantum machine learning models for materials design.

Article.Title: Generation of a recombinant, antibiotic resistance gene-free Leishmania tarentolae strain as a live vaccine platform
Article.Authors: Taheri T.; Davarpanah E.; Santi A.; Gholami E.; Seyed N.; Späth G.; Rafati S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLive vaccines based on non-pathogenic microorganisms are among the most effective vaccine platforms.L. tarentolae, a non-pathogenic protozoan for humans, is a valuable expression system capable of producing eukaryotic proteins while preserving their native structure and post-translational modifications. Leishmaniasis, a sand fly–borne disease with diverse clinical forms, remains a significant health concern. Sand fly salivary proteins such as PpSP15 and PsSP9 have been identified as promising protective vaccine candidates. However, the common use of antibiotic resistance genes as selection markers in recombinant strains raises safety concerns for human applications. In this study, an antibiotic marker–free system was developed by removing the neomycin resistance gene (Neor) from the pLEXSY-Neorvector to construct pLEXSY-noNeor. The PpSP15-T2A-PsSP9 fragment was cloned into this modified vector, and CRISPR-Cas9 technology was used to integrate the genes into the SSU locus ofL. tarentolae. Successful gene insertion and expression were confirmed at DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Importantly, mutant parasites showed infectivity comparable to wild-type strains. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of generating antibiotic resistance–free transgenicL. tarentolae, supporting its potential as a safe live vaccine platform.

Article.Title: Stability-aware social welfare optimization for renewable power dispatch with virtual synchronous generators
Article.Authors: Maity S.; Shrivastav A.; Chanda S.; Kumar P.; Dutta S.; De A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIn the last few decades, there has been a considerable increase in the implementation of renewable generation technologies within power systems, owing to the fact that there is a need to provide sustainable and environment- friendly options for generating electricity, as opposed to the traditional modes. However, the unpredictable nature of the renewable generation makes it necessary to implement proper demand management techniques. Demand response-based rescheduling algorithms such as Social Welfare Maximisation are thus gaining attention for mitigating this problem in the dispatch planning stage of power system. However, for very short or real time equilibrium system has to rely on inherent inertia. Conventional thermal power plants generate considerable rotational inertia using synchronous machines; therefore, they can deal with real-time disturbances because of load fluctuations, generation variations, and faults in the electrical system. To address these challenges of rich Renewable power systems, the Virtual Synchronous Generator’s theories has proven to be a potential solution. The virtual inertia and damping parameters are software-defined, but constrained by converter power ratings and control loop bandwidth. Also, excessively high virtual inertia settings can cause slow dynamic response or instability under fast disturbances. This paper revisits the VSG approach and intended to extend the range of controllability of VSGs by additional closed loop control circuit, enhancing the inherent software inertia adaptively, and thereby improving transient stability of VSG augmented renewable systems. Further, the renewable model thus developed with VSG was used in a benchmark IEEE 30 bus system with demand response based Social Welfare allied optimisation algorithm which demonstrated improvement of the values of Critical Clearing Time during worst possible contingencies and electrical faults of the system. The DEQPSO algorithm, based on the combination of the Differential Evolution (DE) algorithm and the Quantum Particle Swarm Optimisation (QPSO) algorithm, is ideal for solving the nonlinear optimization problem investigated in this research, where not only static operating constraints but also transient stability constraints are involved. In this respect, the current research aims to incorporate renewable energy sources with the VSG controller in the power system in order to improve its transient stability and reliability.

Article.Title: Controlled water immersion as a post-harvest strategy for the valorization of underripe Coffea arabica L. fruits
Article.Authors: de Souza G.; Zagato N.; Júlio A.; dos Santos M.; dos W.; Gomes S.; Moreli A.; Menini L.; Pereira L.
Article.Abstract: No preview available

Article.Title: Solar-driven MOF-derived Co–N–C@TiO₂ direct Z-scheme heterostructure for efficient antibiotic degradation via enhanced interfacial charge transfer
Article.Authors: El-Sawaf A.; Nassar A.; Mohamed M.; Ali A.; Mubarak M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe development of efficient and sustainable photocatalysts for solar-driven environmental remediation remains an important challenge in the elimination of emerging water contaminants. In this study, a MOF-derived Co–N–C@TiO₂ direct Z-scheme heterostructure was rationally engineered to enhance visible-light utilization and interfacial charge transfer for tetracycline degradation. The composite was synthesized through pyrolysis of a cobalt-based zeolitic imidazolate framework to produce a conductive Co–N–C scaffold, followed by sol–gel deposition of TiO₂ nanoparticles. Structural and physicochemical characterizations (XRD, FTIR, BET, SEM/TEM, XPS, UV–Vis DRS, PL, and Mott–Schottky analyses) confirmed the formation of a porous architecture with a high specific surface area (176.4 m² g⁻¹), uniformly dispersed TiO₂ nanodomains, enhanced visible-light absorption, and efficient suppression of electron–hole recombination. Under visible-light irradiation, the Co–N–C@TiO₂ photocatalyst achieved 93.7 ± 0.8% tetracycline degradation within 60 min, accompanied by a pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.054 ± 0.001 min⁻¹ and 67.5 ± 2.3% total organic carbon removal, indicating substantial mineralization. The superior photocatalytic performance is attributed to the synergistic interaction between the conductive MOF-derived carbon framework, Co–Nₓ active sites, and the direct Z-scheme heterojunction, which facilitates rapid charge separation while preserving strong redox capability. By efficiently utilizing solar energy for advanced water treatment, this work provides a sustainable photocatalytic strategy that contributes to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).

Article.Title: Source apportionment and health risk assessment of PAHs in commercial fish from Al Jubail, Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alluhayb A.; Algreiby A.; Younis A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study measured polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) contamination in ten commercially important fish species from the Al-Jubail industrial coastline, Arabian Gulf, Saudi Arabia. Muscle tissue concentrations were quantified by GC-MS. Source apportionment used diagnostic molecular ratios, positive matrix factorization (PMF), and hierarchical clustering, and health risk was assessed separately for adults and children. Total Σ16PAH concentrations ranged from 481.99 to 758.82 ng/g wet weight, withScomberomorus commersoncarrying the highest burden. Pelagic species accumulated consistently more PAHs than demersal fish, suggesting atmospheric deposition and surface microlayer enrichment are the dominant exposure routes here. Low-molecular-weight compounds made up 55.16% of the total profile. PMF modeling traced most of the contamination to pyrogenic combustion (53–67%), with petrogenic inputs making up the rest (28–42%). Cluster analysis grouped the species by trophic level, matching the bioaccumulation patterns already observed. Benzo[a]pyrene concentrations exceeded EU regulatory limits for thermally processed seafood. The non-carcinogenic hazard index came in above the acceptable threshold for adults (2.07–3.18) and, more sharply, for children (4.52–6.95). Incremental lifetime cancer risk for benzo[a]pyrene ranged from 7.73 × 10⁻⁵ to 1.52 × 10⁻⁴ with values exceeding the 10⁻⁴ acceptable threshold for several species, indicating a potential carcinogenic concern that warrants proactive management consideration. Taken together, this points to meaningful dietary exposure risk in this population, particularly for children, and supports calls for stricter industrial emission controls and routine seafood monitoring along heavily industrialized coasts.

Article.Title: Influence of seed sources and seeding rates on bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) productivity in Banja District, Northwestern Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Aleminew A.; Achenef E.; Azmeraw Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractBread wheat productivity in Northwestern Ethiopia is extremely low due to poor-quality seeds and inappropriate seed rates. To address these problems, field and laboratory experiments were conducted during the 2024 cropping season in Banja District to evaluate the effects of seed sources and rates. Seed quality was evaluated in the laboratory using a Completely Randomized Design with three replications. The field experiment employed a factorial randomized complete block design with three replications, including four seed rates (125, 150, 175, and 200 kg ha⁻¹) and three seed sources: Adet Research Center, Ediget Bandnet Cooperative, and farmer-saved seeds of theDanda’avariety. Laboratory results indicated that seed sources significantly influenced by initial seed quality of bread wheat. Seeds from Adet Research Center showed the highest physical purity (99.97%), standard germination (98.33%), thousand kernel weights (41.20 g), seedling vigor index I (27.18), and seedling vigor index II (0.02). In the field experiment, grain yield was highly significantly affected by both seed sources and rates. The highest grain yield of 5.39 t ha⁻¹ was achieved with Adet Research Center seeds, while 200 kg ha⁻¹ seed rate produced 5.37 t ha⁻¹. The combination of Adet Research Center seed with 200 kg ha⁻¹ contributed the maximum net benefit of 103,480.30 Ethiopian Birr ha⁻¹ and a marginal rate of return of 582.9%. These results suggest that using 200 kg ha⁻¹ ofDanda’avariety seeds from Adet Research Center can substantially improve wheat productivity. Further verification across multiple varieties, locations, and years is recommended to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Occupational stress and associated factors among industrial workers across industries in Markazi Province Iran
Article.Authors: Zokaei M.; Falahati M.; Parvari A.; Karsidani S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractOccupational stress is an important psychosocial hazard influencing the physical and mental health of employees. This study assessed the levels and determinants of occupational stress among industrial workers in Markazi Province, Iran one of the country’s major industrial regions. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in 2023–2024 among 1,102 employees from four sectors: metal, construction, chemical, and food–pharmaceutical industries. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering demographic, occupational, socioeconomic, and lifestyle variables, along with the validated HSE Occupational Stress Indicator Tool (35 items, seven subscales). Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS v26 and R version 4.5.0, including descriptive tests, ANOVA, and multiple regression analysis (p< 0.05). The final analysis included 1,102 participants (mean age 39 ± 7.5 years; 73% male). The mean total HSE score was 120.19 ± 14.11, with significant differences observed across industrial sectors (p= 0.022). Several HSE dimensions also differed significantly between industries, particularly role, communication, control, and demand. Significant differences were observed across sectors (p< 0.001), with chemical and construction workers reporting higher demands and lower control compared to the metal and food sectors. The multiple regression model explained 11.6% of the variance in stress scores (R2= 0.116). Income satisfaction was negatively associated with HSE scores (B = − 0.186,p< 0.001), inadequate job control (B = 0.225,p< 0.001). Occupational stress was generally low but varied across industries. Findings indicate that stress is shaped mainly by organizational and economic factors such as workload, job control, and fairness of rewards rather than individual characteristics. Strengthening participation, welfare, and supportive supervision, alongside periodic stress monitoring and mental health programs, can effectively enhance resilience and productivity among industrial workers.

Article.Title: HQDeTransformer: hybrid quantum denoising Transformer for time series forecasting
