Article.Title: Advanced machine learning framework for hole quality prediction and optimization in polycarbonate AWJD
Article.Authors: Bharani Chandar J.; Rathinasuriyan C.; Lenin N.; Sivakumar M.; Singh R.; Salunkhe S.; GaneshKumar P.; Palanisamy R.; Nasr E.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAbrasive waterjet drilling of polymers is difficult to optimize owing to nonlinear interactions and conflicting performance requirements. This study suggests combining experimental, ML models, multi-objective optimization, and statistical validation to improve polycarbonate drilling performance. A full factorial design was used to vary water pressure (250–350 MPa), standoff distance (1.5–2.5 mm), and traversal rate (300–500 mm/min) in 125 tests. DE and drilling rate were performance responses. Analysis of variance showed water pressure and standoff distance were the principal variables affecting the hole diameter error (DE) and drilling rate (DR). Four machine learning models, namely XGBoost, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and AdaBoost Regressor were built in the Anaconda-based Python environment. The Random Forest model demonstrated high reliability in capturing complex process behavior, with R² = 0.92263 for DE and 0.90471 for DR. Random Forest was utilized as a stand-in paradigm for multi-objective optimization using the Grey Wolf optimizer, Whale optimization algorithm, and Arithmetic optimization algorithm. With Whale optimization method, Water pressure = 350 MPa, Standoff distance = 2.5 mm, and Traverse rate = 300 mm/min produced the highest performance with decreased DE (0.1238) and improved DR (2.0450). The Friedman test (p< 0.001) and post-hoc analysis show that Whale optimization method outperforms Grey Wolf and Arithmetic optimization algorithms. The results of confirmation tests with the optimized parameters for the WOA showed good agreement with the predicted results, within a range of ± 3%.

Article.Title: Novel intercalation of MnPS3 with polypyrrole and effect on magnetic and optical properties

Article.Title: Large-scale marine eDNA database reveals seasonal latitudinal diversity gradients in Japan driven by vagrant fish
Article.Authors: Kasada M.; Shinohara N.; Tanaka K.; Fukasawa R.; Tanabe A.; Yamakawa H.; Abe H.; Abe M.; Araki H.; Enoki T.; Fukuoka M.; Fukuzawa K.; Goto R.; Hamaguchi M.; Hamaoka H.; Hasegawa N.; Henmi Y.; Hori M.; Igari T.; Ishii M.; Ito A.; Kadota T.; Kajita T.; Kasai A.; Kishida O.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe spatial and temporal patterns of marine diversity are essential for the sustainable use and management of marine ecosystems. Here, we investigated latitudinal and seasonal diversity gradients of fish genera in Japanese waters using environmental DNA (eDNA) data from 1,765 surveys conducted between 2017 to 2022. We found a negative relationship between genus richness and latitude, consistent with latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG). Importantly, the strength of the gradient varied seasonally, with steeper slopes observed during warm seasons compared to winter. This seasonal restructuring of LDGs may reflect the increased occurrence of tropical vagrant fish, rather than the commonly assumed pattern of seasonal migration. These transient taxa may temporarily elevate observed richness at higher latitudes but do not persist through winter conditions. As a result, short-term increases in biodiversity under warming conditions may not necessarily indicate stable ecological change. Our findings highlight that eDNA-based richness metrics can capture both persistent community structure and transient ecological processes, underscoring the need for careful interpretation of biodiversity patterns in a changing climate.

Article.Title: Spatial estimation of standardized precipitation index based drought severity across Türkiye using machine learning models
Article.Authors: Atasever U.; Taşkanat T.; Erol A.; Köylü Ü.; Citakoglu H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractReliable spatial estimation of extreme drought intensity represented by the minimum SPI value is essential for water resources management under increasing climate variability. However, conventional assessments often rely on station-based temporal indices, providing limited representation of spatial heterogeneity and topographic controls. This study developed a machine learning framework to estimate the spatial distribution of extreme drought intensity represented by the minimum SPI value across Türkiye using long-term precipitation records from 102 meteorological stations. For each station and SPI accumulation period, extreme drought intensity was represented by the minimum (most negative) SPI value observed over the 1935–2024 record; this minimum SPI value was used as the machine-learning target, while latitude, longitude, and elevation were used as geographic predictors. Seven machine learning models were evaluated; among them, GBM yielded the highest accuracy (R2= 0.991, RMSE = 0.007), followed by XGBoost and CatBoost. These results indicate that ensemble tree-based methods reproduce the observed spatial pattern of extreme drought intensity across the station network with high accuracy; establishing predictive skill at unmonitored locations would require evaluation under a station-grouped partition. Furthermore, feature importance and SHAP analyses showed that spatial predictors (longitude, latitude, and elevation) were substantially more influential than the time-scale variable, although their relative importance varied among the evaluated models. This framework offers a robust tool for interpretable and spatially explicit drought monitoring in topographically complex regions.

Article.Title: Synthesis, characterization, biological evaluation, and computational studies of novel metal complexes derived from 1-isopropyl-1H-benzimidazole-2-carbaldehyde and tri-substituted imidazole
Article.Authors: Almohyawi A.; Abdou A.; Al-Rooqi M.; Samman S.; Alsimaree A.; Alkubaysi S.; Moussa Z.; Timoumi A.; Jassas R.; Ahmed S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTwo novel Ni(II) and Cu(II) mixed-ligand complexes, NiMBIM and CuMBIM, were successfully synthesized using 1-isopropyl-1H-benzimidazole-2-carbaldehyde (MB) and 2-(4,5-diphenyl-1H-imidazol-2-yl)phenol (IM). Their structures were characterized via CHN elemental analysis, UV–Vis and FT-IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, molar conductivity, magnetic susceptibility, and thermal analysis. NiMBIM adopts a tetrahedral geometry, while CuMBIM forms a distorted octahedral structure with coordinated chloride and water. Conductivity measurements indicated that NiMBIM behaves as a 1:1 electrolyte in ethanol (43.15 μS cm2mol−1), whereas CuMBIM is non-electrolytic (9.06 μS cm2ol−1). Thermogravimetric analysis confirmed the presence of one coordinated water molecule in CuMBIM and none in NiMBIM. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations revealed that CuMBIM possesses the smallest HOMO–LUMO gap (1.61 eV), highest softness (σ = 0.62), and electrophilicity (ω = 9.58), indicating superior reactivity. TD-DFT simulations of the electronic spectra showed good agreement with experimental UV–Vis data, supporting the proposed structures and transition assignments. Biological evaluations demonstrated promising in vitro antimicrobial activity for both complexes, with CuMBIM exhibiting the highest inhibition againstKlebsiella pneumoniae(26.00 ± 0.14 mm) andCandida albicans(24.30 ± 0.15 mm). Anti-inflammatory assays confirmed effective inhibition, with IC50 values of 30.25 µg/µL for CuMBIM and 32.88 µg/µL for NiMBIM. Molecular docking studies targeting FabH-CoA (PDB: 1HNJ) and COX-2 (PDB: 1CX2) corroborated these results, showing CuMBIM achieves the strongest binding affinities (− 8.80 and − 10.90 kcal/mol) through key hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions, consistent with its enhanced in vitro biological activity.

Article.Title: Experimental context determines repeated UVB responses and photoageing-associated phenotypes in human dermal fibroblasts
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Ye H.; Jia H.; Ren S.; Cui Z.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRepeated ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure of dermal fibroblasts is widely used to investigate photoaging-associated cellular stress responses; however, substantial variation in experimental design limits reproducibility and complicates comparison across studies. Here, We systematically evaluated how experimental context—including seeding density, cumulative UVB dose, irradiation schedule and experimental time—collectively shapes repeated UVB responses in human dermal fibroblasts. Full-factorial analysis demonstrated that cumulative UVB dose and experimental time accounted for the largest proportion of biological variation, while Dose × Day, Dose × Schedule, and Dose × Density interactions were also substantial. Experimental observations confirmed that identical cumulative UVB doses produced distinct proliferative outcomes depending on irradiation schedule, culture density and recovery time. Experimental validation showed that initial cell density reshaped the apparent dose-response relationship, with low-density cultures exhibiting greater UVB sensitivity but reduced experimental stability, whereas intermediate-density cultures revealed distinct low- and high-response states. Furthermore, equivalent cumulative UVB doses delivered under different irradiation schedules produced distinct proliferative responses, demonstrating that recovery interval modifies cumulative UVB responses independently of total dose. A representative repeated-UVB condition reproduced canonical photoaging-associated phenotypes, including recurrent oxidative stress, impaired migration, extracellular matrix remodeling, and activation of stress- and senescence-associated transcriptional programs. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that repeated UVB responses are determined not only by cumulative UVB dose but also by experimental context. Considering seeding density, experimental time, and recovery dynamics alongside UVB dose provides a practical framework for improving the reproducibility, interpretation, and comparison of fibroblast-based photoaging models.

Article.Title: Deep binarized photonic reservoir computing for ultrafast multimedia signal processing
Article.Authors: Iqbal M.; Alassir M.; Marsal N.; Rontani D.
Article.Abstract: AbstractWe present a deep photonic neural network architecture based on ultrafast binary optical modulation using a digital micromirror device (DMD), optical scattering in a random medium, high-speed photodetection with a CMOS sensor, and a time-multiplexed multilayer structure. Operating at Gigabit-per-second (Gb/s) optical information throughput, our system based on the reservoir computing (RC) framework achieves state-of-the-art performance across various multimedia tasks, including video, image and speech recognition. We show that the careful optimization of key physical intra- and inter-layer hyperparameters can significantly enhance the deep photonic RC system’s ability to extract relevant temporal and spatial features by balancing memory retention and dynamical response of individual layers. This approach paves the way for highly scalable hierarchical photonic reservoir computing systems for high-throughput real-time multimedia signal processing.

Article.Title: A memory-adaptive Karma–Dharma optimizer for global optimization and VLSI design
Article.Authors: Moodi H.; Razavi S.; Hajiaghaei-Keshteli M.; Hadavandi E.
Article.Abstract: AbstractWhile many recent metaheuristics rely on elaborate biological or physical metaphors, their underlying mathematical mechanics often remain obscured. This paper introduces the Karma–Dharma Optimizer (KDO), a transparent, memory-adaptive metaheuristic designed for continuous and constrained engineering optimization. KDO couples two complementary phases: a memory-guided exploration phase that utilizes a historical success archive (the Dharma operator) and a structured exploitation phase (the Karma operator). An adaptive stagnation-recovery mechanism, termed Nirvana Reset, is further incorporated to help the search escape locally stagnant regions. The global search capability and dimensional scalability of KDO are extensively evaluated on the CEC-2017 and CEC-2022 benchmark suites across dimensions up to$$D=50$$. Furthermore, KDO is applied to four constrained analog, RF, and VLSI circuit design problems: a two-stage Miller operational amplifier, an RF CMOS cascode LNA, a low phase-noise LC-VCO, and a 6T FinFET SRAM cell. These circuits are evaluated under both closed-form analytical surrogates and an automated, physics-driven MATLAB–ngspice-in-the-loop simulation framework accounting for process–voltage–temperature (PVT) variations and Monte Carlo yield constraints. Non-parametric statistical analyses alongside component-wise ablation studies, reveal aproblem-dependent performance profilefor KDO. It achieves the best overall rank on the constrained VLSI design problems under both analytical and physics-based evaluations, while remaining competitive against strong mathematical optimizers (DE, GBO) on the standardized CEC benchmarks.

Article.Title: P2Y receptor-mediated regulation of lipolysis, lipid droplet dynamics, and energy metabolism in podocytes
Article.Authors: Szrejder M.; Audzeyenka I.; Rachubik P.; Grochowalska K.; Rogacka D.; Narajczyk M.; Piwkowska A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAbnormal lipid metabolism that results in excessive lipid accumulation in the kidney is closely associated with the pathogenesis of glomerulopathies. Podocytes cover the external surface of glomerular capillaries and are known to be particularly sensitive to lipid overload. Lipids accumulate in lipid droplets, specialized organelles that store neutral lipids. Lipid droplets regulate the mobilization of free fatty acids (FFAs) through lipolysis, coordinated by complex machinery, including adipose triglyceride lipase and perilipins. Moreover, activation of the lipolytic cascade leads to the release of stored energy in the form of FFAs, which serve as substrates for subsequent mitochondrial oxidation. Because cyclic adenosine monophosphate, a key second messenger downstream of purinergic P2Y receptors, governs lipolysis, we investigated whether P2Y signaling modulates podocyte lipid metabolism and bioenergetics. Primary rat podocytes were stimulated with uridine-5’-triphosphate and selective P2Y₁ and P2Y₄ receptor agonists. P2Y activation suppressed lipolysis, reflected by alterations of lipolytic protein levels, lower FFA levels, and changes in lipid droplet morphology and distribution. Lower FFA availability was accompanied by a decrease in oxidative phosphorylation and a compensatory increase in glycolysis. Altogether, these findings highlight a significant role for P2Y signaling in overall podocyte metabolism through the regulation of lipid metabolism. Targeting purinergic signaling to control lipolysis may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate lipid-driven podocyte injury and glomerular dysfunction.

Article.Title: National trends, incidence and regional variations in lower extremity amputations in Sweden, 2008–2024: a register-based study
Article.Authors: Swärd N.; Nilsson G.; Axenhus M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLower extremity amputation (LEA) trends are changing worldwide. This population-based study aimed to describe the incidence, temporal trends, demographic distribution, and regional variation of LEA in Sweden from 2008 to 2024. Data were obtained from the Swedish National Patient Register, and individuals undergoing LEA from toe to hip-level were identified using NOMESCO procedure codes. Incidence were calculated per 100,000 inhabitants/year and analyzed by sex, age, and geographic region. A total of 53,005 patients underwent LEA during the study period, corresponding to an overall incidence of 37.9 per 100,000 person-years. Men had significantly higher incidence than women (p< 0.001). Incidence declined over time, with an estimated future decrease of 0.5% per year in men and 1.9% per year in women. The reduction was mainly driven by decreasing incidence of transtibial amputations and knee disarticulations. Incidence was highest among older individuals and varied geographically, with higher incidence observed in rural regions compared with urban areas. In conclusion, the incidence of LEA in Sweden decreased during the study period, although substantial differences by sex, age, and region persist. Understanding these patterns may help guide preventive strategies and improve equity in healthcare access.

Article.Title: Application of a PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents
Article.Authors: Feng S.; Zhong B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTeaching film-reading is the most basic clinical teaching activity in the standardized residency training of laboratory medicine department. How to integrate theoretical knowledge with clinical cases and imaging data in a resident-centered manner remains a challenge. Problem-based learning (PBL) is a student-centered teaching method that fosters critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Considering that artificial intelligence technology has a wide range of application prospects in the field of medical education, we introduced a combined pedagogical package of PBL and ChatGPT in teaching film-reading. The aim of the study was to measure the effectiveness of the PBL-ChatGPT combined package in teaching film-reading for laboratory medicine residents in comparison with traditional teaching. Residents were randomly assigned to receive either the PBL-ChatGPT combined package (hereafter referred to as the PBL-ChatGPT group) or traditional teaching (traditional group). After each course, the members of each group were required to complete in-class quizzes and a standardized film-reading assessment form for residency training. Residents’ acceptance and satisfaction with the combined package were evaluated through a survey. Both the theoretical and film-reading examination scores were significantly higher in the PBL-ChatGPT group than in the traditional group (bothP< 0.001), with large effect sizes (rank-biserial correlation 0.72 and 0.65, respectively). On the standardized film-reading assessment form, the PBL-ChatGPT group scored significantly higher in the preparation, methodology and overall evaluation domains (allP< 0.001, below the Bonferroni-corrected threshold of 0.0125 applied across the four pre-specified domains) and in the total score (P< 0.001), whereas no significant difference was detected in the process domain (P= 0.121). Residents’ feedback on the combined package was highly positive. The study indicates that the PBL-ChatGPT combined package holds significant potential as an innovative model for teaching film-reading to laboratory medicine residents.

Article.Title: Attitudes toward patient safety culture among respiratory therapy students: an online cross-sectional study in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Aldhahir A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPatient safety culture is a fundamental component of healthcare quality; however, limited evidence exists regarding safety attitudes among respiratory therapy (RT) students. This study aimed to assess the attitudes toward patient safety and identify factors associated with positive safety attitudes among RT students in Saudi Arabia. An online survey using the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire (SAQ) was conducted between August 28 and December 27, 2025. RT students from the second academic year through internship year were recruited using convenience sampling through social media channels. A mean SAQ score of ≥ 75 defined a positive safety attitude. Non-parametric tests were used to compare SAQ scores and multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with positive safety attitudes. A total of 1,457 RT students from 18 programs across Saudi Arabia participated in the study, with a mean age of 23 ± 2 years; 68.4% were male. Overall, only 26.9% of RT students demonstrated a positive safety attitude. Male gender (aOR = 1.4, 95% CI: 1.03–1.81) and increasing age (aOR = 1.1, 95% CI: 1.06–1.21) were independently associated with higher odds of positive safety perception. Internship RT students were significantly more likely to report positive safety attitudes compared with second-year RT students (aOR = 3.0, 95% CI: 1.10–7.98). Significant regional disparities were observed, with RT students from the Southern, Northern, and Central regions demonstrating higher odds of positive safety perception compared with those from the Eastern region. Higher cumulative GPA was also strongly associated with positive safety attitudes, particularly among RT students with GPAs ≥ 4.00. Safety attitudes among RT students in Saudi Arabia remain suboptimal, highlighting the need to strengthen patient safety education during professional training.

Article.Title: Cumulative-incidence crossover and conditional mortality after definitive surgery for endometrial cancer: a population-based competing-risk analysis
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Guo C.; Tong F.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLong-term survivors of endometrial cancer face competing risks from cancer and other conditions, but how these risks evolve remains uncertain. We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study of 255,104 women who underwent hysterectomy-based definitive surgery for endometrial cancer in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program (2000–2021). Cause-specific cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen–Johansen methods. Crossover was the earliest month when composite non-endometrial mortality (cardiovascular, other malignant cancer, or other non-cancer death) exceeded endometrial cancer-specific mortality and remained higher for 12 months. During a median follow-up of 8.2 years, 62,347 deaths occurred. Endometrial cancer mortality was 6.2%, 7.1%, and 7.4% at 5, 10, and 15 years, compared with 5.3%, 16.6%, and 28.3% for composite non-endometrial mortality. Crossover occurred at 5.6 years (95% confidence interval, 5.4–5.8) overall but was not reached within 15 years for stage III/IV disease or chemotherapy recipients. Among 10-year survivors, subsequent 5-year mortality was 0.4% from endometrial cancer and 15.3% from non-endometrial causes; cardiovascular mortality remained elevated relative to U.S. female rates (standardized mortality ratio, 1.21; 95% confidence interval, 1.16–1.26). These findings support integrated cardiovascular and metabolic risk management from diagnosis alongside individualized, guideline-concordant oncologic surveillance.

Article.Title: Adiposity and insulin resistance indices and progression to advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome in Chinese adults
Article.Authors: Jiang Z.; Zhang J.; Zhang X.; Jin L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMetabolic and adiposity-related indices may help identify individuals at increased risk of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) progression; however, comparative prospective evidence remains limited. We examined the associations of seven metabolic and adiposity-related indices with progression to advanced CKM stages and assessed their incremental discrimination and exploratory internal machine-learning performance. This prospective analysis included 2,871 participants from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study with CKM stages 0–2 at baseline in 2011. CKM progression was defined as progression to stages 3–4 at the 2015 follow-up. Associations of the triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), lipid accumulation product (LAP), visceral adiposity index (VAI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and body roundness index (BRI) with CKM progression were examined using multivariable Cox regression after multiple imputation. Dose–response, subgroup, sensitivity, and incremental discrimination analyses were performed. Separate LAP-, TyG-WC-, and TyG-WHtR-based machine-learning frameworks were evaluated using a stratified 70:30 training/test split. During follow-up, 595 participants (20.7%) progressed to CKM stages 3–4. In fully adjusted analyses, the highest versus lowest quartile of each index was associated with a higher risk of CKM progression, with HRs ranging from 1.52 for TyG (95% CI, 1.20–1.94) to 2.03 for TyG-WC (95% CI, 1.60–2.57; allPfor trend < 0.001). Corresponding HRs were 2.01 (95% CI, 1.57–2.57) for TyG-WHtR and 1.98 (95% CI, 1.55–2.54) for LAP. Six indices showed nonlinear dose–response associations. Subgroup analyses showed significant interactions by sex for TyG-WHtR, LAP, WHtR, BRI, and VAI; by smoking status for TyG-WHtR, LAP, and VAI; and by age for WHtR (allPfor interaction ≤ 0.049). Addition of individual indices to the covariate model yielded C-indices of 0.702–0.715, compared with 0.701 for the basic model; TyG-WC achieved the highest C-index. In the held-out internal test set, logistic regression achieved the highest ROC-AUC in the LAP (0.721), TyG-WC (0.729), and TyG-WHtR (0.726) frameworks. SHAP analyses of the corresponding logistic regression models identified age as the predictor with the largest mean absolute contribution across all three frameworks. Elevated levels of all seven indices were associated with CKM progression, particularly TyG-WC, TyG-WHtR, and LAP. Given the structural overlap between several index components and the CKM staging framework, the incremental discrimination and machine-learning findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation.

Article.Title: Material recognition from cross-category morphing
Article.Authors: Liao C.; Schmidt F.; Cheeseman J.; Sawayama M.; Fleming R.; Xiao B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMaterials from distinct categories share common image features but also exhibit unique characteristics. How do humans recognize materials despite their enormous appearance variations? Using generative neural networks, we create both prototypical and ambiguous materials that morph between categories. To capture the richness of material representation, we characterize how people judge materials using cross-material morphs through three behavioral tasks: material categorization, material property rating, and visual similarity judgment. We find that morphing smoothly modulates perceptual scales of material appearance. Despite this smooth variation, participants can reliably identify the prototypical materials within given appearance ranges, indicating a strong association between material categories and their visual characteristics. Material properties structure the perceptual space, where the salient dimensions–particularly rigidity–strongly correlate with perceived material categories. In contrast, analyzing image embedding derived from a self-supervised deep learning model reveals that learning visual similarities alone is insufficient to reproduce human perceptual space of materials. Together, our results suggest that material representation is more than visual similarities and may require learning material properties that structure relationships among materials within and across categories. Visual features might be used flexibly and task-dependently to support multiple levels of material perception, ranging from discrimination to material property inference to categorization.

Article.Title: Population driven emissions call for earlier climate mitigation
Article.Authors: Liuzzi D.; Lupi V.; Marsiglio S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractEconometric studies based on the STIRPAT framework suggest that carbon emissions respond more strongly to population size than to per capita income, yet this relationship has not been explicitly incorporated into the integrated assessment models used for climate policy analysis. We extend one of the most widely known framework, namely the DICE model, to allow population to directly determine emissions beyond its indirect effect through economic activity, calibrating the relevant elasticities on existing empirical estimates. We find that unabated emissions may exceed twice the standard DICE baseline by 2100, requiring substantially earlier and more intensive abatement effort. Full decarbonization appears necessary around mid-century to meet the 2$$^{circ}$$C temperature target, and socially optimal by 2070 when mitigation costs and benefits are weighed against each other. These results are primarily driven by a population elasticity above unity which amplifies emissions, combined with a sub-unitary response to per capita income which partly offsets this effect. Our analysis suggests that explicitly accounting for non-proportional effects of population and income on emissions can significantly affect conclusions about the urgency and cost of climate action.

Article.Title: Physicochemical properties, selective cytotoxicity, and hemocompatibility of silver nanoparticles biosynthesized using Schizophyllum commune extract
Article.Authors: Sukdee S.; Prajuabjinda O.; Thepsilvisut O.; Chutimanukul P.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe integration of biologically derived surface functionalities into metallic nanomaterials offers a promising approach for tailoring nanoparticle performance. In this study, structure–property-bioactivity relationships of biofunctionalized silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized usingSchizophyllum communeextract were investigated. The fungal extract contained abundant phenolics, triterpenoids, proteins, and carbohydrates that mediated nanoparticle formation and surface functionalization. The resulting AgNPs exhibited a face-centered cubic crystalline structure, an average hydrodynamic size of approximately 50 nm, a zeta potential of − 20.2 mV, and stable colloidal behavior. FTIR analysis revealed the persistence of hydroxyl, amide, and carbohydrate-associated functional groups on the nanoparticle surface, supporting the presence of a fungal-derived biomolecular surface layer rather than confirming the formation of a complete biomolecular corona. These surface characteristics were closely associated with enhanced biological performance, including strong antioxidant activity and selective cytotoxicity against cancer cells. The AgNPs demonstrated potent anticancer activity with IC50values of 5.07, 27.93, and 29.07 µg/mL against HepG2, SW480, and NCI-N87 cells, respectively, corresponding to selectivity index (SI) values of 44.18, 8.02, and 7.71. Furthermore, hemolytic activity remained below 5%, indicating acceptable hemocompatibility. Overall, the findings establish a direct relationship between fungal-derived surface chemistry, nanoparticle physicochemical properties, and biological performance, highlighting the potential ofS. commune-mediated biofunctionalized AgNPs as advanced nanotherapeutic materials with promising anticancer and biocompatible characteristics.

Article.Title: Cross-configuration data-driven modeling of separation efficiency and diluate production flux in Persian Gulf seawater electrodialysis
Article.Authors: Sharafi S.; Sharafi M.; Sharasfi A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study compared four data-driven approaches, GMDH-GA, ANFIS-PSO, support vector machine (SVM), and pattern mining engine (PME), for predicting separation efficiency and diluate production flux in laboratory-scale electrodialysis treatment of Persian Gulf seawater. A complete 486-run factorial dataset covering volumetric flow rate, solute concentration, temperature, applied voltage, and pressure was evaluated using 31 predictor configurations and a common 340/146 development/test partition. Factorial decomposition identified volumetric flow rate as the dominant source of response variation, accounting for 73.90% of the corrected variation in separation efficiency and 59.65% in diluate production flux, while interaction terms contributed 10.44% and 23.67%, respectively. Under the primary held-out evaluation, PME achieved the lowest median test RMSE across the 31 predictor structures for both separation efficiency (0.5774 percentage points) and diluate production flux (0.0934 l m-2h-1), producing the lowest RMSE in 17 and 23 configurations, respectively. Repeated-resampling analysis revealed a metric-dependent pattern for separation efficiency, with GMDH-GA achieving the lowest mean RMSE while PME showed the highest mean Pearson correlation. In contrast, PME retained the lowest mean RMSE, highest predictive R2, and highest correlation for diluate production flux across repeated evaluation resamples and remained comparatively stable across temperature and concentration regimes. These results demonstrate that model performance depends on predictor composition, response variable, evaluation metric, and operating regime, with the most persistent predictive advantage of PME observed for diluate production flux.

Article.Title: Application of eDNA metabarcoding for high-resolution reconstruction of the trophic web of an Arctic fjord
Article.Authors: Piroli C.; Marinchel N.; Galli S.; Russo T.; Azzaro M.; Filiciotto F.; Di Marco G.; D’Agostino A.; Gismondi A.; Profeta A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIn a rapidly changing Arctic, the Kongsfjorden marine ecosystem was investigated to explore its community composition and structural dynamics using environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding. Samples were collected withmetaprobes, passive eDNA samplers deployed within fish traps in the coastal zone and towed along a transect in the mid-fjord zone. Mitochondrial COI and ribosomal 18 S SSU (V8-V9 region) genes were amplified to characterize metazoan and protist communities, respectively. Community analysis highlighted significant differences between coastal and mid-fjord sites (ANOSIM,R= 0.7,p< 0.05), identifying 23 taxa as indicators of one of the two zones. Taxa identified through metabarcoding were used as nodes in trophic networks, while feeding relationships (producer–consumer and predator–prey) were reconstructed through literature review. Qualitative food webs were obtained for each sampling site and for the coastal and mid-fjord zones. The networks were characterized using key trophic indicators and differences emerged in the apical part of the webs. Overall, eDNA proved to be a sensitive and effective tool for detecting spatial differences in community structure. This approach also shows strong potential for long-term monitoring, offering a rapid, cost-effective, and scalable alternative to traditional methods.

Article.Title: Sexual dimorphism and hemispheric asymmetry in the morphology of the sylvian fissure: a magnetic resonance imaging based study
Article.Authors: Phuyal N.; Pandey N.; B.C. B.; Pandeya A.; Mishra A.; Khanal B.; Shrestha A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Sylvian Fissure, the first sulcus to appear during the embryological period, is considered a conventional passageway by neurosurgeons for surgeries related to insular and temporal horn tumours and aneurysm clipping. This study aimed to report the morphological types of the sylvian fissure, explore their distribution patterns among sexes and age groups, and assess the symmetry of morphology between the right and left cerebral hemispheres. A prospective cross-sectional study was performed with 520 participants who visited the Department of Radiology for brain MRI. The participants were recruited after ethical approval was obtained from the Institutional Review Committee and after written informed consent was obtained from participants. MRI scans were assessed during the reporting of the MRI, and the categorization was performed by a senior radiologist. Statistical methods such as Pearson’s chi-square test, Bowker’s test, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient were used to assess the association and symmetry of the Sylvian fissure morphology. The type II Sylvian fissure was found to be the most prevalent among both males and females and in both right and left hemispheres. It was also the most common in all age groups except for the > 50 years group, where type I was the most common. The assessment of symmetry reported κ = 0.879 (SE = 0.021,p< 0.001), indicating concordance between the right and left hemispheres. Multinomial regression analysis revealed that older participants and females were associated with lower odds of having SF of types I and III in both hemispheres. Younger participants were more likely to have a narrow Sylvian fissure, whereas wider types were more prevalent in older patients. Future studies should focus on exploring the associations between surgical outcomes and Sylvian fissure morphology.

Article.Title: Inclisiran ameliorates diabetes-associated skeletal muscle remodeling through modulation of FOXO1/PDK4 and ER stress-UPR signaling
Article.Authors: He Z.; Li H.; Ran L.; Zhong Y.; Luo Y.; Wu W.; Bao D.
Article.Abstract: AbstractType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is accompanied by pathological alterations in skeletal muscle, yet effective therapeutic strategies targeting these alterations remain limited. Current interventions, including exercise and nutritional supplementation, often exhibit poor long-term adherence and limited efficacy under diabetic conditions. Therefore, convenient, durable, and metabolically effective therapies are urgently needed. Evidence suggests that excessive endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and unfolded protein response (UPR) activation contribute to diabetic skeletal muscle remodeling, while pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 (PDK4) may serve as a key mediator linking metabolic dysfunction to ER stress signaling. A T2DM mouse model was established using high-fat diet feeding combined with streptozotocin administration. Inclisiran was administered intraperitoneally after model establishment. RNA sequencing combined with SVM-RFE analysis identified key targets potentially associated with protective effects of inclisiran. Metabolic parameters, muscle atrophy markers, ER stress/UPR signaling, and muscle fiber type transition were evaluated by real-time qPCR, immunoblotting, and immunofluorescence. Inclisiran significantly reduced fasting blood glucose levels and improved metabolic abnormalities in diabetic mice. Transcriptomic analysis identifiedPDK4as a key hub gene potentially associated with pathological alterations in diabetic skeletal muscle and the response to inclisiran treatment. Diabetic mice exhibited marked activation of ER stress/UPR signaling and increased expression of FOXO1, PDK4, and FBX32, whereas inclisiran treatment significantly suppressed these alterations. Additionally, inclisiran partially reversed diabetes-induced muscle fiber type transition from oxidative to glycolytic phenotypes. Inclisiran was associated with improved metabolic abnormalities and favorable alterations in skeletal muscle molecular and fiber-type remodeling in diabetic mice. Transcriptomic analysis identifiedPDK4as a potential molecular factor associated with these skeletal muscle alterations. Inclisiran treatment was associated with reduced expression of FOXO1, PDK4, and ER stress-UPR-related markers, together with partial preservation of skeletal muscle fiber-type homeostasis. These findings provide preliminary molecular and histological evidence supporting a potential protective effect of inclisiran on diabetes-associated skeletal muscle remodeling.

Article.Title: Physics-informed sparse deep neural networks for ultra-fast solar power forecasting and frequency response support in ancillary service markets
Article.Authors: Mohanty A.; Ramasamy A.; Mohanty S.; Rajamony R.; Satpathy A.; Bhutto J.; Alzahrani S.; Ali Arabi A.; Mohanty P.; Allasi H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe rising penetration of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems into the current power grid leads to large variations and uncertainties, which are key challenges to frequency stability and reliable auxiliary services. In this research, a novel Physics-Informed Sparse Deep Neural Network (PI-SDNN) framework is proposed for quick and accurate solar power forecasting specially built to enable fast frequency response (FFR) in auxiliary service markets. The proposed approach incorporates domain-specific physical constraints such as irradiance-power correlations, inverter dynamics and ramp-rate limitations, in a sparsity-promoting deep learning framework, which facilitates superior generalization, lower computational complexity and improved interpretability. The PI-SDNN model exploits structured physics-informed regularization to capture rich spatiotemporal features from high-resolution meteorological and historical generation data. The approach ensures fast inference suitable for real-time grid operations while preserving the forecasting accuracy in highly dynamic environmental scenarios. Furthermore, the forecasting findings are strongly related to a frequency response support module for proactive deployment and reserve allocation of solar-integrated ancillary services. Extensive simulations on real solar datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms classical deep learning and statistical models, yielding 25–40% improvement in forecasting accuracy metrics and significant reduction in computational latency. The integration of PI-SDNN with grid frequency management enhances the reaction speed and reduces frequency nadir variations during disturbances. The results show the potential of physics-informed sparse learning as a disruptive tool for reliable, scalable and commercially viable participation of solar in fast frequency response services, thus increasing the resilience and sustainability of future low-carbon power systems.

Article.Title: Aberrant CPS1 expression is linked to metabolic alterations and metastatic phenotypes in colorectal cancer liver metastasis
Article.Authors: Xiang Q.; Yang M.; Li X.; Tang J.; Yang X.; Zhang F.; Wu S.; Song X.; Wu Z.; Xiang T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractColorectal carcinoma liver metastasis (CRLM) is the main cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its metabolic drivers remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated three GEO datasets to identify metabolic reprogramming signatures distinguishing CRLM compared to primary tumors. A four-gene metabolism-related risk model was constructed using LASSO-Cox regression in the TCGA M1 cohort and independently validated in GSE17536. Carbamoyl-phosphate synthase 1 (CPS1) emerged as an independent prognostic factor and was markedly upregulated in CRLM tissues compared with matched primary tumors and normal colon, as validated by immunohistochemistry and qRT-PCR in seven paired clinical specimens. Reciprocal loss- and gain-of function experiments in HCT116 and SW480 cells demonstrate that CPS1 promotes invasion and migration without affecting proliferation. Mechanistically, CPS1 exerted pro-metastatic effects independently of canonical urea cycle activity. Instead, CPS1 positively correlated with ether lipid metabolism, reciprocally regulating key enzymes including AGPS and modulating cadherin expression to enhance cellular plasticity. These finding reveal a previously unrecognized role of CPS1 in promoting CRLM via ether lipid metabolic remodeling, highlighting its potential as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Developing analysis algorithm for engineered skeletal muscle contractile function based on a microphysiological system
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Li Y.; Li Y.; Du X.; Zhang Z.; Song B.; Li X.; Zhang J.; Ouyang J.; Si N.; Li Q.; Gu Z.; Yin N.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAutonomous contractility is a key functional characteristic of skeletal muscle and an important indicator of engineered muscle maturation. Conventional contact-based force measurements are limited by mechanical interference, restricted spatial resolution, and poor compatibility with high-throughput microphysiological systems. Here, we present a non-contact optical–mechanical framework for quantitative evaluation of contractile dynamics in three-dimensional engineered skeletal muscle. C2C12-derived muscle bundles were generated in fibrin–Matrigel hydrogels and cultured within a customized PDMS microdevice incorporating dual elastic cantilevers and integrated electrodes for controlled electrical stimulation. High-resolution video microscopy combined with optical flow tracking was used to quantify cantilever deformation, which was subsequently converted into contractile force using cantilever beam theory. This approach enabled the extraction of multiple functional parameters, including contraction amplitude, frequency, velocity, and force–time characteristics. The engineered tissues formed aligned, striated myofibers and exhibited rhythmic contractions synchronized with stimulation. Quantitative analysis demonstrated a strong correlation between separately recorded optical deformation and calcium transient signals (r = 0.88 ± 0.03, n = 5 independent constructs,p< 0.01). Reproducible force outputs and frequency-dependent changes in deformation amplitude and contraction velocity were observed across stimulation frequencies from 1 to 3 Hz. Estimated cantilever forces were consistently higher on the right than on the left, suggesting a possible contribution from systematic device- or measurement-related factors. Overall, this framework provides a non-invasive and quantitative approach for functional assessment of engineered skeletal muscle and may facilitate applications in disease modeling, drug evaluation, and microphysiological system-based research.

Article.Title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward pulmonary function testing among patients with cough
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Liu J.; Cheng Q.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis cross-sectional study aimed to examine the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to pulmonary function testing (PFT) among patients presenting with cough. Self-designed KAP questionnaire was conducted at Ruijin Hospital, involving 387 patients between 24 June 2024 and 7 March 2025. Participants were mostly female (53.0%) and aged 35–54 years (47.5%). The majority were married (82.9%) and lived in urban areas (88.6%). Regarding cough duration, 37.7% reported ≥ 8 weeks and 35.7% <3 weeks. Most had never smoked (84.2%). For prior pulmonary function testing (PFT), 39.3% reported undergoing testing within 1 year. The mean ± SD knowledge and attitudes scores were 21.53 ± 6.66 (possible range: 0–23), 30.48 ± 3.76 (possible range: 8–40), respectively. Adherence to routine pulmonary function testing was observed in 57.9% of patients. In multivariate analysis, higher knowledge scores (OR = 1.080, 95%CI: 1.037–1.124,P< 0.001) and attitude scores (OR = 1.133, 95%CI: 1.052–1.220,P= 0.001) were significantly associated with increased PFT adherence. Conversely, a lower Body Mass Index was associated with active practice (< 18.5: OR = 13.413,P= 0.013), though this warrants cautious interpretation due to the small subgroup size. Additionally, employees from enterprises showed significantly higher adherence (OR = 4.353,P= 0.009). Patients presenting with cough showed good awareness of general PFT concepts but poor understanding of specialized pulmonary function tests, also, patients showed passive attitudes and suboptimal practices toward pulmonary function testing.

Article.Title: Digital twin-guided service-aware graph attention ant colony optimization for reliable dynamic IPv6 routing in power data networks
Article.Authors: Hu F.; Huang Y.; Zhang S.; Lin X.; Wu L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPower data networks operating over IPv6-enabled communication infrastructures carry heterogeneous grid services with different latency, bandwidth, operational-risk, and recovery-priority requirements. Static routing metrics and manually weighted Quality of Service (QoS) objectives are insufficient to represent the dynamic coupling among traffic load, service priority, link risk, queueing delay, and fault states in dynamic IPv6 routing environments. This paper proposes a digital twin-guided service-aware graph attention ant colony optimization framework, termed SAG-RTACO, for reliability-oriented dynamic IPv6 routing in power data networks. A routing-oriented network digital twin is first constructed to synchronize topology, traffic, QoS, risk, service, and fault states into a time-varying graph for IPv6 service flows. A service-aware Graph Attention Network (GAT) then learns link suitability under heterogeneous service requests, and the learned edge scores are incorporated into a risk-time Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) search process. A priority-aware primary-backup routing and fault-recovery mechanism is further designed to improve the recovery priority of critical grid services carried by the IPv6-enabled network. Experiments on a 14-node power data network with ten representative service types show that SAG-RTACO achieves a mean path satisfaction of 0.538, reduces average risk cost to 28.7, improves backup availability to 88.9%, and lowers the service failure rate to 9.4%. Additional out-of-distribution IPv6 routing tests under priority-skewed traffic, bursty arrivals, clustered faults, and combined distribution shifts yield GAT AUC values of 0.761–0.816 and SAG-RTACO path satisfaction values of 0.478–0.522 without retraining, indicating graceful performance degradation under unseen operating conditions. Additional fidelity, ablation, robustness, and statistical analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed framework under the tested routing scenarios.

Article.Title: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms and sleep disturbance in college freshmen: a cross-sectional conditional process analysis
Article.Authors: Luo K.; Li C.; Huang J.; Wang L.; Liu Y.; Sun C.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSleep disturbance is common among college students, but the statistical relationships linking obsessive-compulsive symptoms (OCS), affective symptoms, and problematic Internet use remain unclear in nonclinical freshmen. In this cross-sectional study, 9,418 college freshmen aged 18–23 years (M = 19.60, SD = 0.65; 3,660 females) completed relevant subscales of the Chinese College Students’ Mental Health Screening Scale. Covariate-adjusted conditional process analyses (analyticN= 9,416) estimated separate and serial indirect associations through anxiety and depression and first-stage moderation by Internet addiction (IA). OCS was positively associated with sleep disturbance (B = 0.284, t = 20.58,p< .001, 95% CI [0.257, 0.311]). Indirect associations were observed through anxiety (estimate = 0.263, 95% bootstrap CI [0.232, 0.293]), depression (estimate = 0.098, 95% bootstrap CI [0.084, 0.114]), and anxiety followed by depression (estimate = 0.113, 95% bootstrap CI [0.098, 0.130]). The OCS × IA interaction in the anxiety equation was statistically significant but small (B = 0.0057, SE = 0.0015, t = 3.71,p< .001). Concurrent measurement prevents conclusions about temporal ordering or causality.

Article.Title: Analysis of unloading failure mechanical characteristics in columnar jointed rock mass
Article.Authors: Ma S.; Yuan Y.; Zhou Y.; Ma D.; Kang J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study fabricated columnar jointed rock mass specimens with varying joint inclination angles using rock-like materials and conducted triaxial unloading tests under different initial confining pressures and unloading rates to investigate their mechanical characteristics under various conditions. The results indicate: (1) As the initial confining pressure increases, the peak strength of the specimens gradually rises, and the elastic modulus progressively increases. With increasing joint inclination angle, both the peak strength and elastic modulus of the specimens exhibit a "U"-shaped trend, initially decreasing and then increasing. (2) Under triaxial unloading conditions, the stress–strain curve of columnar jointed rock mass shows an inflection point at the unloading stage, where the elastic modulus suddenly increases, and the specimen volume transitions from compression to expansion. The strength of columnar jointed rock mass under triaxial unloading conditions is lower than that under conventional triaxial compression conditions. Moreover, as the unloading rate increases, the specimen strength gradually decreases, and the characteristics of brittle failure become more pronounced.

Article.Title: Social context information and acoustic convergence in elephant vocal choruses
Article.Authors: Mahon L.; Pardo M.; Miron M.; Chemla E.; Granli P.; Njiraini N.; Moss C.; Keen S.; Poole J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractElephants use low-frequency rumbles to communicate among individuals. Rumbles occur in several patterns: as discrete, non-overlapping calls, in antiphonal sequences where individuals alternate vocalizations, and in choruses where multiple individuals produce overlapping calls. Despite the wide availability of bioacoustics tools, most studies focus on non-overlapping signals rather than on choruses. Here, we address this gap by investigating multi-caller rumble choruses recorded in several behavioral contexts. We show that behavioral context can be predicted from single (i.e., non-overlapping) and from overlapping, chorused rumbles. We find that individual rumbles in a chorus share structural similarities with single rumbles used in the same behavioral context, suggesting that choruses are composed of context-matched individual elements that together form a distinct multi-caller signal. We also find that the rumbles within choruses converge acoustically in particular behavioral contexts. Lastly, we find that the rumbles associated with various contexts vary systematically among individuals and family groups and suggest that individual acoustic differences may account for the observed family-level variation. Our findings extend previous work showing that rumbles encode behavioral context and caller identity, providing novel evidence that elephant choruses function as group signals encoding context through both their composition and patterns of acoustic convergence.

Article.Title: Discrepancy between soil safety and herbal risk: high cadmium enrichment in roots and leaves of Plantago asiatica and associated health implications
Article.Authors: Qiu S.; Dong Y.; Ai Q.; Yu X.; Liang J.; Zhang L.; Ye M.; Shao H.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPlantago asiatica(P. asiatica) plays an important role in traditional Chinese medicine treatments and ecological environment assessments. This study focused on the heavy metals discrepancy between soil safety and health risk from different parts ofP. asiatica. The contents of 10 heavy metals in the roots, stems, leaves, seeds and corresponding soils were determined using ICP-MS. A health risk assessment method for heavy metal elements was established and simulated by Monte Carlo. The assessment integrated the Bioconcentration Factor (BCF), Hazard Index (HI) and Total Carcinogenic Risk (TCR) models. Results revealed significant variations in heavy metal concentrations and exceedance rates among different plant parts. Roots and leaves exhibited the highest exceedance rates (100% and 57.69%, respectively), while the growth soils remained below the risk screening values for agricultural land. This was primarily attributed to their strong Cd enrichment capacity (BCF: 10.18 in roots, 6.73 in leaves). However, low translocation factors (TF < 1) were found in stems, leaves and seeds, suggestingP. asiaticaas a potential candidate for phytostabilization research. Furthermore, risk assessment from the proposed medicinal material safety threshold indicated that heavy metal levels in all four parts posed potential non-carcinogenic health risks for both adults and children under the conservative assumption that all measured As was inorganic As. This contrasted with the food safety framework, under which only roots exceeded the threshold. Moreover, a potential carcinogenic effect was identified in roots for adults under the conservative assumption that all measured As was inorganic As. Therefore, significant discrepancy existed in heavy metal contamination and associated health risks across different parts ofP. asiatica. In particular, As in roots and leaves were identified as the primary drivers of potential non-carcinogenic health risks, warranting prioritized attention in quality control and risk management. It was recommended to avoid or reduce using high-risk parts (especially roots) in medicinal applications.

Article.Title: Cu(II) coordination complex doped PVA/NaAlg polymer blend as a redox active composite electrodes for energy storage devices
Article.Authors: Elamin N.; Rajeh A.; Gomaa E.; Zaky R.; El-Hady M.; Alqarni M.; Alzahrani S.; Mannaa A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPolymer-based composite electrodes with tunable electrochemical properties are of growing interest for energy storage applications. In this work, flexible PVA/NaAlg polymer blend films were modified via molecular coordination doping using a Cu(II) coordination complex as filler to elucidate the structure–property-performance relationship governing their electrochemical behavior. The induced increase in the amorphous structure of the PVA/NaAlg mix and the development of intermolecular contacts between the host polymer and the additional filler were shown by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra. The direct and indirect band gaps decreased from 4.75 to 3.50 eV and from 4.49 to 3.11 eV, respectively, as filler loading increased, according to UV–visible spectroscopy. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) measurements in acidic electrolyte demonstrated a transition from weakly capacitive behavior in the pristine blend to a mixed electric double-layer/pseudocapacitive response in the doped films, driven by redox-active coordination centers. The specific capacitance, calculated from CV curves, increased markedly upon Cu(II) complex incorporation and decreased with increasing scan rate, consistent with diffusion and kinetics-limited pseudocapacitive systems. The 1.00 wt% Cu(II) doped film exhibited the highest capacitance, while intermediate loadings showed improved rate capability. Overall, the results highlight coordination-based molecular doping as an effective strategy for tailoring the structural, electronic, and electrochemical properties of polymer composites for energy storage applications.

Article.Title: Prevalent α-chain–centric TCR metaclones shape specificity and focus early SARS-CoV-2 T cell responses
Article.Authors: Bansal S.; Bottorff T.; Linsley P.
Article.Abstract: AbstractChain-centric TCRs or metaclones, in which one chain pairs with diverse partners, are well documented, but their role in immunity remains unclear. Here, we characterize paired human αβ TCR datasets and show that alpha-centric TCRs are more prevalent than beta-centric TCRs across healthy and diseased individuals. Sequence modeling links alpha-centricity to shorterTRACDR3 length, greater flexibility, and increased hydrophobicity. Alpha-centric TCRs are enriched for multi-epitopeVDJdbannotation, especially for epitopes most dissimilar to each other in sequence. T cells with Spike-motif alpha-centric TCRs, including 1–2-mismatch variants, are activated in COVID-19 patients. These TCRs also shareTRAjunctions with CMV, EBV, and influenza-reactive TCRs, consistent with broadly cross-reactive,TRA-dominant CD4+ responses. Our findings suggest a role forTRA-dominant recognition in shaping cross-reactive CD4+ T cell immunity.

Article.Title: Reliability gated cross-modal attention with shear reparameterized directional reasoning for RGB-thermal salient object detection
Article.Authors: Othman K.; Noorwali A.; Alohali M.; Ullah I.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRGB-Thermal (RGB-T) salient object detection localizes salient regions where appearance cues alone are insufficient, since thermal radiation stays informative under poor illumination. Two limitations persist. Cross-modal attention is applied at a strength fixed in advance, so a momentarily uninformative stream continues to contribute in full, and directional reasoning is confined to the two image axes, because diagonal coverage has required a dense affinity mask of quadratic cost. We present CDRNet, a Confidence and Directional Reasoning Network with dual ResNet-50 encoders. Cross-modal attention is reliability-gated: a coefficient estimated for each modality from spatial entropy and gradient energy scales the transferred context through a gated residual, and the attention scale is derived from the cosine discrepancy between the pooled modality embeddings, so sharpness follows the semantic gap instead of a fixed constant, and balanced inputs recover symmetric fusion. Directional reasoning is shear-reparameterized: a circular shear maps each diagonal onto an axis, so a single axial operator covers four orientations at axial rather than quadratic cost, a per-pixel gate exposes the learned anisotropy, and a weight-shared second stage refines the result without additional parameters. A boundary gated decoder returns edge evidence to the representation through multiplicative modulation under auxiliary supervision, and its cross scale aggregator mixes two dilation rates per branch under context-dependent weights. On VT821, VT1000, and VT5000, CDRNet attains S-measure values of 0.908, 0.949, and 0.918, surpasses 19 recent methods on all metrics, and ablations isolate each contribution.

Article.Title: Phytotoxicity of potassium antimony(III) oxide tartrate trihydrate in Allium cepa revealed through multilevel biological responses
Article.Authors: Sarsar O.; Çavuşoğlu K.; Yalçın E.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAntimony is an increasingly widespread environmental metalloid capable of exerting significant toxic effects on biological systems. However, the mechanisms underlying its multi-faceted toxicity in plant cells remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to provide an integrated assessment of the physiological, cytogenetic, biochemical, and anatomical effects of potassium antimony (III) oxide tartrate trihydrate inAllium cepaL. root meristem cells. Root-based endpoints were evaluated following exposure to 20, 100, and 500 µg/L Sb for 72 h, whereas exposure was extended to 144 h to allow sufficient leaf development for chlorophyll analysis. Germination and growth parameters, mitotic index, micronucleus frequency, chromosomal abnormalities, DNA damage, malondialdehyde content, superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, chlorophyll contents, and anatomical alterations were evaluated. Antimony exposure significantly reduced germination, root length, weight gain, and mitotic index, while markedly increasing micronucleus and chromosomal abnormality frequencies. Comet assay revealed a reduction in head DNA from 96.9% to 66.5%, accompanied by an increase in tail DNA from 3.10% to 33.5%. Moreover, antimony exposure markedly enhanced lipid peroxidation and antioxidant enzyme activities, while substantially reducing chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b contents. Anatomical analyses demonstrated increases in epidermal cell damage, cortical cell wall thickening, and flattened nucleus. Collectively, these findings suggest that antimony suppresses cell division, disrupts genomic integrity, and induces structural tissue damage inA. ceparoot meristem cells. This integrated assessment demonstrates the multilevel phytotoxic effects of potassium antimony(III) oxide tartrate trihydrate and provides a basis for future investigations of its toxicological mechanisms and ecotoxicological significance.

Article.Title: Adaptive evolutionary PID controller using SHADE and L-SHADE for TRIGA mark-II reactor
Article.Authors: Lokman G.; İşcan S.; Çelik E.; Sharma S.; Sharma G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes a trajectory-tracking PID (TTPID) controller optimized using Success-History Based Adaptive Differential Evolution (SHADE) and its improved variant Linear Population Size Reduction SHADE (L-SHADE) for power regulation of the ITU TRIGA Mark-II research reactor. The main novelty of the study is the integration of adaptive differential evolution mechanisms with a trajectory-tracking PID framework for nuclear reactor power control, which has not previously been reported in the literature. A constrained Integral of Time-Weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) objective function is employed to simultaneously minimize tracking error and limit excessive control-rod motion. The optimization performance of SHADE and L-SHADE is first compared, showing that L-SHADE achieves faster and more stable convergence with lower fitness fluctuations. The optimized controller is then evaluated under different initial and desired power levels ranging from 50 to 250 kW. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed L-SHADE-TTPIDC successfully tracks the reference trajectory with negligible steady-state error and overshoot below 1.1% at a target power level of 225 kW. The controller achieves settling times below 23 s and response times as low as 17 s, outperforming previously reported FLC-PSO and MFLNN-PSO controllers in most operating scenarios. In addition, all operational constraints were satisfied while maintaining smooth control-rod movement. The results confirm that adaptive differential evolution-based PID tuning provides an effective and robust solution for nonlinear reactor power control and represents a promising alternative to existing intelligent control approaches.

Article.Title: Preliminary safety and efficacy of liquid-type polycaprolactone for neck rejuvenation in Asian adults in a prospective pilot study
Article.Authors: Thongjaroensirikul P.; Techapichetvanich T.; Maneeprasopchoke P.; Nokdhes Y.; Buranaporn P.; Wannawittayapa T.; Bhorntarakcharoen W.; Sittiwanaruk S.; Abhinoraseth P.; Yamlexnoi P.; Meethong O.; Wanitphakdeedecha R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe neck is a challenging area for aesthetic rejuvenation due to its thin dermis and the risk of nodule formation associated with traditional particulate fillers. A novel, liquid-type polycaprolactone (PCL) offers a potential alternative by mitigating these risks. To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of liquid-type PCL for the treatment of horizontal neck lines in Asian patients. In this prospective, open-label, single-arm pilot study, 30 Asian subjects received three sessions of liquid-type PCL (GOURI; 210 mg/mL, 21% PCL) injections at one-month intervals using a subdermal cannula technique. All participants completed the treatment series; follow-up data were available for 29 participants at 1 month and 28 participants at both 3 and 6 months after completion of treatment. Objective biophysical parameters, including skin elasticity (Cutometer) and skin texture/wrinkle depth (Antera 3D), were assessed over a 6-month follow-up period. Subjective satisfaction and safety were also evaluated. Visual and quantitative assessments demonstrated measurable improvement in horizontal neck lines and skin quality over 6 months. In participant-level paired analyses, skin distensibility (R0) decreased from 0.214 ± 0.089 at baseline to 0.102 ± 0.091 at 6 months (mean change, −0.109; 95% CI, −0.152 to −0.066; standardized mean change [Cohen’s dz], −1.03;p< 0.001). Gross elasticity (R2) changed from 66.66 ± 15.72 to 38.16 ± 29.35 (mean change, −28.68; 95% CI, −40.70 to −16.67; dz, −0.93;p< 0.001). Skin roughness, volume of depression, and melanin index also decreased significantly. At 6 months, 85% of participants with available follow-up data reported ≥ 51% improvement. The treatment was generally well tolerated; one participant developed mild bruising that resolved spontaneously within 8 days. Liquid-type PCL may represent a safe and minimally invasive option for neck rejuvenation in appropriately selected patients. These pilot data suggest measurable improvement in neck skin texture, firmness-related parameters, and pigmentation; however, controlled studies with longer follow-up and blinded evaluation are required to confirm efficacy, durability, and optimal candidate selection.
