Article.Title: PPTM-IoV: a privacy-preserving trust management framework for the Internet of Vehicles (IoV)
Article.Authors: Malik A.; Mian Qaisar S.; Shah S.; Uddin M.; Salhi A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Internet of Vehicles (IoV) enables seamless Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication among connected vehicles, infrastructure, and cloud services, supporting Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) through real-time information exchange. However, the dynamic and decentralized nature of IoV environments introduces significant challenges related to trust management, privacy preservation, and secure communication. To address these challenges, in this paper, we propose PPTM-IoV, a privacy-preserving trust management framework that enables vehicles to establish trust without revealing their private data. The framework first introduces a privacy-preserving identity and credential management scheme that uses pseudonymous identities and verifiable credentials, combined with a non-interactive zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) mechanism based on established cryptographic techniques. Next, a dynamic trust evaluation mechanism is designed by combining direct observations and weighted indirect recommendations. The trust model is further strengthened with adaptive updating based on significant behavioral changes and supported by analytical properties. To protect sensitive trust information during outsourced computation, the framework employs Paillier-based homomorphic encryption, enabling secure trust aggregation in the encrypted domain. A privacy-preserving trust processing workflow is achieved by integrating homomorphic computation with trusted-authority-assisted proxy re-encryption. Furthermore, a proxy re-encryption mechanism supports authorized trust verification between vehicles without exposing trust scores to unauthorized entities. Finally, a secure and trust-aware communication protocol incorporates bidirectional trust verification, threshold-based decision-making, and encrypted as well as digitally signed message exchange to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and mutual trust enforcement. The proposed framework is implemented using SUMO and NS-3 simulators. Experimental results demonstrate that PPTM-IoV achieves superior performance compared to the best-performing benchmark schemes, reducing average latency by 4.80%, while improving PDR by 1.43%, throughput by 4.09%, and trust accuracy by 1.47%.

Article.Title: Discovery of FGFBP1 as a novel target of isorhamnetin against LUSC and preliminary study of sea buckthorn-derived carbon dots
Article.Authors: Ji H.; Li X.; Luo J.; Nie C.; Liu C.; Yao W.; Gan J.; Jin Y.; Chen W.; Fu A.; Wu H.; Cui Y.; Mo F.; Ge Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) remains a challenging malignancy with limited targeted therapies. Isorhamnetin (ISO), a natural flavonoid derived from sea buckthorn, exhibits promising antitumor activity. However, its molecular targets and underlying mechanisms in LUSC remain unclear. Concurrently, carbon dots (CDs) synthesized from herbal sources have emerged as promising nanoplatforms for cancer theranostics. This study aimed to elucidate the antitumor mechanism of ISO in LUSC and explore the potential of sea buckthorn-derived CDs as a functional nanomedicine. LUSC cells were treated with different concentrations (0, 50, 100 μM) of ISO. The effects on cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were assessed via CCK-8 assays, colony formation assays, scratch assays, and Transwell assays. Differentially expressed genes were screened through transcriptome sequencing, with key targets validated by Western blot analysis. Construct FGFBP1 overexpression cell lines for reversal experiments and detect downstream FGF2c/ERK signalling pathway-related protein expression. Additionally, sea buckthorn carbon dots (SB-CDs) were synthesised via hydrothermal synthesis using sea buckthorn as the carbon source. Characterisation was performed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, ultraviolet–visible absorption spectroscopy, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Preliminary evaluation assessed their inhibitory effect on the malignant phenotype of LUSC cells. ISO significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of LUSC cells in a dose-dependent manner. Transcriptomics and protein analysis revealed that ISO downregulated fibroblast growth factor binding protein 1 (FGFBP1) and inhibited the downstream FGF2/ERK signaling pathway. Overexpression of FGFBP1 partially reversed the antitumor effects of ISO. Meanwhile, SB-CDs were successfully prepared with excellent fluorescence properties and effectively inhibited the malignant behaviors of LUSC cells in a concentration-dependent manner. ISO exerts its anti-tumour effects in LUSC by downregulating FGFBP1 and inhibiting the FGF2/ERK signalling pathway. Furthermore, sea buckthorn-derived carbon dots exhibit inherent antitumor properties, demonstrating a successful transformation from medicinal plant to functional nanomaterial. This study not only provides new insights into the mechanism of ISO but also offers a green and sustainable strategy for developing plant-based nano-theranostic agents against LUSC.

Article.Title: Ultrasonic-assisted green synthesis of schiff base-functionalized CdS nanoparticles with enhanced optical, anticancer, and antibacterial properties
Article.Authors: Kumar K.; Reena V.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIn the present investigation, a novel Schiff base ligand was synthesized through the condensation of benzaldehyde, o-hydroxyacetophenone, and 1,2-ethylenediamine using an ultrasonically assisted green chemical approach. The resulting ligand was subsequently employed as a capping agent for the synthesis of cadmium sulfide nanoparticles (CdS NPs), yielding Schiff base-functionalized CdS nanoparticles (L–CdS NPs). The synthesized Schiff base ligand and functionalized nanoparticles were comprehensively characterized by elemental analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), UV–Vis, IR,13C and1H NMR, and HRMS techniques. XRD analysis confirmed the crystalline nature of CdS and revealed nanoscale crystallite dimensions, while the observed peak broadening was indicative of reduced particle size and the formation of a highly crystalline, phase-pure structure. Photoluminescence studies further demonstrated enhanced emission characteristics of the Schiff base-capped CdS nanoparticles compared with the uncapped CdS nanoparticles. These results indicate that Schiff base functionalization not only contributes to the stabilization of the CdS nanoparticle surface but also modulates its physicochemical and biological properties. Both the free Schiff base ligand and L–CdS NPs exhibited appreciable in vitro cytotoxicity against Dalton’s lymphoma ascites (DLA) cells, with the nanoparticle formulation displaying substantially enhanced cytotoxic efficacy. Consistent with these findings, in vivo studies demonstrated pronounced antitumor activity against both Ehrlich ascites carcinoma (EAC)-induced ascites and DLA-induced solid tumour models in Swiss albino female mice, underscoring the therapeutic potential of the Schiff base-functionalized CdS nanostructure as a multifunctional bioactive platform. The L–CdS NPs were further investigated for their biological potential, particularly antibacterial activity. Overall, the findings demonstrate that Schiff base capping provides an effective strategy for stabilizing CdS nanoparticles while enhancing their biological activity, highlighting their potential for future biomedical and nanotechnological applications.

Article.Title: Terminal hydroxylation of eIF5A hypusination influences mitochondrial protein expression and cellular metabolism in fission yeast
Article.Authors: Kondo N.; Shirai A.; Magpantay H.; Arioka M.; Hamamoto M.; Yoshida M.; Matsuyama A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractHypusination of eIF5A is an essential, oxygen-dependent post-translational modification catalyzed sequentially by DHPS and deoxyhypusine hydroxylase (DOHH). Although previous SILAC-based studies in budding yeast established that DOHH acts as an oxygen sensor regulating mitochondrial translation, whether this mechanism represents a generalized eukaryotic paradigm or a species-specific adaptation remains unknown. Here, we investigated the proteome-wide impact of disrupting the terminal hydroxylation of eIF5A using a DOHH-deficient mutant (mmd1Δ) in the evolutionarily distant fission yeastSchizosaccharomyces pombe. Utilizing an ORFeome-scale proteomic approach under a uniform expression framework, we demonstrate that DOHH loss does not uniformly reduce protein abundance but preferentially alters the abundance of mitochondrial proteins, specifically oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) components. Reflecting these proteomic shifts,mmd1Δ cells exhibited impaired respiration and a compensatory metabolic shift toward fermentation. Crucially, oxygen limitation reduced hypusinated eIF5A levels and recapitulated themmd1Δ phenotype in fission yeast. By demonstrating that this post-translational circuit operates identically across highly divergent yeast models, our results establish the evolutionary conservation of the DOHH-eIF5A axis, firmly validating it as a universal mechanism coupling environmental oxygen availability to mitochondrial translation.

Article.Title: Characteristics of ESBL-positive Escherichia coli causing community-acquired UTIs in India
Article.Authors: Kocher D.; Pundir S.; Mohapatra S.; Kalaivani M.; Gautam H.; Sood S.; Dhawan B.; Nayak B.; Kumar A.; Kumari R.; Mahajan S.; Hari P.; Kapil A.; Das B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUropathogenicE. coli(UPEC) is the predominant uropathogen in community-acquired urinary tract infections (CA-UTIs) globally. However, data from India on relationship between antimicrobial resistance, virulence factors, and clonal markers in UPEC remain scarce. We studied 80 ESBL-positive UPEC isolates causing CA-UTI across four Indian regions. Antimicrobial susceptibility done using VITEK-2. PCR assays detected ESBL genes (blaCTX-M-15,blaTEM), carbapenemase genes (blaNDM,blaOXA-48-like), virulence genes (fimH, pap, sfa, hlyA, aer) and serogroup O25b. Phenotypic virulence assays assessed hemolysin, haemagglutination, biofilm and gelatinase production. All isolates susceptible to fosfomycin, with high susceptibility to nitrofurantoin (87.5%) and ertapenem (85%). Predominant resistance gene wasblaCTX-M-15(97.5%), followed byblaTEM(55%),blaNDM(16.3%) andblaOXA-48-like(5%). Biofilm formation (41.3%) most prevalent virulence trait, followed by haemagglutination (35%). Frequently detected virulence genes werepap(61.3%),fimH(55%), andaer(48.8%). The O25b serogroup found in 41.3% of isolates had lower ertapenem resistance than non-O25b strains. This study shows ESBL-producing UPEC isolates from community settings in India frequently harbour multiple beta-lactamase resistance genes and virulence factors, underscoring their adaptability and clinical threat in CA-UTIs. These findings emphasize the critical need for continued molecular surveillance, strengthened infection control, and robust antibiotic stewardship programs to mitigate the spread of multidrug-resistant, virulent UPEC strains.

Article.Title: Empirically informed AHP-FR modeling for multi-hazard susceptibility mapping in a mountainous transport corridors
Article.Authors: Hussain M.; Xie X.; Su C.; Mehvish F.; Muneer M.; Akbar M.; Alanazi A.; Pinto M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMountainous transport corridors are increasingly exposed to interacting natural hazards that intensify infrastructure, socio-economic, and land-use risks. However, most susceptibility assessments for high-mountain corridors still focus on single hazards or rely heavily on expert-based weighting, which can introduce subjectivity into spatial decision-making. This study develops an empirically informed Analytical Hierarchy Process–Frequency Ratio (AHP-FR) framework for integrated landslide, debris-flow, and flood susceptibility mapping along the Barakhan–Gilgit–Juglot section of the northern China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC). The main methodological contribution is the use of frequency-ratio-derived empirical evidence that was integrated with AHP-derived factor weights to calculate final subclass weights and thereby reducing reliance on purely subjective expert judgment. Field surveys, remote sensing datasets, historical hazard inventories, and 12 conditioning factors were integrated in a GIS environment to generate single-hazard susceptibility maps and an eight-class multi-hazard susceptibility map. Independent ROC-AUC validation showed acceptable to very good predictive performance, with AUC values of 0.803 for landslides, 0.762 for debris flows, and 0.872 for floods. The results indicate that 63% of the corridor is exposed to one or more hazards, including 59% exposed to two or more overlapping hazards; 41% are co-susceptible to landslides and debris flows, while 37% falls within the no/very low multi-hazard susceptibility class. The spatial outputs identify major hazard-prone sections, including Attabad, Chalt, and Passu, providing practical guidance for road-maintenance prioritization, slope-stabilization planning, drainage improvement, and emergency preparedness. The added value of this study lies in combining empirical FR-based weighting with AHP and translating separate hazard maps into explicit multi-hazard combination classes, offering a reproducible decision-support framework for resilient planning in mountainous transport corridors.

Article.Title: Factors associated with persistent post-COVID-19 condition and functional limitation four years after SARS-CoV-2 infection
Article.Authors: Faraj M.; Grosshennig A.; Goedecke N.; Dirks M.; Hennemann A.; Greten S.; Ehrenreich H.; Blasczyk R.; Weissenborn K.; Beutel G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPost-COVID-19 condition (PCC) can persist for years after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, but factors associated with long-term persistence and functional outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this longitudinal cohort study, adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection who had volunteered for plasma donation completed surveys approximately 16 and 48 months after infection. Acute-phase demographic characteristics and symptoms were examined for associations with PCC and persistent PCC using multivariable logistic regression analyses. Persistent symptoms at follow-up and their associations with functional limitation, assessed with the Post-COVID Functional Status (PCFS) scale, were examined separately. Among 992 participants in 2021, 609 (61.4%) met criteria for PCC, while 333 of 568 participants (58.6%) fulfilled PCC criteria in 2024. Older age, fatigue, palpitations, depressive symptoms, and concentration and memory difficulties during acute infection were associated with PCC at both follow-up assessments, whereas female sex was associated with PCC only at the 4-year follow-up. Among participants with PCC in 2021, 77.4% continued to meet PCC criteria in 2024; concentration difficulties, depressive symptoms, and older age were associated with persistent PCC. Functional limitation was associated with persistent fatigue, concentration difficulties, dyspnea at rest, and depressive symptoms. These findings demonstrate the persistent nature of PCC and highlight the need for further research into the mechanisms behind PCC and the development of therapeutic strategies.

Article.Title: Design and realization of robust disturbance rejection decoupling control strategy for time delayed multi-variable process
Article.Authors: Maniramakrishna A.; Mahapatro S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper presents design and development of a robust decentralized PI controller exploiting an analytical model based approach for multi-variable system. In this work, a two-degree-of-freedom control approach is employed to tackle load disturbance rejection, enhance robustness against parametric uncertainties, and ensure precise set-point tracking. Proposed 2-DoF based disturbance rejection decoupling control guarantees robust stability in the face of a$$\pm 40\%$$variation in process gain and delay, while preserving equivalent performance.The robustness of the proposed controller has been verified by sensitivity analysis employing various perturbation levels range of$$\pm 40\%$$. To exhibit the superiority of the proposed controller, three industry-scaled case studies are considered. The obtained response of the proposed controller has been compared with similar other model-based controllers. From the obtained results it is envisaged that, the proposed controller provides adequate servo and regulatory performance as compared to other earlier reported approaches.

Article.Title: Monocular depth estimation for endoscopic surgery using swin transformer and conditional random fields
Article.Authors: Deng Y.; Yan C.; Cheng N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMonocular depth estimation in endoscopic surgery is challenging due to weak tissue textures, uneven illumination, specular reflections, and frequent smoke or instrument interference. This paper proposes CRFDepth, a pseudo‑supervised framework for endoscopic monocular depth estimation. A Swin Transformer encoder extracts hierarchical global features under weak‑texture conditions. The proposed CRFDepth framework effectively addresses key challenges in endoscopic monocular depth estimation, achieving superior accuracy and robustness. A Pyramid Scene Parsing module aggregates multi‑scale contextual information to improve structural perception in distorted regions. A NeWCRF decoder performs cross‑scale structured inference for boundary refinement and detail recovery. A RangeAwareLoss is introduced to stabilize optimization within the narrow endoscopic depth range. The network is trained with stereo-derived pseudo-ground-truth supervision using binocular image pairs, while only monocular input is required during inference. Experiments were conducted on the da Vinci laparoscopic dataset. CRFDepth achieves 44.27 dB PSNR and 0.9942 SSIM, outperforming baseline methods, and demonstrates strong robustness to occlusion and smoke interference.

Article.Title: Species distribution models of ESA-listed corals highlight niche differences among taxa that may guide recovery planning
Article.Authors: Tanaka K.; Oliver T.; Couch C.; Shantz A.; Turnham K.; Sena E.; Perelman J.; Huntington B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUnderstanding the biogeography of living marine resources is essential for informed management, particularly in data-limited environments. Here, we use two corals listed under the U.S. Endangered Species Act (ESA) around Tutuila, American Samoa, to evaluate a transferable workflow that combines presence-only occurrence records, open biodiversity repositories, and open-access environmental data to extend existing survey records and support species monitoring. We developed ensemble maximum entropy (MaxEnt) models for two Indo-Pacific corals,Acropora globicepsandIsopora crateriformis, using multi-source occurrence records collected from 2007 to 2025. Dynamic environmental predictors, including thermal stress, water clarity, and wind variability, were derived from open-access satellite datasets and temporally summarized to match field sampling dates, while static predictors represented seafloor structure and land-based stressors. To evaluate one-year-ahead forecast performance, we trained models on records through 2024, generated 2025 relative habitat-suitability forecasts using lagged 2024 environmental summaries, and evaluated them against independent 2025 observations. The 2025 forecasts showed moderate discrimination under temporal validation, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.74 forA. globicepsand 0.71 forI. crateriformis. The models revealed contrasting realized niches:A. globicepswas associated with shallower, rugose habitats and specific thermal-history conditions, whereasI. crateriformisshowed highest suitability at intermediate depths and appeared more constrained by thermal variability. These results suggest that occurrence-based SDMs can help distinguish species-specific habitat associations and guide monitoring or spatial prioritization, while remaining best interpreted as relative habitat suitability rather than definitive forecasts of occurrence. Because the workflow relies on presence-only records and open-access environmental data, it can be adapted to other taxa, regions, and applied questions where field data are limited.

Article.Title: Hybrid-integrated nonreciprocal polarization rotator based on dielectric metasurfaces and a magnet-free thin-film Faraday rotator
Article.Authors: Sunwoo Y.; Kwon Y.; Jeong J.; Zou X.; Lee W.; Choi D.; Kim J.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIntegrated nonreciprocal polarization control is essential for optical isolators and circulators that suppress back-reflection in photonic integrated circuits. In this study, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a hybrid-integrated metasurface-based nonreciprocal polarization rotator (MNPR) consisting of a metalens (ML), a magnet-free Faraday rotator (MFFR), and a bifunctional metasurface (BFMS). The ML provides reciprocal beam collimation and focusing, while the BFMS combines the same wavefront-shaping function with half-wave-plate-like 45° polarization rotation. The MFFR provides nonreciprocal 45° Faraday rotation without an external magnetic field. By aligning the beam path and polarization axes of the three components, the MNPR preserves the input polarization in the forward direction and converts it into the orthogonal polarization in the backward direction. The fabricated MNPR operates over the C-band (1527–1565 nm). At 1550 nm, the MNPR exhibits polarization extinction ratios of 21.3 ± 1.6 dB and 21.2 ± 0.7 dB and insertion losses of 6.4 ± 0.5 dB and 6.4 ± 0.1 dB in the forward and backward directions, respectively. After integration with a silicon waveguide chip, the MNPR preserves its nonreciprocal behavior, with insertion losses of 12.6 dB and 12.5 dB in the forward and backward directions, respectively. Structural optimization strategies are presented to reduce the insertion loss, suggesting its potential as a polarization-control building block for future on-chip optical isolators and circulators.

Article.Title: Success rate and determinants of intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke from the Malaysia National Stroke Registry
Article.Authors: Sies N.; Mat Ruzlin A.; Sidek N.; Ibrahim K.; Law W.; King T.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractIntravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is an established intervention for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet comprehensive real-world evidence on its success rate and determinants in low and middle countries (LMCs) remains limited. This retrospective cohort study aimed to determine the success rate of IVT and identify key determinants using data from the Malaysian National Stroke Registry (2014–2023) from two tertiary hospitals. Successful IVT was defined as a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of ≤ 4 at 24 h post-IVT. Individual-related, clinical-related, and treatment-related determinants were included as the independent variables. Multiple logistic regression was used to identify the determinants of successful IVT. A total of 1,011 eligible patients were included in the study with a median (IQR) age of 62.0 (19.0) years and 61.3% were males. The success rate of IVT was 37.8% (95% CI 34.8–40.8), with median onset-to-needle time of 192.0 (95.0) minutes. Younger age (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.99 (95% CI 0.98–0.99)), lower baseline NIHSS score (aOR 0.87 (95% CI 0.84–0.89)), and small vessel occlusion subtype (aOR 2.52 (95% CI 1.65–3.86)) were significant determinants of successful IVT. These findings highlight important determinants that may help optimize IVT delivery and improve stroke outcomes in Malaysia.

Article.Title: A novel hybrid and ensemble deep learning model for enhancing sentiment analysis in Persian context
Article.Authors: Rasooli A.; Servi S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAdvances in mobile technologies have established social media as a major platform for expressing emotions and opinions. Analyzing such publicly shared sentiments enables companies and political organizations to make informed and data-driven decisions. As a result, sentiment analysis has become an essential tool for researchers and policymakers seeking to accurately interpret public opinion. However, traditional text processing approaches often struggle to achieve high accuracy when dealing with complex and informal textual data, highlighting the need for more robust analytical frameworks. Although deep learning techniques have recently achieved notable success in Natural Language Processing (NLP), research on Persian sentiment analysis remains relatively limited. The primary objective of this study is to propose a novel hybrid and ensemble deep learning framework specifically designed for sentiment analysis in the Persian language. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed approach, multiple architectures were examined, including standalone models (BERT, RoBERTa, RNN, and BiLSTM), ensemble models based on averaging and majority voting strategies, and two hybrid configurations that integrate sequential and transformer-based models. Experimental results indicate that BiLSTM outperforms other standalone approaches, while the ensemble model using average voting and the hybrid configuration Hybrid-1 (BERT-RNN-BiLSTM) achieve the highest classification performance across accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating diverse deep learning strategies and emphasize the practical applicability of hybrid and ensemble architectures for Persian sentiment classification. This study presents a comprehensive and systematic investigation of hybrid transformer–recurrent architectures and ensemble learning strategies for Persian sentiment analysis, supported by extensive experiments on benchmark datasets. The proposed models were evaluated on four benchmark Persian sentiment analysis datasets, namely the Persian Electronic Dataset, MirasOpinion Dataset, Instagram Persian Comment Dataset and SentiDariPers Dataset. Experimental results, supported by comparative analysis with existing studies, demonstrate the consistent superiority of the proposed framework across all datasets. In particular, the Hybrid-1 (BERT-RNN-BiLSTM) model achieved the highest accuracy of 97.00% on the Persian Electronic Dataset, while accuracies of 84.00%, 80.75% and 95.19% were obtained on the MirasOpinion, Instagram Persian Comment and SentiDariPers datasets, respectively. Furthermore, the Hybrid-2 (RoBERTa-BiLSTM-RNN) and the proposed ensemble models also demonstrated strong and consistent performance across all four datasets, confirming the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed architectures for Persian sentiment classification.

Article.Title: Exploratory analysis of peripheral blood monocytes in breast cancer using prospective high-dimensional immune profiling
Article.Authors: Alsuwaidi L.; Panicker N.; AlHalabi W.; Samreen B.; Abdulrahim M.; AlSharhan M.; Otaki F.; Ghazi E.; Al Awa A.; Senok A.; Hachim M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractBreast cancer is a heterogeneous disease characterized by diverse molecular and immune features and blood-based immunophenotyping may provide insights into systemic immune variation relevant to treatment. Baseline immune profiling before surgery or systemic therapy reflects the natural tumor–host interaction and systemic immune status. In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating study, we integrated in silico analysis of publicly available high-dimensional immune profiling data with an independent prospective assessment of selected peripheral immune populations. Publicly available mass cytometry data from CD45 + viable singlet peripheral blood mononuclear cells of healthy donors, hereditary breast and ovarian cancer predisposition carriers, and breast cancer patients were analyzed using the CATALYST pipeline in R. Based on the immune patterns identified in the public dataset, selected immune populations were subsequently examined in an independent cohort of 11 treatment-naïve breast cancer patients using eight-color flow cytometry. The two approaches were used as complementary analyses rather than as direct technical validation of one another. Unsupervised clustering identified 20 immune metaclusters, with CD4 + T-cell and CD14 + monocyte subsets showing the greatest variation across groups. Patients subsequently allocated to neoadjuvant chemotherapy exhibited higher lymphocyte percentages (median, 53% vs. 42%,P= 0.004) and classical CD14 + + CD16 − monocytes (median, 73% vs. 58%,P< 0.0001), whereas patients undergoing surgery showed higher non-classical CD14 + CD16 + + monocytes (median, 16% vs. 10,P= 0.078). CD80/CD86 co-expression further classified patients into high, moderate, and low activation profiles. These baseline immune differences were associated with subsequent treatment allocation but remain descriptive, as patients had not yet received treatment at the time of peripheral blood sampling, providing preliminary, hypothesis-generating evidence of peripheral immune variation in breast cancer and supporting further investigation of monocyte and lymphocyte populations in larger prospective cohorts.

Article.Title: Types and prevalence of digital harassment from external and unknown individuals and prospective associations with employee health outcomes
Article.Authors: Winding T.; Pedersen A.; Andersen L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractDigital harassment from individuals external to the workplace is an emerging occupational health concern, but evidence on its longer-term health consequences remains limited. This prospective cohort study investigated characteristics associated with exposure, its prevalence, types, employee reactions, and associations with health outcomes among employees in Danish workplaces. Data were collected through two survey rounds in 2024, completed by 991 employees. Digital harassment was defined as harassment, intimidation, verbal abuse, threats, or unwanted sexual attention delivered through digital media. Qualitative thematic analysis identified ten harassment types and thirteen employee reactions. Outcomes included burnout, psychological well-being, and self-rated health. Overall, 28% reported at least one incident within the past year. Prevalence was higher among public sector employees, permanent staff, and employees with longer seniority. The most common forms were condescending or offensive messages and false accusations, typically eliciting irritation, intimidation, shock, or emotional exhaustion. Adjusting for gender, age, and seniority, baseline harassment was associated with higher burnout symptoms (β = 3.28, 95% CI 0.54–6.02) and higher odds of low self-rated health at follow-up (OR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.05–2.72), but not psychological well-being. These associations were attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for the respective baseline health outcome.

Article.Title: A personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated knee registration using single-plane moving fluoroscopy
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Li X.; Ćuković S.; Vogl F.; R. Taylor W.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAccurate knee joint kinematics are essential for biomechanical research and clinical assessment. Single-plane fluoroscopy is one of the most accurate tools for measuringin vivojoint motion, but manual estimation of three-dimensional bone pose from individual fluoroscopic frames remains labor-intensive and time-consuming. In this study, we present a personalized 2D/3D image registration pipeline for automated registration of knee fluoroscopic images acquired using single-plane moving fluoroscopy. The proposed framework combines pose standardization across acquisition sessions, subject-specific learning-based pose estimation, and differentiable-rendering-based pose refinement. Tested using fluoroscopic datasets of both natural knees and knee implants together with a PyTorch3D-based differentiable renderer, we trained subject-specific pose estimation networks for both anatomy types. Evaluation against manually matched reference poses showed mean initial in-plane translation differences of approximately 1.1–2.1 mm and geodesic rotation differences of 1.3–3.6$$^\circ$$with mask-only input, while out-of-plane translation differences remained larger, as expected in single-plane imaging. Gradient-based refinement using gradient correlation coefficient (GCC) further reduced the disagreement with the manual reference poses, resulting in sub-millimetre in-plane translation differences and sub-degree rotational differences, with over 95% of test frames satisfying the predefined success criterion that both the femoral and tibial registrations had absolute in-plane translation differences below 1 mm in both$$T_x$$and$$T_y$$and a geodesic rotation difference below 1$$^\circ$$. These results quantify agreement with the existing manual registration workflow rather than independently validated anatomical pose accuracy.

Article.Title: Dual fear mechanisms shaping stochastic population dynamics under the Allee effect
Article.Authors: Gültekin Ö.; Muradli M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTraditional population models that include predator–prey interactions attribute demographic changes directly to predation-related effects. However, predator-induced fear in prey has increasingly been recognised as an important factor shaping population dynamics. In this study, we propose a cubic population model in which fear acts through two distinct functional channels for a single-species population exhibiting the Allee effect. In this model, fear reduces the intrinsic growth rate through a multiplicative suppression mechanism while also playing an integrated role in modulating the growth and interaction dynamics by rescaling the saturation structure of the Holling type III interaction term. The stochastic extension of the model is described by a Langevin formalism containing correlated additive and multiplicative Gaussian noise, and the steady state probability distribution (SSPD) is analytically obtained using the corresponding Fokker–Planck equation. The analytical solution is validated by numerical simulations. The SSPD reveals both noise-induced transitions and fear-controlled regime changes between low- and high-density states, with the dual-channel structure producing structural competition and non-monotonic changes in the distribution. These are analysed through phenomenological bifurcation (P-bifurcation) diagrams and three-dimensional distribution surfaces. Additionally, statistical properties, parameter sensitivity, and escape dynamics are investigated through normalised moments, Fisher information, and mean first-passage time (MFPT) calculations. Notably, our model treats fear as an independent control parameter and provides a theoretical mechanism capable of generating qualitatively contrasting population responses across parameter regimes, while also offering a framework for examining critical transition dynamics of potential relevance to conservation and management.

Article.Title: Repeatability of upper limb volume measurements based on the Kuhnke measurement protocol and frustum volume calculation in women after unilateral mastectomy: a cross-sectional methodological study
Article.Authors: Smoter M.; Roczniok R.; Muracki J.; Maliszewski D.; Tarkowski R.; Trybulski R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe aim of this study was to assess the repeatability of upper limb volume measurements performed with the Kuhnke method using the Frustum Volume Calculation (FVC) in women with lymphedema after unilateral mastectomy. This cross-sectional methodological study included 101 women (stage I: n = 52; stage II: n = 49). Three independent physiotherapists, each with at least five years of clinical experience, performed two repeated measurements (T1, T2) of both the affected and the healthy limb using the Kuhnke FVC method. Repeatability was evaluated with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), standard error of measurement (SEM), and minimal detectable change (MDC). The mean volume of the healthy limb was ~ 2209–2210 ml, while the affected limb averaged ~ 2438–2440 ml, yielding a mean interlimb difference of 229–230 ml. Intra-rater reliability was excellent, with ICC values of 0.986 for the healthy limb, 0.983 for the affected limb, and 0.945 for the interlimb difference. SEM values ranged from 6 to 8 ml, and MDC values were 16–22 ml, indicating very low measurement error. Inter-rater analysis confirmed high agreement, with no statistically significant differences between raters (p≈0.99). The interlimb volume difference was more than twice as large in stage II lymphedema (314.7 ± 67.1 ml) compared with stage I (148.6 ± 38.7 ml; p < 0.000001). The Kuhnke method with FVC formula demonstrates excellent intra- and inter-rater repeatability and can be recommended as a simple, cost-effective, and clinically reliable tool for diagnosing and monitoring upper limb lymphedema in women after mastectomy.

Article.Title: High-throughput screen identifies metabolite regulators of endothelial function
Article.Authors: Oliveira F.; Bondareva O.; Hoffmann A.; Geier F.; Kyselova A.; Karantanou C.; Bibli S.; Sheikh B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractEndothelial cells (ECs) line blood vessels, regulate organ homeostasis, and their dysfunction is central to the development of cardiovascular diseases. Metabolites are critical regulators of EC health and function, yet only a limited number of metabolites that impact ECs have been identified. Here, we undertook a high-throughput screen of 884 metabolites and common drugs found in human biofluids to systematically identify compounds that impact barrier function in primary human umbilical vein ECs (HUVECs). Seven metabolites that deregulate vascular barrier function without causing cell death were shortlisted. These include (-)-epigallocatechin gallate, (±)-3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid, taurocholic acid, myricetin, meloxicam, hesperetin and trans-3-indoleacrylic acid. These metabolites elicited differential effects on HUVECs, coronary artery ECs and pulmonary ECs. Transcriptional profiling revealed that each of the seven metabolites triggered distinct transcriptional responses in ECs, suggesting distinct mechanisms triggering EC barrier disruption. Notably, trans-3-indoleacrylic acid deregulated VE-cadherin junctions and increased EC sprouting, suggesting a potential role in angiogenesis. Together, these results provide a screening resource for metabolite-endothelial interactions and identify candidate circulating metabolites that regulate endothelial function.

Article.Title: Exploring the potential of distributed acoustic sensing for fish bioacoustics
Article.Authors: Eceiza A.; Sladen A.; Brunel O.; Bonnet N.; Gaglio V.; Simonet R.; Mittaine F.; Cottalorda J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUnderwater soundscapes are critical indicators of marine ecosystem health, but traditional passive acoustic monitoring with hydrophones is spatially limited and logistically challenging for long-term observations. This study investigates the potential of distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) to overcome these limitations. A field trial was conducted using a bespoke fiber-optic cable deployed off the coast of Monaco, focusing on three sound-producing Mediterranean species:Ophidion rochei,Sciaena umbra, andEpinephelus marginatus, all known for their distinct acoustic signatures. DAS recordings reveal species-specific patterns consistent with documented behaviors, and are validated by co-located hydrophone recordings. Due to its high sensor density, DAS allows the isolation and localization of individual sounds over tens of meters. The results demonstrate that DAS can detect and locate fish sounds under real-world conditions, while also assessing ambient noise levels. The DAS setup in this experiment may not match the performance of conventional hydrophones, but the approach’s potential for dense, continuous, and low-maintenance monitoring, particularly where suitable fiber-optic infrastructure already exists, points to a promising complementary role in marine conservation in the context of climate change and biodiversity loss.

Article.Title: Nano route with DFT, docking studies, ADMET, and SAR of a pyran-functionalized pyrimidine scaffold as a potent Rhizoctonia solani
Article.Authors: Farag B.; El-Bana G.; El-Lateef H.; Bouachrine M.; El-Sayed A.; Saeed A.; Fouad M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractNumerous plant infections known as phytopathogenic fungi are responsible for a broad range of agricultural illnesses. Recent research focuses on developing, synthesizing, and evaluating pyran-linked pyrimidine hybrids as potential antifungals. In this study, the target hybrids of the pyran-functionalized pyrimidine scaffold were optimized synthesized using nanoscience-based techniques. A multi-step process involving nucleophilic substitution reaction, cyclization, acetylation, hydrolysis, condensation, and Dimroth rearrangement afforded pyran-pyrimidine hybrids 1–7. In this study, the antifungal potency of optimized synthesized compounds (3, 5, and 6) against various therapeutic targets of the phytopathogenic fungusRhizoctonia solaniwas assessed using a thorough computational approach. Investigated hybrids, especially 3, 5, and 6 at 20 ppm and 50 ppm, exhibited strong resistance to the fungusRhizoctonia solani, representing a potential antifungal control against soil-borne plant pathogens. Molecular docking analyses revealed these compounds exhibit potent, multi-target binding affinities, frequently outperforming the reference drug fluconazole, particularly against sterol-14-alpha-demethylase, chitin synthase, cellulose synthase, and cytochrome bc1. Simulations involving molecular dynamics and MM-GBSA (Molecular Mechanics/Generalized Born Surface Area)/PBSA (Poisson-Boltzmann Surface Area) free energy computations over trajectories for compound3confirmed the formation of highly stable and dynamically viable complexes. Pharmacokinetically and according to ADMET assessments, tested hybrids comply with accepted drug-likeness rules (Lipinski, Pfizer, and Golden Triangle) and present minimal risk of cytochrome P450 inhibition. According to findings of computational analyses that confirmed fungal potency evaluation, optimized synthesized compounds are promising bioactive candidates for developing effective fungicides. This study is the first to compare the protective effects of pyran-functionalized pyrimidine againstRhizoctonia solanisupported by computational analyses.

Article.Title: Development and validation of the eHealth literacy scale for college students aged 18-24 years, Faridabad, India
Article.Authors: Haldar P.; Jeer G.; Kant S.; Malhotra S.; Dwivedi S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Internet is commonly used source of health information all over the world. Despite this availability, many people doesn’t have ability to use this health information for their benefit. This ability depends on eHealth literacy’s underlying concept, which is the ability to seek, find, understand, and appraise health information from electronic resources and apply that knowledge in making a health-related decision. There is no studies on eHealth literacy among college students in India who frequently use the internet to access health-related information. The present study was conducted to develop and validate an eHealth literacy scale for college students. The initial phase of the study focuses on developing items from literature review and focus group discussions (FGD) and also on assessing the face and content validity of items through content validity index(CVI). The next three phases focused on design validation, factor analysis, and reliability of newly developed scale among 163 college students. Exploratory factor analysis used to assess construct validity. The internal consistency reliability was measured using Cronbach’s alpha. The tool, which began as a 30-item draft, was gradually reshaped through a series of modifications. A total of 163 participants (81 boys; 82 girls) aged 18 to 24 (mean = 21.21; SD = 1.64) completed the survey. Parallel analysis and exploratory factor analysis supported a five-factor solution (eigenvalues ranging from 2.428 to 1.269), which aligned with our conceptual domains of eHealth Literacy. Retained items demonstrated salient factor loadings (> 0.30). Cronbach’s alpha value of scale came to be 0.75. A 21-item, comprehensive eHealth Literacy scale structured across five distinct factors for college students was developed. The scale demonstrated acceptable overall internal consistency and preliminary evidence of construct validity. Further validation using larger, independent samples is required to confirm the factor structure.

Article.Title: Imbalance-robust predictive maintenance using deep learning with virtual measurement modeling and explainable AI
Article.Authors: Eldeeb O.; Aboutabl A.; Bahloul M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPredictive maintenance (PdM) has become a key enabler of intelligent industrial systems; however, its effectiveness is often constrained by measurement uncertainty, the absence of raw sensor signals, and severe class imbalance between normal and failure events. This paper proposes a measurement-aware predictive maintenance framework that utilizes operational variables as virtual measurement proxies, enabling measurement-oriented analysis without requiring raw sensor signals. Using the AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance Dataset, the proposed framework integrates a hybrid imbalance-handling strategy that combines Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) and cost-sensitive learning to improve failure detection under highly imbalanced conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid framework consistently outperforms the baseline, the SMOTE-only configuration, and the cost-sensitive configuration. Among the evaluated classifiers, LightGBM achieved the best overall performance with an F1-score of 0.9043, followed by DNN (0.8708) and XGBoost (0.8680). SHAP-based explainability analysis identified tool wear and torque as the most influential predictors of machine failure. At the same time, robustness experiments with simulated Gaussian measurement noise demonstrated stable performance across low and moderate noise levels. An ablation study further confirmed the complementary contributions of SMOTE and cost-sensitive learning. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective and interpretable approach for predictive maintenance on the AI4I 2020 benchmark dataset, while further validation using real industrial datasets is required before practical deployment.

Article.Title: Serum metabolomic signatures associated with growth hormone replacement therapy in children with postoperative craniopharyngioma
Article.Authors: Xu R.; Du H.; Zhang L.; Song S.; Chen S.; Duan L.; Zhu H.; Pan H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGrowth hormone replacement therapy (GHRT) is commonly used to treat growth hormone deficiency (GHD) after craniopharyngioma (CP) surgery, but its metabolic consequences in pediatric patients remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to investigate serum metabolomic alterations associated with GHRT in pediatric patients with postoperative childhood-onset CP. We conducted an untargeted serum metabolomics study in 60 pediatric patients with childhood-onset CP following surgery, including 32 patients receiving GHRT and 28 patients not receiving GHRT. Clinical data and biochemical parameters were collected. Serum metabolites were profiled using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Differential metabolite identification, pathway enrichment analysis, and correlation analyses were conducted to characterize GHRT-associated metabolic signatures and their relationships with clinical indicators. Patients receiving GHRT had higher insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) levels, whereas conventional lipid parameters did not differ significantly between groups. HOMA-IR was higher and QUICKI was lower in the GHRT group. Using stringent criteria of VIP > 1, BH-FDR q < 0.05, and |log₂FC| > 2, 10 key positive-ion metabolites were identified, including phosphatidylcholine, triglycerides, sphingomyelins (SMs), and 3,5-diiodo-L-thyronine (T2). Nine lipid-related metabolites were higher and T2 was lower in the GHRT group. These associations remained significant after adjustment for chronological age and postoperative interval and in sensitivity analyses additionally accounting for sex-steroid replacement. GHRT exposure in children and adolescents with postoperative childhood-onset CP was associated with distinct serum metabolomic signatures, predominantly involving phosphatidylcholine, triglycerides, and SMs. These findings represent exploratory associations and require confirmation in longitudinal studies before treatment-related or clinical implications can be established.

Article.Title: Respiration–action coupling and intentional binding in a Libet clock paradigm
Article.Authors: Shibata H.; Patchitt J.; Nagai Y.; Mizuhara K.; Critchley H.; Ohira H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractInteroception, the physiological sensing of internal bodily states, has been proposed to contribute to the sense of self. However, empirical research that directly investigates interoceptive contributions to the sense of agency remains limited. Based on the observed synchronisation between respiratory phase and the initiation of voluntary action, we implemented the Libet clock task to test the hypothesis that the respiratory phase would modulate intentional binding (IB), a temporal binding phenomenon often used as an implicit measure related to agency. Additionally, we aimed to replicate respiration–action synchronisation and to examine exploratory cardiac-phase effects on binding. The overall key-binding effect was small and did not reach statistical significance, whereas tone binding was significant. Neither key nor tone binding showed reliable respiratory-phase modulation, although respiration–action synchronisation was replicated. Bayesian model comparisons strongly favoured models in which binding did not vary with respiratory phase. For cardiac phase, a frequentist mixed-effects model suggested phase-dependent modulation of key binding, but Bayesian model comparison did not support including cardiac-phase interactions. Together, these findings show that respiration–action coupling was present in the task but was not accompanied by detectable respiratory-phase modulation of intentional binding; the cardiac finding should be considered exploratory.

Article.Title: Characterization of the gut microbiota in older adults with vascular stiffness
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Lu Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractVascular stiffness is a hallmark of vascular aging and a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases in older adults. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may contribute to vascular dysfunction; however, the microbial characteristics associated with vascular stiffness remain insufficiently understood. This cross-sectional study included older adults with and without vascular stiffness. A total of 110 adults aged ≥ 60 years were recruited from nursing homes and categorized into the vascular stiffness group (baPWV ≥ 1800 cm/s, VG,n= 91) and a non–vascular stiffness group (baPWV < 1800 cm/s, CG,n= 19). Fecal samples were analyzed using shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the BGI DNBSEQ platform. Microbial composition, α-diversity, and functional profiles were characterized, and differential taxa and their associations with vascular stiffness-related parameters were evaluated. VG exhibited significantly higher abundances ofDeltaproteobacteria,Desulfovibrionales,Rikenellaceae,Desulfovibrionaceae, and the generaAlistipes,Ruthenibacterium, andEisenbergiella(P< 0.05). In contrast,Holdemanella biformisandVeillonella tobetsuensiswere enriched in CG (LDA score > 2). Functional pathway analysis revealed significant upregulation of lipid metabolism and betalain biosynthesis pathways in VG. Correlation analysis showed thatAlistipes putrediniswas positively associated with SBP, whereasVeillonella tobetsuensiswas negatively associated with baPWV (P< 0.05). Older adults with vascular stiffness exhibited distinct alterations in gut microbiota composition and functional profiles compared with non-affected controls. Although several microbial taxa were differentially abundant between groups, these associations were attenuated after adjustment for age, sex, and lipid profiles, suggesting that individual microbial taxa may be influenced by host aging and metabolic status. These findings indicate that vascular stiffness-associated gut microbiota alterations are more likely to reflect broader changes in microbial community structure and function rather than the independent effects of specific microbial taxa (Ethics committee: 2020082 H).

Article.Title: Phenotypic and molecular characterization of INPP5K-related congenital muscular dystrophy in four Egyptian patients
Article.Authors: Zaki M.; Abdel-Ghafar S.; Rafat K.; Elbendary H.; ElKhayat S.; Saleh D.; Gleeson J.; Abdel-Salam G.; Abdel-Hamid M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractINPP5K-related congenital muscular dystrophy is an ultra-rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by variable combinations of early-onset cataracts, proximal muscle weakness, elevated serum creatine kinase, and intellectual disability. To date, about 31 affected individuals have been reported worldwide, and the clinical and molecular spectrum of the disorder remains incompletely defined. Herein, we describe four patients from three unrelated consanguineous Egyptian families. All patients presented with hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, microcephaly, waddling gait, elevated serum creatine kinase, and mild intellectual disability. Cataracts were identified in only two patients, highlighting the incomplete penetrance of this hallmark feature. Brain MRI was normal in two patients whereas mild asymmetry of the lateral ventricles and thin corpus callosum were identified in the remaining two patients. Axonal neuropathy and delayed puberty, features infrequently reported inINPP5K-related disease, were also observed in our cohort. Exome sequencing identified three homozygousINPP5Kvariants, including the recurrent p.(Ile50Thr) and two previously unreported missense variants: p.(Arg234Pro) within the catalytic 5-phosphatase domain and p.(Tyr349Ser) within the C-terminal SKICH domain. Both variants affected highly conserved residues, were absent from public population databases, and consistently predicted to be deleterious by multiple in-silico tools and protein structural modeling analyses. Our findings refine both the clinical and molecular spectrum ofINPP5K-related muscular dystrophy and present the first report from Egypt and North Africa. In addition, the identification of variants affecting both major functional domains of the protein further supports the marked molecular and phenotypic heterogeneity associated with INPP5K deficiency.

Article.Title: Effect of herbal toothpaste versus conventional one on black stains in a group of Egyptian children: a randomized controlled study
Article.Authors: Rashed M.; Zaki Z.; Zeidan H.; Hashish A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTo determine the recurrence rate of Black Stain (BS) in children using herbal versus fluoridated toothpaste formulations, in terms of stain recurrence, stain score, and parental satisfaction. Twenty- eight children with BS were randomly allocated into two groups: Control group I received a fluoridated toothpaste (Signal Cavity Fighter™), and experimental group II received an herbal toothpaste (Dabur Red™). Following dental polishing and salivary sample collection, the levels of four bacterial species—Streptococcus mutans(SM),Lactobacillus casei(LB),Actinomyces naeslundii(AC), andPrevotella melaninogenica(PM), were measured utilizing quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). Both groups were evaluated for changes in stain score, percentage reduction in bacterial load, and degree of parental satisfaction. After 6 months, 85.7% of participants in the herbal group were significantly free from stain recurrence (p = 0.013, ω = 0.53; large effect size), achieved a stain score of 0 (p = 0.004, ω = 0.38; small effect size), and reported a satisfaction score of 5 (p = 0.008, δ = − 0.51; large effect size) compared with the control group. With regard to bacterial counts, the reduction in SM was significantly greater in the control group, whereas reductions in the other bacterial species were significantly greater in the herbal group, all with large effect sizes. Within the limitations of this study, herbal toothpaste may demonstrate promising efficacy in stain removal in terms of improving parental satisfaction, reducing stain recurrence and all included bacteria except SM in comparison to the control group.Trial registration:This study was registered retrospectively on Clinical Trials. gov on 03/06/2025 as first posted date before any outcome assessment; ID: NCT06872827;https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06872827.

Article.Title: Machine learning prediction and analysis of area-averaged external pressure coefficients for low-rise dual-slope building roofs in a uniform turbulent flow field
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Fu Y.; Yuan Y.; Duan H.; Wang J.; Yang I.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAccurate prediction of roof area-averaged external pressure coefficients ($${\overline{C}}_{p,A}$$) is crucial for low-rise building design. To isolate geometric and turbulence effects from atmospheric wind shear, wind tunnel experiments were conducted under uniform turbulent flow conditions covering roof pitch angles (0°–30°), wind directions, and turbulence intensities. To overcome the smoothing limitations of conventional regression methods, an ensemble learning framework (Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM) was developed and evaluated using a rigorous Leave-One-Slope-Out (LOSO) cross-validation strategy. Results show that around the roof pitch angle ofα= 18.4°, a pronounced variation in aerodynamic pressure response occurs under oblique wind conditions. XGBoost maintains robust predictive performance, outperforming conventional response surface modeling under nonlinear transition conditions. Furthermore, extrapolation failure atα= 30° delineates the practical limits of data-driven models in predicting unseen aerodynamic regimes. Finally, SHAP analysis demonstrates that the model-derived feature attribution patterns are generally consistent with previously reported aerodynamic observations, providing a physically interpretable framework for wind load prediction under complex flow transitions.

Article.Title: Multi-parametric quantitative ultrasound imaging evaluation of rat sciatic nerve regeneration
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Pan K.; Cheng X.; Orozco E.; Han A.; Andre M.; Chang E.; Shah S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPeripheral nerve injury is a prevalent condition that significantly impairs patients' sensorimotor function. Noninvasive monitoring of peripheral nerve regeneration could serve as a valuable clinical tool for improving the timing and effectiveness of surgical interventions. We present a multiparametric high-frequency quantitative ultrasound evaluation to noninvasively track temporal and spatial peripheral nerve regeneration following early (n = 16) and delayed (n = 15) graft-based repair of rat sciatic nerve gaps, compared with a sham control group (n = 8). Multiple ultrasound parameters—including backscatter coefficient (BSC) spectra-based measurements (integrated BSC and midband fitted slope), homodyned K envelope statistics (μ and$$\kappa $$), gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features, and B-mode morphological measurements were acquired using a Vevo MD UHF 48 transducer at proximal, intra-graft, and distal nerve locations at 1, 2, and 3 months post-repair. Four sciatic nerve samples were extracted after each time point from each experimental group. A histological grading scheme was applied to classify nerve sections into mild, moderate, and severe pathological grades. Principal component analysis (PCA) combined with support vector machine (SVM) classification was employed to establish decision boundaries among pathological groups. Four parameters (μ, cross-sectional area, normalized integrated BSC, midband fitted slope) significantly differentiated groups with varying pathological severity. PCA-SVM analysis achieved excellent classification performance with an area under the ROC curve of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.85 for distinguishing minimal versus severe pathological injured nerves. These findings demonstrate that multiparametric quantitative ultrasound (qUS) effectively characterizes nerve pathologies by integrating complementary information about microstructural changes across different structural scales, potentially offering a comprehensive, noninvasive assessment of the regenerative microenvironment.

Article.Title: Paternal early-life stress and diet influence sperm DNA methylation, female offspring behavior and amygdala transcription
Article.Authors: Yadid T.; Kisliouk T.; Ramaty M.; Weller A.; Meiri N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractObesity is a global epidemic influenced by stress-related experiences during development, which can program behavioral traits, with the amygdala playing a central role in stress regulation. These programmed effects may be inherited through epigenetic mechanisms. Here, we examined the impact of paternal early-life stress (ELS), alone or combined with a high-fat diet (HFD), on offspring behavior and gene regulation. Male Wistar rats underwent maternal separation to induce ELS, followed by elevated plus maze (EPM) testing and exposure to either HFD or standard chow. These males were bred with naïve females, and F1offspring were raised under standard conditions. Amygdala tissue and sperm were collected; RNA from paternal and offspring amygdalae was deep-sequenced, and sperm DNA was analyzed using Reduced Representation Bisulfite Deep Sequencing (RRBS). Paternal exposure to ELS and HFD independently and jointly altered physiology and behavior in F1female offspring. Offspring of ELS fathers showed increased exploratory behavior and mobility in the EPM; paternal HFD increased time spent in open arms. In the paternal amygdala, ELS and HFD induced distinct gene expression changes. Sperm methylation analysis revealed many differentially methylated genes, some overlapping with transcriptional changes in the F1female amygdala, consistent with a potential role for epigenetic inheritance. Overlapping expression patterns in F0and F1included genes involved in dopamine signaling and epigenetic regulation. Notably, the imprinted gene GRB10 showed increased promoter methylation in sperm and reduced expression in both paternal and offspring amygdala, validated by immunostaining. These findings suggest that paternal ELS and HFD shape offspring phenotype through heritable epigenetic modifications.

Article.Title: A dual-stage self-attention hybrid convolutional neural network-gated recurrent unit architecture for real-time power quality disturbance diagnosis
Article.Authors: Samanta I.; Sahoo B.; Rout P.; Mohanty S.; Jha S.; Swain K.; Cherukuri M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe increased adoption of the smart grid (SG) infrastructure to overcome the limitations of traditional grid have faced growing challenges for real-time monitoring and classification of features due to the complexity and dynamic nature of power quality disturbances (PQDs). In particular, when PQDs overlap each other, traditional approaches relying on signal processing techniques tend to lose the dynamic, non-periodic characteristics which define certain PQDs. In this proposed work, a novel dual-stage hybrid architecture based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and gated recurrent units (GRUs) augmented by self-attention at both stages for real-time high performance PQD classification is presented. This novel hybrid architecture is allows for spatial and temporal feature extraction from electrical power signals, overcoming the weaknesses encountered in traditional approaches. In contrast to previous models that consider either local or sequential patterns independently, the proposed architecture combines both techniques enabling a more robust and computationally-efficient architecture demonstrates software-level real-time inference (21 ms) and provides a computationally efficient architecture suitable for future embedded deployment. The experimental outcomes on the benchmark databases compared to the state-of-the-art convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) architecture offers improved execution time of 21 ms and a classification accuracy of 98.6%. It also outperforms both traditional CNN architecture with improved latency and high accuracy proposing it as a viable alternative for smart grid use cases like phasor measurement units (PMUs), microcontroller-based devices, etc.

Article.Title: A method for predicting tool remaining useful life based on a physics-informed neural network
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Shen L.; Ye Z.; Chen J.; Luo K.; Chen W.; Li S.; He R.; Han Q.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN)-based method for tool remaining useful life (RUL) prediction by incorporating physical wear evolution laws into a data-driven prediction framework. The method improves prediction accuracy and enhances cross-scenario adaptability through consistency with tool wear mechanisms. First, a quantitative mapping model between tool RUL and flank wear is established based on tool wear theory, clarifying the mathematical relationship between the tool degradation state and its RUL. A PINN is then constructed by embedding the wear rate derived from the Archard wear equation as a physical constraint in the loss function. A hybrid loss function integrating data-driven and physics-informed terms is designed, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based time-series prediction model is developed. The method is validated using the PHM2010 dataset, including comparative tests on labeled sub-datasetsD1,D4, andD6against multiple baseline methods, as well as generalization tests on unlabeled sub-datasetsD2,D3, andD5. The results show that the proposed method achieves a Mean Absolute Error of 4.25 μm and a Root Mean Square Error of 4.83 μm on the test dataset, reducing MAE by 57.33% compared with Support Vector Machine and by 37.13% compared with Convolutional Neural Network. The end-of-life prediction deviation rate under the same working conditions is 2.46%, and the model shows reliable generalization ability on unlabeled data. It should be noted that, in the current implementation, the wear coefficientkin the Archard constraint is fixed to a handbook value and treated as a constant during training; online adaptive estimation ofkis left to future work. These results provide a physically interpretable technical approach for intelligent tool health management and maintenance decision-making.

Article.Title: Multifunctional marine polymers composite supplemented with Artemisia absinthium emulsion for improving chronic wound healing: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Gaspar-Pintiliescu A.; Seciu-Grama A.; Plangu A.; Manoiu V.; Râpă M.; Serafim A.; Tomescu J.; Craciunescu O.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe aim of this study was to develop a 3D multifunctional porous composite based on marine polymers, fish collagen (COL) extracted fromDicentrarchus labraxskin and sulfated polysaccharides (SP) extracted fromCladophora vagabundaseaweed, supplemented with wormwood (Artemisia absinthium) emulsion (WE) for improving the healing of chronic wounds. Characterization of the submicron WE based on wormwood hydrolate showed spherical droplets by TEM, Z-average diameter of 21.31 nm and negative zeta potential determined by DLS and antimicrobial activity againstStaphylococcus aureus.The 3D COL-SP-WE composite revealed porous morphology by SEM, and a gradual stress increase characteristic for a soft network capable of sustaining medium loads before deformation. The composite had good cytocompatibility in human HaCaT keratinocytes culture. In addition, supplementation of marine composite COL-SP with WE demonstrated higher decrease of the intracellular ROS production in oxidative stressed HaCaT cells, reduced level of pro-inflammatory cytokines in inflamed human THP-1-derived macrophage cells, and downregulation of matrix metalloproteinases mRNAs expression and secretion level in a HaCaT/THP-1 co-culture. However, WE supplementation did not significantly improve HaCaT migration rate in a scratch assay. All these results highlighted multifunctionality of marine composite COL-SP supplemented with WE and recommend further in vivo testing in relevant wound healing models.

Article.Title: Optimal hybrid PV-PTC integration with existing hydropower for reliable and cost-effective energy supply
Article.Authors: Ahmadullah A.; Faizi M.; Bourezgui A.; Ali E.; Elazim S.; Irshad A.; Muslih N.; Ghazouani N.; Senjyu T.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis study investigates the integration of existing hydropower with photovoltaic (PV), parabolic trough collector (PTC), and hybrid PV-PTC systems to achieve zero loss of power supply probability (LPSP), minimum levelized cost of energy (LCOE), and near-complete hydropower utilization (remaining ≤ 0.05%). An 8760-hour simulation and coarse-to-fine parametric optimization framework are employed to evaluate system reliability, renewable-energy utilization, curtailment, and economic performance. The PV-based system requires 177.48 MW, utilizes 289.90 GWh of PV energy, exhibits 7.88% curtailment, and achieves an LCOE of 0.090576 $/kWh. The PTC-based system requires 143.36 MW, utilizes 289.96 GWh, reduces curtailment to 4.05%, and achieves an LCOE of 0.087199 $/kWh. The optimal hybrid configuration comprises 52,000 PV units (12.43 MW) and 724 PTC units (131.88 MW), achieving zero unmet load and utilizing 696.160178 GWh of hydropower with only 0.00026% remaining. It supplies 22.05 GWh from PV with zero curtailment and 267.85 GWh from PTC with 3.66% PTC curtailment, while achieving the lowest baseline LCOE of 0.087156 $/kWh. Sensitivity analysis shows that the economic advantage over the PTC-only system is marginal and dependent mainly on PV and PTC investment costs. Overall, the hybrid configuration provides the most balanced technical performance through high reliability, reduced renewable curtailment, and effective utilization of the existing hydropower resource.

Article.Title: Effects of deposition parameters and cobalt hexacyanocobaltate surface modification on magnetron-sputtered ZnIn₂S₄ thin film photoanodes
Article.Authors: Roda D.; Trzciński K.; Sawczak M.; Ilnicka A.; Szkoda M.; Nowak A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractFor the first time, ZnIn₂S₄ (ZIS) thin films were successfully prepared by magnetron sputtering and systematically investigated as photoanodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. The PEC performance of the layers strongly depended on the deposition parameters. The highest photocurrent density of 2.77 mA cm⁻² at 1.62 V vs. RHE was achieved for films deposited at 200 °C for 90 min, whereas films deposited at 300 °C for 90 min exhibited improved stability. The optimized ZIS photoanode was subsequently modified with a cobalt hexacyanocobaltate (Cohcc) surface layer formed via electrooxidation of a Co layer in an electrolyte containing Co(CN)₆³⁻. This surface modification improved photoanode performance, particularly in terms of stability, likely due to enhanced oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics at the electrode surface. Cohcc-modified photoanode generated almost 3 times higher photocurrent density after 100 s operation compared to unmodified photoanode. Electrochemical measurements performed under dark conditions further confirmed the role of Cohcc as cocatalyst toward OER. Overall, the results demonstrate that magnetron sputtering enables effective control over the properties of ZIS photoanodes through optimization of deposition parameters, while surface modification with cobalt hexacyanocobaltate represents a viable strategy for tuning interfacial kinetics and improving the functional performance of ZIS-based photoanodes.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal analysis of land use change in the Eastern Slopes of the Jerusalem Area
Article.Authors: Muhsen M.; Elhannani M.; Almanasra A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUrban expansion is one of the main drivers of land use changes in the Central Palestinian Mountains. It influences the basic environmental components, including water, soil, and specifically vegetation cover. In the present study, the study area has experienced noticeable land use changes over the past three decades, resulting in many adverse impacts on the environment. This study aims to examine land use changes and identify the main drivers and consequences of these changes on vegetation cover during the period 1997 and 2022. Spatiotemporal analysis is used to quantify land use changes using the GIS tool and fieldwork methods to study vegetation cover. Findings have revealed significant changes in the land use over the study period. The total area of rangeland and grassland has decreased 12.2%, while the total area of urban fabric has increased 7% due to Israeli activities and 5.2% due to the expansion of Palestinian built-up areas, at the expense of rangeland and grassland. Additionally, the environmental impact on vegetation cover has been evidenced by an increase in the number and density of unpalatable and invasive plants, in contrast to the degradation in the number, density, and diversity of palatable plants. Consequently, the conversion of land use reduces the area of land available for livestock grazing. The natural landscape has become highly converted to an urban landscape pattern as a result of the rapid increase in urban areas. In response to these results, more efforts must be imposed to enforce strict land use control and management to slow down environmental degradation.

Article.Title: Hybrid GA-DQN for opportunistic cluster head selection and routing in resource constraint Internet of Things networks
Article.Authors: Thalaimalaichamy M.; Baskaradas J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractEnergy efficiency and reliable data transmission are two important challenges in Internet of Things (IoT) networks because of the limited energy resources of sensor nodes and their dynamic nature. Accordingly, this research develops a Genetic Algorithm Deep Q-Network (GA-DQN) based hybrid framework for intelligent cluster head selection and adaptive IoT Network routing to counter these threats. A Genetic Algorithm (GA) selects the best cluster heads based on residual energy, coverage ratio, inter-cluster distance, and node density. In turn, this ensures balanced cluster formation and efficient energy utilisation. Next, the Deep Q-Network (DQN) learns the forwarding decision from a network state, including the node’s energy level, node location, information of a neighbour node, link quality, and distance to the sink. The reward mechanism has been formulated to reduce energy consumption, enhance communication reliability, and optimise routing efficiency. The results show over a 100 m × 100 m field containing 100 nodes shows that the proposed framework postpones the first node death to approximately 700 rounds and the half-node death to approximately 4200 rounds, against 550–600 and 2200–3000 rounds respectively for EERRL, ICR-HHODRL and CGA-GWO, so that the overall network lifetime increases by 7.69%, 2.94% and 1.45% with respect to the same baselines. Average energy consumption per node falls to 0.18 J from 0.28 J, 0.30 J and 0.35 J, the average packet delay falls to 3 × 10⁻³ s, a reduction of 25.0%, 33.3% and 40.0%, and the end-to-end latency falls to 0.24 s, a reduction of 29.4%, 36.8% and 42.9%. Notwithstanding a lower peak per-round throughput of 1.7 × 10⁵ bits against 2.6 × 10⁵ to 3.5 × 10⁵ bits for the baselines, delivery is sustained beyond 6000 rounds, whereas the throughput of the baseline’s decays to a residual level within approximately 2500 rounds. A scalability campaign spanning 50 to 200 nodes in fields of 50 m × 50 m to 200 m × 200 m extends the last node death from 5385 to 15,763 rounds without any modification of the learning architecture. These results confirm that GA-based cluster optimisation combined with DQN-based adaptive routing balances energy expenditure and sustains data delivery in the IoT network.

Article.Title: Uptake of sickle cell screening among sexually active unmarried young adults in Gulu City, northern Uganda: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Bwamiki D.; Okema J.; Lunyuta S.; Opaci I.; Abor M.; Acomo G.; Obal R.; Pitua I.; Bongomin F.; Akello F.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSickle cell disease (SCD) is a major public health challenge in Uganda, where up to 20% of the population in northern regions carry the sickle cell trait (SCT). We conducted a community-based cross-sectional study among 321 sexually active unmarried young adults aged 15–35 years in Pece-Laroo Division, Gulu City, to determine the prevalence and predictors of sickle cell screening uptake. Participants were enrolled through stratified random sampling and data collected using a pre-tested interviewer-administered questionnaire; modified Poisson regression with robust standard errors was used for analysis. The median age was 21 years [IQR: 18–24]. Overall, 85 participants (26.5%) had ever undergone sickle cell screening. Favorable knowledge-scale scores were recorded for 176 (54.8%) and positive attitude-scale scores for 178 (55.5%) participants. Tertiary education was the sole independent predictor of screening uptake (adjusted prevalence ratio 2.89; 95% CI 1.98–4.21;p< 0.001). The most commonly cited barrier was lack of awareness of where to access screening services (52.1%). Despite critically low uptake, 78.0% of unscreened participants intended to be screened in the future. Structural barriers rather than individual awareness alone constrain health-seeking behavior. Youth-targeted education campaigns, integration of screening into community health services, and stigma reduction are urgently needed.
