Article.Title: Simultaneous fermentation of beetroot juice and pulp with water kefir grain – a sustainable approach for zero waste
Article.Authors: Jaeger A.; Sahin A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractReducing food waste represents a challenge in the transformation of our food system towards sustainable practices. Amongst these losses are nutritious by-products, like vegetable pulp during juicing. A simultaneous fermentation of beetroot juice and pulp was performed using water kefir grains, a consortium of lactic acid bacteria (LAB), acetic acid bacteria (AAB), and yeast (Y), to transform waste (pulp) into value (ingredient) with fermented juice as a valuable ready-to-drink by-product. During fermentation an increase in LAB-, AAB-, and Y-cell count occurred, indicating the suitability of beetroot as a substrate. The pH decreased from 5.78 to 3.89 in beetroot juice, and from 5.35 to 4.35 in beetroot pulp. The TTA increased by 9.87 ml 0.1 M NaOH in juice and by 6.47 ml in pulp. Fermented beetroot juice retained its high foaming capacity (108–114%) but showed reduced foam stability (-49%). Total polyphenol content (TPC) slightly decreased. Pulp showed stable foam stability up to 48 h of fermentation followed by a decline. Water- and oil-holding capacity of pulp increased, and TPC was elevated. The outcome of this study demonstrate that simultaneous fermentation of juice and pulp using water kefir grains is a suitable process to reduce waste by using minimal resources and time.

Article.Title: Distribution of movable fluid and its influencing factors in super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs: a case study of Chang 6 member, Wuqi area, Ordos Basin
Article.Authors: Zhong H.; Yang Z.; Zhang Y.; Jia X.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe influences of multiple factors on movable fluid saturation remain inadequately constrained for continental tight sandstones. Moreover, comparative studies on the occurrence characteristics of movable fluids between tight sandstone reservoirs and super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs are relatively scarce. This research takes Chang 6 member in the Wuqi area as an example, and through a series of experiments, analyzes the distribution patterns and influencing factors of movable fluids. The results show that the super-low to ultra-low permeability sandstone reservoirs in this research have porosity values ranging from 8.78% to 16.12%, permeability values ranging from 0.094 mD to 2.453 mD, and the values of movable fluid saturation ranging from 31.38% to 62.67%. All the samples can be broadly divided into two types, type I samples have higher content of feldspar, more developed dissolved pores, and generally locate in middle part or top part of thicker sand bodies. For all the samples, permeability, peak pore-throat radius, and average pore-throat radius exhibit strong mutual correlations, which may be associated with the development of large pore-throats, and all show a strong correlation with movable fluid saturation. Although the movable fluid occurs in pore-throat with a wide size range, the development of micron pore-throats is the key factor influencing the values of movable fluid saturation, differentiating super-low to ultra-low permeability reservoirs and tight sandstone reservoirs.

Article.Title: Large-scale chromatin topological remodeling accompanies hepatocellular carcinoma progression
Article.Authors: Jiang F.; Zhang Z.; Chen Z.; Xu S.; Cai S.; Liu J.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMultistep hepatocarcinogenesis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is associated with dynamic alterations in chromatin topology. Previous studies have primarily compared three-dimensional (3D) genomic structure between tumor and normal adjacent tissues, largely overlooking the role of cirrhosis, a major precancerous lesion and risk factor in HCC pathogenesis. Here, we systematically analyzed chromatin conformation changes across paired tumor, cirrhotic, and normal adjacent tissues to identify stage-specific structural alterations during hepatocarcinogenesis. We constructed high-resolution 3D genomic maps using pore chromatin conformation capture (Pore-C), complemented by chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq), RNA-seq, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS), to investigate key chromatin topological remodeling events in HCC development. Significant alterations in A/B compartments, topologically associating domains (TADs), and chromatin loops were observed across different tissue types and patients. Comparisons between normal liver and cirrhotic tissues revealed predominant enhancement of inter‑chromosomal interactions; comparisons between cirrhotic and HCC tissues showed predominant elevation of intra‑chromosomal interactions. Across normal, cirrhotic and HCC disease states, we observed compaction of the highly active A compartments and concomitant decompaction of the silent B compartments. In general, both cirrhosis and tumor exhibited more transcriptionally active compartment states compared to normal adjacent tissues. TAD size and numbers were more conserved within tissues from the same individual than across different patients with the same tissue type. Few TAD boundaries were gained or lost consistently. Integrative analysis with H3K27ac identified genomic regions co-occurring with loop formation and enhancer activation. In normal adjacent tissue, theCXCL12gene locus maintained a well-defined chromatin loop structure that was disrupted in tumor tissues. Corresponding RNA-seq analysis confirmed significant downregulation ofCXCL12expression in tumors. By integrating SVs identified from Pore-C datasets and the Chinese Liver Cancer Atlas (CLCA), we identified SV-induced neo-loops, which were more prone to transcriptional alterations and could promote cell proliferation by activating choline metabolism and phospholipase D signaling pathways. Comparing the three disease states, cirrhosis represents an intermediate state with reversed patterns of chromosomal interactions relative to normal liver and HCC. Although canonical A/B compartment shifts involved limited genomic regions, we consistently observed progressive compaction of compartment A and decompaction of compartment B. Compared with normal tissues, HCC exhibits the disruption ofCXCL12chromatin loop and a significant reduction in enhancer signals, accompanied by a marked downregulation ofCXCL12expression in tumor tissues. SV-induced neo-loops were key events influencing gene expression. The proteins encoded by these genes are highly involved in homologous recombination, and drove cell proliferation via specific signaling pathways. Our findings revealed that stage-specific chromatin structural changes and provided novel insights into the mechanisms of gene dysregulation in hepatocarcinogenesis.

Article.Title: A noise-aware hardware-software co-design framework for real-time EEG-based stress detection across heterogeneous embedded platforms
Article.Authors: Zia Z.; Amin F.; Qureshi M.; Fatima M.; Rahman J.; Mashal A.; Hamd Z.; Almudaimeegh L.; Ali B.
Article.Abstract: AbstractDeploying EEG-based stress detection on embedded hardware demands that the signal processing pipeline and classification algorithm to be jointly co-designed with the resource constraints of the target platform, rather than optimized in isolation. This paper presents a hardware-software co-design framework centered on a noise-aware feature selection strategy that jointly optimizes three competing objectives: maximization of mutual information with respect to stress labels, robustness of features under degraded signal-to-noise conditions, and minimization of inter-feature redundancy. Applying this strategy reduces an initial 312-dimensional EEG feature space to a compact set of 47 discriminative features, yielding a 3.8 MB Random Forest model that generalizes across deployment targets without platform-specific retraining. The framework is validated on six heterogeneous embedded systems spanning a wide capability spectrum from FPGA-accelerated SoCs to commodity microcontrollers costing as little as $4 demonstrating that a single trained model can be deployed across divergent hardware architectures while preserving classification fidelity. This paper aims to balance algorithmic accuracy with the hardware constraints by proposing a hardware-software co-design system that allows the real-time, energy-efficient monitoring of stress in small embedded systems. In this direction, we initially develop a strict software pipeline, which integrates robust preprocessing methods, such as Independent Component Analysis and adaptive filtering, along with a noise-sensitive feature-selection strategy comprising 47 dimensions.. Based on this unified methodology, there is an ensemble classification model which achieves a high accuracy of 99.57% to detect exam induced stress. We explored deployment of six non-homogenous platforms, including a desktop CPU (HP G10 450, Intel Core i7-1355U), a hybrid Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)FPGA ARM system on chip (SoC)SoC (PYNQ-Z2, Zynq-7020), an embedded ARM processor (Raspberry Pi 4), and two resource-constrained Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) (Tang Nano 9 K, ICESugar iCE40UP5K), and an IoT microcontroller (ESP32). An important observation is that the classical Random Forest models (3.8 MB) are edge compatible.. The PYNQ-Z2 has a 7.9 speedup and 48.1 energy efficiency improvement with 99.57% accuracy with hardware acceleration. The hybrid ICE Sugar FPGA + ESP32 system provides 92.7% energy efficiency with a 99.57% classification accuracy and 19-h battery backup on a 5000 mAh battery. The standalone S4 ESP32 microcontroller alone in 35-h of battery life achieves an accuracy of 99.21%, showing that stress monitoring at a clinical level is possible on a commodity microcontroller. These findings establish a comprehensive methodology for signal acquisition and silicon implementation of enabling technologies, facilitating the development of on-demand wearable neurotechnology capable of continuous mental health monitoring across educational, clinical, and occupational settings.

Article.Title: Renal microcirculatory impairment on contrast enhanced ultrasound predicts persistent renal impairment in cardiogenic shock patients receiving venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
Article.Authors: Chen W.; Wang B.; Pan H.; Pei M.; Chen S.; Wei Y.; Zhou Y.; Wu R.; Qiu G.; Duan W.; Tang Y.; Chen X.; Li Z.; Qin Q.; Liu J.; Liao H.; Zhang L.; Zhong Z.; Meng L.; Li K.; Lyu L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAcute kidney injury (AKI) is one of the most frequent complications in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) receiving veno‑arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO). Microcirculation dysfunction is an important mechanism and it can be effectively evaluated by contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS). This study aimed to investigate the association between CEUS-derived parameters and the progression of persistent renal impairment following AKI in this population. This prospective observational study involved 127 CS patients receiving VA-ECMO and developing AKI within 48 h. All patients underwent CEUS at 48 h after ECMO initiation. The study endpoint was the non-recovery of renal function at the 7, 30 and 90 days after ECMO initiation. CEUS-derived parameters included time to peak (TTP), rise time (RT) and time from peak to one half (TPH). Logistic regression was used to identify the correlation between these parameters and study endpoints. Additionally, seven machine learning (ML) algorithms were employed to validate the comprehensive predictive power of CEUS parameters. The proportions of AKI non-recovery at 7, 30 and 90 days were 67.72%, 37.79%, and 23.62% respectively. The univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis for the clinical outcomes demonstrated increased TTP, RT and TPH in both cortex and medulla were associated with increased risk of AKI non-recovery at 7, 30, and 90 days (allP< 0.05). All ML algorithms demonstrated acceptable discrimination in predicting endpoints. CEUS may be a valuable tool for assessing renal microcirculation alterations. CEUS-derived indices were effective in predicting the progression of renal impairment after AKI.

Article.Title: Ecophysiological and anatomical variation in Setaria parviflora (Poaceae) between contrasting environments in the Brazilian Cerrado
Article.Authors: Sousa M.; Sanches M.; Welker C.; Boselli M.; Alonso A.; Marzinek J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractEnvironmental heterogeneity can be associated with substantial phenotypic variation in plant populations, but the integration of ecophysiological and anatomical variation under natural field conditions remains poorly understood for many tropical grasses.Setaria parviflorais a perennial C4grass occurring in contrasting environments of the Brazilian Cerrado. We compared ecophysiological and anatomical traits of populations from a preserved palm swamp and an adjacent dry disturbed area. Net CO₂ assimilation, water-use efficiency, and instantaneous carboxylation efficiency were higher in plants from the dry disturbed area, whereas stomatal conductance, transpiration, relative water content, and specific leaf area did not differ between populations. Root aerenchyma area and vascular cylinder area were greater in individuals from the palm swamp, whereas the number of xylem poles was greater in the dry disturbed area. Culm vessel element area was greater in the dry disturbed area, whereas abaxial stomatal density was higher in the palm swamp. Principal component analyses showed clearer differentiation between populations for physiological than for anatomical traits, while the environmental PCA summarized the distinct field conditions recorded during the two sampling campaigns. Together, these results show that anatomical and ecophysiological traits vary differently between natural populations ofS. parvifloraunder contrasting local conditions, highlighting the value of integrating structural and functional traits when assessing phenotypic variation in field populations.

Article.Title: Adaptive search-space reduction and partial shading detection for high-efficiency MPPT in photovoltaic systems
Article.Authors: Rouabah D.; Azri M.; Ramli M.; Lekbir A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper proposes an integrated maximum power point tracking (MPPT) framework for photovoltaic systems operating under uniform and partial shading conditions. The framework incorporates a partial shading detection technique (PSDT) that simultaneously identifies the operating condition and adaptively reduces the search space by eliminating regions that cannot contain the global maximum power point (GMPP) and avoiding redundant sampling, thereby accelerating the subsequent MPPT process. Based on the identified condition, an enhanced divide-and-conquer algorithm with ternary ratio (EDCA-TR), designed to avoid unnecessary inner-point evaluations, is deployed under uniform shading conditions, while a modified JAYA (M-JAYA) algorithm is employed under partial shading conditions. Unlike conventional iteration-based metaheuristic approaches, the proposed M-JAYA employs particle-based updates that immediately incorporate newly acquired search information, together with an adaptive search-space confinement mechanism based on iteration count and particle power information. Experimental validation under seven shading patterns demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an average tracking time of 1.86 s and an average tracking efficiency of 95.27%, outperforming the Hybrid, improved coot optimization algorithm (ICOA), and improved water cycle optimization algorithm (IWCO) benchmark methods. Moreover, the proposed framework achieves an average tracking energy loss of 3.45 W·s, representing a reduction of more than 50% compared with the benchmark methods. Repeated-run simulation analysis further demonstrates generally consistent performance despite the stochastic nature of the M-JAYA algorithm. Overall, the proposed framework improves convergence speed, tracking stability, and energy extraction by combining condition-dependent MPPT selection with adaptive search-space reduction and particle-based optimization.

Article.Title: Metacognitive regulation of cognitive control to adjust choice accuracy in rhesus macaques
Article.Authors: Lespart A.; Bénon J.; Daunizeau J.; Bouret S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMaking the best choice in one situation is critical, but it relies on limited cognitive capacities. Numerous animal species adjust the amount of cognitive resources allocated to a decision using a trade-off between speed and accuracy, where decision time corresponds to an investment of cognitive control, which scales with the expected increase in reward. In humans, recent studies indicate that control allocation is regulated not only based upon its potential benefits, but also upon its potential cost, through a metacognitive monitoring process. Is it the case in other primates? We addressed this issue in rhesus monkeys with a detailed analysis of the relation among choice accuracy, choice difficulty and response time in a two-choice task. In contrast to typical demonstrations of speed-accuracy trade-off, we found higher choice accuracy in trials with faster response time, above and beyond choice difficulty. This relationship can be explained by a model of metacognitive decision monitoring where the cost of cognitive control is traded against confidence benefits. Thus, rhesus monkeys also seem to rely upon supervisory monitoring to modulate the amount of control exerted over their decision efficacy. This might drive future research on the evolution of cognitive and neurophysiological processes underlying decision making.

Article.Title: Decoding the ICU resistome: integron-mediated spread of blaIMP-85 and novel gene cassettes in XDR pathogens
Article.Authors: Abdelrazik M.; Gameel W.; Alsayed Y.; El-Demerdash A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractHealthcare-associated infections (HAIs) in intensive care units (ICUs) are critically compounded by multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial pathogens. Mobile integrons act as pivotal site-specific recombination systems that facilitate the capture and horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of antimicrobial resistance determinants. This study aimed to characterize the molecular epidemiology, cassette array diversity, and clinical impact of plasmid-borne integrons (intI1,intI2, andintI3) among bacterial isolates recovered from ICU patients in Egypt. A total of 153 non-duplicate clinical bacterial isolates were recovered from 117 ICU patients (50 monomicrobial and 67 polymicrobial specimens). Isolates were stratified into Gram-negative bacilli and Gram-positive cocci. Species identification and phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) were performed using the VITEK® 2 system, Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion, and CLSI-compliant broth microdilution assays. Extrachromosomal plasmid DNA was extracted and screened for integrase genes and variable cassette regions via PCR, followed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing, restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) validation, and bioinformatic analysis. Statistical associations and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted$$p$$-values were evaluated using R software (v4.3.3). Gram-negative isolates (n=116) comprisedKlebsiella pneumoniae(49.1%, n= 57),Escherichia coli(37.1%, n= 43),Pseudomonas aeruginosa(11.2%, n= 13),Proteus mirabilis(1.7%, n= 2), andSerratia fonticola(0.9%, n=1). All Gram-positive isolates were identified asStaphylococcus aureus(n =37), with 100% exhibiting resistance to cefoxitin and oxacillin (mecA-positive MRSA status). Isolates displayed elevated rates of MDR (49.2%) and extensive drug resistance (XDR; 27.0%), with high-level vancomycin resistance (VRSA) confirmed in 70.3% ofS. aureusstrains. Integron prevalence was significantly higher in Gram-negative isolates (91.3%) than inS. aureus(44.0%). Class 1 integrons (intI1) predominated (52.1%), whereasintI2(13.0%) andintI3(17.4%) were restricted exclusively to Gram-negative species. Sanger sequencing confirmed the metallo-$$\beta $$-lactamase alleleblaIMP-85(GenBank: PP663295) inP. aeruginosa, a novel tandemdfrA27–aadA2cassette structure (PP663294) inE. coli, and an extrachromosomalsat2–aadA1array (PP663297) harbored byS. aureus, confirming cross-gram-class interspecies HGT. Non-synonymous point mutations withinaadA1,sat2, andintI3indicated active genetic drift. Correlation analysis demonstrated that total Gram-negative integron carriage strongly predicted XDR phenotypes (p= 0.69,p< 0.01) and resistance to levofloxacin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, gentamicin, and imipenem. Plasmid-borne integrons are strongly associated with MDR and XDR profiles in critical care pathogens. The identification of functional, plasmid-locatedintI1arrays bridging Gram-negative species andS. aureusunderscores the urgent necessity of integrating molecular integron surveillance alongside routine AST to combat plasmid-mediated resistance dissemination in ICUs.

Article.Title: Closed-form solution and parametric study on lateral dynamic response of pile-type bridge piers resting on cement-soil composite pipe piles
Article.Authors: Liu H.; Zhu W.; Dai G.; Ji Z.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThis paper develops a closed-form analytical framework for the lateral dynamic interaction between a pile-type bridge (PTB) pier and a cement-soil composite (CC) pipe pile in viscoelastic soil, based on Timoshenko beam theory. The derived analytical solutions are rigorously verified through two parallel approaches: comparison with published theoretical results and cross-validation against PLAXIS 3D numerical simulations. On this basis, systematic parametric analyses are conducted to quantify the influences of key parameters of the PTB pier, cement-soil pile and PHC pipe pile on the lateral dynamic response of the coupled system. The results reveal that piers with smaller heights deliver stronger low-frequency load-bearing performance but face a higher risk of resonance under high-frequency excitation, whereas taller piers can effectively postpone the occurrence of resonant peaks. Enlarging the reinforcement radius and elastic modulus of the cement-soil pile, as well as increasing the outer radius and elastic modulus of the inner PHC pipe pile, all improve the lateral vibration resistance of the entire coupled system. In particular, increasing the structural mass at the pier top amplifies the horizontal inertial force of the system, which adversely affects the lateral vibration resistance of the coupled pile-pier system.

Article.Title: Multi-directional control of a bio-inspired robot with a single undulating fin propulsion
Article.Authors: Garcia G.; Uddin M.; Odeh O.; Karim M.; Curet O.
Article.Abstract: AbstractControl of agile and highly maneuverable underwater vessels is fundamental to explore complex maritime environments including survey closed to ocean structures and shallow waters. Currently, traditional autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) and remote operated vehicles (ROVs) can encounter challenges navigating through these tight spaces. In this work, we explore the use of a flexible undulating membrane as a propulsive and force control mechanism for an underwater vehicle. We present a control scheme where modulations in the amplitude of two counter-propagating waves can provide a wide range of motion control including station keeping, heading, turning and speed control. We first present it through a user-operated control and then in closed-loop feedback to modulate the fin actuation to control the motion of the vessel. Free-swimming is executed with an elongated membrane positioned ventrally along the vehicle. The membrane fin was actuated through independently controlled flexible rays. The vehicle was tested in a flume at different flow speeds and pool where real-time tracking was used to obtain the position and orientation of the vessel. Using time-varying and spatial modulations of sinusoidal traveling waves, controlled trajectory of the vessel in addition to station-keeping in the presence of external perturbations can be achieved. Finally, we present the vessel swimming in the wake of an object where the fin has to overcome flow fluctuations from the shed vortices. We found that relatively simple controllers for flexible fin kinematics are sufficient to perform path following and station keeping and a variety of swimming maneuvers, providing a versatile alternative to conventional propulsion mechanisms in complex environments. Although control was implemented with sinusoidal traveling waves, it is envisioned that further exploration of a wider range of kinematics for optimal swimming will allow engineered vessels to the perform the graceful maneuvers that aquatic animals can.

Article.Title: Paternal antenatal depression and its associated factors among expectant fathers in Debre Tabor Town, Ethiopia: a community-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Dagne A.; Erlandson K.; Seyoum T.; Azale T.; Lindgren H.; Wells M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractPaternal antenatal depression remains under-recognized and under-investigated, particularly in low-and middle-income countries such as Ethiopia, where evidence on its prevalence and associated factors is limited. This study aimed to determine paternal antenatal depression symptoms and identify its associated factors in expectant fathers during their partners’ third-trimester pregnancy. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 859 expectant fathers, selected through stratified multistage cluster sampling techniques from March 27 to July 31, 2025. The Edinburgh postnatal depression scale assessed depression symptoms. Descriptive statistics were computed, and bivariable logistic regression identified variables withp< .2 for multivariable analysis. Statistically significant associations were declared atp< .05 using adjusted odds ratios (AOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). The prevalence of paternal antenatal depression symptoms was 22.6% (95% CI: 19.8–25.4%). Significant predictors included fathers’ age (AOR = 1.07, CI = 1.02–1.11), lower wealth index (AOR = 1.89, CI = 1.05–3.40), first-time fatherhood (AOR = 9.25, CI = 3.54–24.14), work-family conflict (AOR = 1.14, CI = 1.10–1.19), poor social support (AOR = 7.29, CI = 3.49–15.22), and maternal depression symptoms (AOR = 10.64, CI = 6.50–17.40). In conclusion, over one-fifth of expectant fathers experienced antenatal depression symptoms. Statistically significant associated factors included fathers’ age, lower wealth, first-time fatherhood, poor social support, work-family conflict, and maternal depression.

Article.Title: An adaptive multi-objective differential evolution algorithm to fine-tune the constructive cost model constants for software effort estimation
Article.Authors: Gouda S.; Ramasubbareddy S.; Chaudhury K.; Mishra S.; Mohapatra H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe primary goals of software effort and cost estimation are to determine project cost, shorten development time, and provide a reliable prediction. This issue is also classified as a multi-objective optimization problem. A new adaptation-based multi-objective differential evolution algorithm, enhanced with Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, solves these problems by tuning the parameters. This paper includes new mutation techniques with a Pareto-based differential evolution algorithm, leveraging Generative AI to increase candidate solution diversity. The new mutation operator provides more bandwidth, which helps the differential evolution algorithm to avoid local optimality problems. This study applies a non-dominated sorting technique to lower the computational complexity involved in Pareto dominance. The article further examines the software cost estimation problem by fine-tuning the parameters for a multi-objective constructive cost model using Generative AI to predict software costs accurately. The software cost estimation problem aims to minimize prediction errors while maximizing accuracy, ultimately reducing overall project costs. Compared to existing modern versions of multi-objective evolutionary optimization algorithms across all objective problems, the proposed approach, which integrates Generative AI, shows improved prediction and lower error rates on the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)-93 and Constructive Cost Model (COCOMO)-81 datasets.

Article.Title: Fractal gene losses and concomitant genesis of novel clades sculpt the metazoan Gα gene repertoire
Article.Authors: Abu Obaid A.; Abdullahi A.; Korsching K.; Oka Y.; Korsching S.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGα proteins are integral components of cellular signaling, with an ancient evolutionary origin. Within animals, Gα proteins have been categorized into five canonical classes: Gαs, Gαi, Gαq, Gα12, and Gαv, with few unclassified genes outside of these groups. Here we have performed comprehensive phylogenetic analyses of nearly one thousand metazoan species, focusing on two species-rich phyla, arthropods and nematodes. Our analysis reveals a fractal pattern of gene loss in all five canonical classes, with Gαs and Gαv most prone to gene loss. On the other hand, gene gains are common in all five classes, most pronounced in Gαq and Gα12. Unexpectedly, we observe the emergence of thirteen novel clades, the majority specific to single phyla (arthropods, nematodes, tardigrades) and some even specific to lower taxonomic classifications. Those new clades exhibit all G box and switch region motifs, characteristic for the five canonical classes. For all of the new clades we observe many representatives in transcriptome assemblies, validating their expression and suggesting a functional role for them. Our results show a highly dynamic evolutionary landscape for Gα proteins, including extensive gene losses and frequent gains in the five canonical classes and recurrent genesis of new clades—unexpected in such a highly conserved and ancient family of proteins with central importance in cellular signalling. Our findings advance the understanding of Gα protein evolution, and lay the foundation for deciphering the functional role of the novel Gα clades.

Article.Title: An intelligent virtual coaching system for traditional martial arts based on 3D pose estimation and generative adversarial networks
Article.Authors: Fu C.; Yin L.; Yang F.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTraditional martial arts are hard to hand on. The masters who hold the repertoire are ageing, instruction rarely travels beyond the training hall, and verbal correction remains stubbornly subjective. This paper presents an intelligent virtual coaching system that couples enhanced three-dimensional pose estimation with generative adversarial network refinement. A modified High-Resolution Network, augmented with attention and temporal convolution, extracts skeletons that survive fast strikes and self-occlusion, while a discriminator-guided sequence optimization module pulls noisy trajectories back onto the manifold of biomechanically plausible movement. On top of these components, a hierarchical feedback mechanism turns quantitative learner-reference comparisons into real-time, multimodal corrections. Evaluated on public benchmarks and on a purpose-built martial arts corpus, the pipeline reaches 38.6 mm Mean Per Joint Position Error while sustaining 28.4 frames per second, and its automated quality scores track expert ratings closely, with a correlation coefficient of 0.847. Taken together, the results describe a workable technological pathway for preserving intangible cultural heritage and for widening access to high-quality martial arts instruction.

Article.Title: Optimization scheduling of cascade reservoirs under an ecological approach: a case study
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang S.; Xiao G.; Fu X.; Ming L.; Huang W.; Liang C.; zhan Y.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Yalong River Basin is a significant hydropower base and a crucial component of the global biodiversity hotspot, Mountains of Southwest China. There are five key cascade reservoirs in the lower reaches of Yalong River. The current optimal operation focuses on power generation and flood control, which alters the natural flow regime and adversely affects the river ecosystem. To address the lack of ecological flow considerations in this basin, a study on optimal dispatching of cascade hydropower stations with minimum ecological flow requirements incorporated was conducted. First, based on hydrological variations in the study area, the Improved Ten-day Frequency Method (ITFM) is used to calculate the minimum ecological flow requirements. Second, a medium- and long-term multi-objective optimization model balancing power generation and ecological objectives was established, which aimed to maximize power generation and minimize the sum of ecological alteration degrees for the cascade hydropower stations, and was solved using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Subsequently, ecological scheduling schemes for cascade reservoirs in various typical years are determined. The results show that the hydrological change point of the Yalong River Basin occurred in 1992, with the runoff differences before and after this point are significant. Compared to conventional scheduling schemes, under the ecological-prioritizing scheme, the proposed ecological scheme achieved reductions in ecological alteration degrees of 37.74%, 19.84%, and 58.6% in the three typical years of wet, normal, and dry, which shows a significant increase in ecological benefits. This approach demonstrates the significant role of ecological regulation in facilitating the restoration of river ecosystems and provides a valuable reference for reconciling the conflict between reservoir power generation and downstream ecological water use.

Article.Title: Clinical documentation quality in routine care with AI scribe support: a large‑scale Spanish analysis
Article.Authors: Álvaro de la Parra J.; Alcázar-Peral J.; Blanco D.; Martín C.; Rodríguez B.; Campos S.; Espelt E.; Cristóbal I.; Caramés C.
Article.Abstract: AbstractClinical documentation is essential for care quality, safety, and coordination, yet the growing burden of electronic health record (EHR) tasks contributes to clinician burnout and may compromise documentation quality. Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribe systems have emerged as a potential solution, but their impact on documentation quality and readability remains underexplored. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the effect of an AI-assisted scribe system (Scribe) on the semantic agreement, readability, and structured quality of outpatient clinical documentation across multiple specialties in a large Spanish healthcare network, within the framework of value-based healthcare (VBHC). Thus, we conducted a retrospective, multi-method study of over 2.3 million outpatient consultations across 45 specialties (Oct 2024–Dec 2025). Documentation with and without Scribe was compared using automated metrics (semantic agreement, INFLESZ and Perspicuity) and an 18-item structured quality rubric. Semantic agreement was evaluated across all 45 specialties, whereas report quality was assessed in a stratified sample of 300 reports from 15 specialties. A manual audit evaluated completeness of key safety elements (past medical history, allergies), and statistical analyses included descriptive metrics, Welch and paired t-tests, and Hedges’ g. Notably, Scribe achieved a weighted mean semantic agreement of 89.3% (SD 2.1). Readability improved significantly: INFLESZ scores increased from 72.05 to 77.61 (p< 0.001), and Perspicuity scores from 76.19 to 81.49 (p< 0.001). Structured quality scores rose from 5.79 (95% CI 5.60–5.99) to 8.02 (95% CI 7.87–8.17), with a large effect size (Hedges’ g = 2.06;p< 0.001). A manual audit showed significant improvements in documentation of past medical history (7.75 vs 1.75;p< 0.001; dz = 1.10) and allergy status (9.75 vs 7.75;p= 0.010; g = 0.43). Altogether, AI-assisted scribe technology was associated with improvements in documentation quality, readability, and safety-related documentation elements. These improvements align with VBHC principles by supporting better patient outcomes, safer care, and more efficient use of clinical resources through high-quality documentation.

Article.Title: Accelerated development and deployment of computer vision models for invasive aquatic pests
Article.Authors: Pearson R.; Preston G.; Bulleid J.; David S.; Zareie-Vaux F.; Clements D.; Tait L.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAquatic non-indigenous species (NIS) incur significant cultural, environmental and economic costs worldwide, and human surveillance is expensive and impractical at large scales. Computer vision models (CVMs) deployed on remote and autonomous vehicles can reduce the burden on trained human observers, but aquatic environments present unique challenges and lack frameworks for biosecurity-focused development and deployment. We present a practical framework for developing and deploying new species-specific CVMs for real-time use across surface vessel and remote vehicle platforms. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through its application to several taxonomically and ecologically diverse NIS in New Zealand: Mediterranean fanwormSabella spallanzanii, South African oxygen weedLagarosiphon major,and exoticCaulerpa(Caulerpa brachypusandC. parvifolia). ForS. spallanzanii, we demonstrate efficient training from small datasets and deployment for real-time detection. Using exoticCaulerpa, we show how CVMs can be rapidly improved during an early incursion response. ForL. major, standardised field validation methods enable the comparison of CVM and human detection rates across diverse locations and operating conditions. Collectively, these case studies demonstrate that our framework enables accurate detection and the robust assessment of model effectiveness under realistic field conditions and can be effectively applied to imagery from multiple platforms.

Article.Title: Financial literacy and gambling-related risk in adult ADHD: a decision-making perspective
Article.Authors: Hamurcu Ç.; Öztürk M.; Hamurcu H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractGambling-related risk represents a financially consequential form of risk-taking and may be particularly relevant in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This cross-sectional study examined associations among ADHD symptom severity, financial literacy, and gambling-related risk in 83 adults with clinically diagnosed ADHD who had not yet started methylphenidate treatment. Financial literacy was assessed using basic financial literacy questions, gambling-related risk with the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS), and ADHD symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS). Structural equation modeling showed that higher financial literacy was associated with lower gambling-related risk in the Maximum Likelihood estimation, although this association was not statistically significant in the bootstrap analysis. ADHD symptom severity was not directly associated with either gambling-related risk or financial literacy. Gender was associated with ASRS, financial literacy, and SOGS scores in both the Maximum Likelihood and bootstrap analyses. These findings suggest that financial literacy may be a relevant correlate of gambling-related risk among adults with ADHD, while ADHD symptom severity alone may not account for individual differences in gambling-related risk. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these associations and their underlying mechanisms.

Article.Title: Magnetic-field-assisted photocatalytic activity of CoFe₂O₄/graphene oxide nanocomposite for dye degradation
Article.Authors: Negedu S.; Assaro A.; Ayalew M.; Sewnet A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractEfficient removal of persistent organic dyes from wastewater remains a significant environmental challenge. This study presents the hydrothermal synthesis of a CoFe2O4/graphene oxide (CF/GO) nanocomposite and evaluates its photocatalytic performance under magnetic-field assistance for the degradation of methylene blue (MB) and Congo red (CR) under visible-light irradiation. Comprehensive characterization was conducted using SEM, EDX, TEM, XRD, FTIR, Raman, UV-Vis DRS, and VSM techniques. The incorporation of GO reduced the band gap from 2.4 eV to 1.9 eV, enhancing visible-light absorption, while the nanocomposite maintained strong ferromagnetic properties (Ms = 53.29 emu/g, Hc = 949 Oe), facilitating magnetic recovery. Under visible-light irradiation, the CF/GO nanocomposite achieved degradation efficiencies of 84% for MB and 74% for CR within 90 min. Applying an external magnetic field (0.5 T) further increased the efficiencies to 98% and 86%, respectively. This enhancement is attributed to Lorentz-force-induced charge-carrier separation, which suppresses recombination and increases the generation of reactive oxygen species, primarily•O₂⁻ and h⁺. The photocatalyst exhibited excellent reusability, retaining over 93% efficiency after five cycles. These findings demonstrate that the CF/GO nanocomposite is a highly efficient, magnetically separable photocatalyst for wastewater treatment and underscore the synergistic effect of magnetic-field assistance in ferrite-graphene systems.

Article.Title: COH fluids and melts drive mantle refertilization and organic synthesis in nascent subduction zones
Article.Authors: Herviou C.; Soret M.; Debret B.; Andreani M.; Montagnac G.; Olivieri O.; Vitale Brovarone A.; Rividi N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSlab-derived fluids and melts released during subduction refertilize the mantle wedge, shaping arc magmatism and volatile transfer. Yet the nature and efficiency of the earliest metasomatizing agents active under the warm thermal gradients of nascent subduction zones remain poorly constrained. Here, we report multiphase and polymineralic inclusions from the high-temperature metamorphic sole of the Semail ophiolite (Oman–United Arab Emirates), which record the trapping of COH fluids and hydrous silicate melts derived from both mafic and sedimentary slab components during subduction infancy. Multiphase inclusions act as micro-reactors where fluids react with host minerals during exhumation, driving the abiotic synthesis of solid organic compounds, including nanodiamond-like structures, demonstrating that subduction zones can generate molecules of prebiotic relevance. Combined with the ophiolite record, our results indicate that such COH fluids and melts refertilize the mantle wedge from the onset of subduction, generating proto-arc magmas and promoting deep carbonation and hydration.

Article.Title: Impact of premixing on the propulsion performance of N2O/hydrocarbon thrusters: a combined numerical and experimental study
Article.Authors: Jung E.; Kim J.; Lee K.; Kim Y.; Lee E.; Jung E.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractNitrous oxide (N$$_2$$O)-based bipropellant systems utilizing self-pressurizing hydrocarbon fuels offer a promising non-toxic alternative for space propulsion applications. However, a systematic comparison between non-premixed and premixed combustion modes under controlled operational conditions remains unreported. This study quantitatively evaluates the propulsion performance of a 10 N-class N$$_2$$O/C$$_2$$H$$_6$$thruster using a combined framework of three-dimensional numerical simulations and hot-fire experiments. A non-premixed unlike-impinging injector was compared against two premixed configurations under identical propellant mass flow rates, mixture ratios, and combustor geometries. Numerically, the premixed like-doublet impinging configuration showed a 16.4% increase in thrust over the non-premixed baseline, and these trends were successfully validated through hot-fire tests. While the single-hole configuration experienced flashback, the premixed like-doublet thruster sustained stable 5-s combustion, delivering a sea-level thrust of 5.34 N and a specific impulse ($$I_{sp}$$) of 111 s. This represents an 11.1% increase in$$I_{sp}$$over the non-premixed baseline, along with a characteristic velocity rise from 1336 to 1350 m/s. This improvement is attributed to enhanced propellant mixing and a more uniform axial flow field through the nozzle. This comprehensive numerical and experimental investigation demonstrates the definitive performance advantages of the premixed injection strategy, providing critical design benchmarks for next-generation high-performance propulsion systems.

Article.Title: Federated privacy-preserving facial paralysis severity classification using hybrid deep learning and pufferfish optimization
Article.Authors: Kiruthiga S.; Anbuananth C.; Dhilipkumar V.
Article.Abstract: AbstractFacial paralysis (FP) severity assessment requires accurate identification of subtle facial asymmetry while maintaining the confidentiality of sensitive patient information. Conventional centralized deep learning approaches require patient images to be transferred to a central repository, which can increase privacy risks and limit collaborative learning across healthcare institutions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Federated Learning-based Secure and Privacy-Preserving Hybrid Deep Learning with Pufferfish Optimization (FLSDPP-HDLPO) framework for automated FP severity classification. The proposed framework first performs image preprocessing and augmentation to improve facial-image quality and class representation. A hybrid feature extraction strategy integrating Capsule Network (CapsNet), ResNet50, and LeViT is then employed to learn complementary spatial, hierarchical, and attention-based facial representations. The extracted features are classified using a CNN-BiGRU architecture, while the Pufferfish Optimization Algorithm (POA) is employed to optimize the relevant model parameters. To preserve data confidentiality during distributed learning, homomorphic encryption is incorporated into the federated learning process so that sensitive model information can be securely exchanged without exposing the original patient data. The framework is evaluated using combined MEEI and YFP facial paralysis datasets containing six severity classes. Experimental evaluation under different training and testing configurations demonstrates that the proposed FLSDPP-HDLPO framework achieves a maximum classification accuracy of 97.56%, with precision, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score of 92.48%, 92.53%, 98.54%, and 92.50%, respectively. Repeated experiments further produced an accuracy of 97.56% ± 0.42%, demonstrating consistent performance. The proposed framework therefore provides an accurate and privacy-preserving approach for distributed FP severity assessment. Future work will focus on larger multi-center datasets, stronger robustness evaluation, computational optimization, and real-world clinical validation.

Article.Title: Innovative application of frankincense resin as a sustainable bio-adhesive for insect trapping in legume crops
Article.Authors: Ammar R.; Kandil R.
Article.Abstract: AbstractField experiments were conducted in Kafr El-Dawar, El-Beheira, Egypt during the 2025 summer season using a completely randomized design with four replications to evaluate bio-adhesive sticky traps formulated from frankincense resin as eco-friendly alternatives to imported commercial traps in cowpea fields. Two colors (yellow and blue) were tested for each trap. Luban-based adhesive was prepared using frankincense resin, starch, sugar, yeast, beeswax, molasses, and essential oils. Yellow traps captured significantly higher numbers of aphids and whiteflies compared with other pest groups, with no significant differences between Luban-based and commercial traps for most pests, except cotton bollworm where Luban traps recorded significantly higher captures. Blue Luban traps also outperformed commercial ones in capturing whiteflies, jassids, thrips, and cotton bollworm, while aphid and cowpea beetle catches were statistically similar. Economic analysis revealed that Luban-based traps cost less (360 L.E/fed) than commercial traps (780 L.E/fed). Although commercial traps resulted in a significantly higher yield, the net return and investment ratio remained comparable between treatments (0.26 and 0.27). Furthermore, a preliminary carbon-footprint assessment indicated that Luban-based traps reduced estimated environmental emissions by approximately 25–40% compared to imported synthetic traps, due to their biodegradable composition and reliance on locally sourced natural materials, supporting low-carbon agricultural systems. These findings indicate that Luban-based sticky traps are cost-effective, environmentally sustainable, and demonstrate considerable potential as patentable innovations that enable sustainable pest management in cowpea systems and reducing dependence on chemical insecticides.

Article.Title: A VSV-based pseudotyping system for studying entry and neutralization of papiine alphaherpesvirus 2
Article.Authors: Elsasser L.; Gärtner S.; Stomberg P.; Schröter L.; Naßl A.; Decker K.; Arora P.; Damert A.; Pöhlmann S.; Winkler M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSimplexviruses of non-human primates differ in their capacity to cause severe disease in humans. Papiine alphaherpesvirus 2 (PaHV-2) of baboons has not been reported to be pathogenic in humans while human infection with macacine alphaherpesvirus 1 (McHV-1, Herpes B Virus) can cause fatal disease. In order to study PaHV-2 entry into cells, we established a pseudotyping system based on vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV). For this, the genes coding for core glycoproteins of PaHV-2, gD, gH, gL and gB as well as gC were cloned and the glycoproteins were equipped either with the native signal peptide or a heterologous signal peptide and an epitope tag. Glycoproteins with Igκ-signal peptide were most robustly expressed and incorporated into pseudotyped VSV particles. VSV bearing the core glycoproteins (DHLBpp) or an extended set of glycoproteins (DHLBCpp) efficiently entered several cell lines of human, rhesus macaque, African green monkey and mouse origin. In addition, DHLBppwere efficiently neutralized by baboon sera at levels comparable to those determined with a PaHV-2 reporter virus. In summary, VSV particles bearing glycoproteins of PaHV-2 are a novel tool to study PaHV-2 entry and neutralization.

Article.Title: From arithmetic-sequence gradient architectures to interfacial-modulus-corrected bending models in laser-sintered laminates
Article.Authors: Han Z.; Wang Y.; Liu S.; Hu J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractLaser-sintered 316 L/CuSn10 laminates with slow, medium, and fast gradient transitions are fabricated via arithmetic-sequence stacking. Classical laminate theory predicts nearly identical elastic bending stiffness for all configurations (differences < 1%). Three-point bending tests, however, reveal strong gradient-rate dependence: the medium-gradient configuration exhibits the highest maximum bending load (837.850 N), which is ~ 103% and ~ 55% higher than those of the slow- (412.247 N) and fast-gradient (540.714 N) configurations, respectively. The experimental bending stiffness per unit width also varies markedly (slow: 59,851 N·mm; medium: 136,249 N·mm; fast: 94,375 N·mm), contradicting classical predictions. This discrepancy exposes a fundamental limitation of classical laminate theory—its neglect of interfacial modulus degradation induced during laser sintering. To address this, a modified bending stiffness model is developed, incorporating elastic modulus attenuation within the interfacial transition zone and a gradient-distribution-controlled weakening factor. The modified model quantitatively reproduces the experimental bending stiffness values and their ranking (medium > fast > slow). These results establish a quantitative framework for regulating elastic behaviour through gradient sequence design in laser-sintered multi-material laminates.

Article.Title: Plasma membrane vesicles preserve cell type specific physicochemical signatures
Article.Authors: Pogoda K.; Chrabąszcz K.; Deptuła P.; Bucki R.; Piergies N.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe plasma membrane encodes critical information about cellular identity and phenotype, yet detailed characterization of this complex interface remains technically challenging in whole cells. Giant plasma membrane vesicles (GPMVs), generated via chemically induced blebbing, offer a simplified yet biochemically rich model of the cell membrane. Here, we investigate whether GPMVs retain biophysical and biochemical properties reflective of their cell of origin. Using a panel of human cell lines - including microglial and four glioblastoma cell lines - we characterized both cells and their vesicles using fluorescence microscopy, atomic force microscopy (AFM), Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, and principal component analysis (PCA). GPMVs preserved cell-line-specific stiffness ranking observed in AFM measurements, and notably, FT-IR spectra of GPMVs enabled discrimination between cell lines, unlike spectra from intact cells. Our results highlight GPMVs as faithful surrogates of native membranes and suggest their utility for biophysical phenotyping in health and disease.

Article.Title: Thermo-hydraulic limits of streamwise rib height grading in high-aspect-ratio cooling channels
Article.Authors: Yekani S.; DindarSafa A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractRib turbulators are the standard means of enhancing internal cooling in gas turbine blades, and a recent line of work proposes grading the rib height along the flow so that turbulence is generated where the coolant is coldest. The degree of grading over which this remains beneficial has not been established. The present study quantifies that range for a high-aspect-ratio (AR = 4) rectangular channel with five square ribs mounted on a uniformly heated wall. The grading is described by a single parameter, the rib height ratio RHR, defined as the ratio of the first to the last rib height at a fixed pitch and a fixed downstream rib height, and five configurations from RHR = 1 (uniform) to RHR = 5 are compared on an otherwise identical geometry. Three-dimensional steady RANS simulations with the SST k–ω model are performed for Reynolds numbers from 2 × 10⁴ to 8 × 10⁴. Increasing RHR raises the normalised Nusselt number monotonically, from 1.29 to 1.42 at Re = 8 × 10⁴, but the normalised friction factor rises from 2.05 to 4.30 over the same range, an increase an order of magnitude larger. Both performance criteria therefore fall monotonically with RHR: at Re = 8 × 10⁴ the thermal performance factor η₁ decreases from 1.016 to 0.870, so that under an equal-pumping-power constraint the uniform array outperforms every graded array examined. The flow field identifies the cause: beyond moderate grading the tall leading ribs cease to act as discrete turbulence promoters and collectively deflect the bulk flow away from the heated wall, lifting the shear layer off the surface and leaving a low-momentum, low-Nusselt-number region downstream that offsets much of the upstream gain. Applying η₁ ≥ 1 as a design criterion yields an admissible upper limit that contracts from RHR = 4.41 at Re = 2 × 10⁴ to RHR = 1.36 at Re = 8 × 10⁴. Height grading therefore remains attractive where heat transfer rather than pumping power is the binding constraint, since it delivers up to 10% more heat transfer, but the admissible degree of grading must be selected for the design Reynolds number.

Article.Title: Culture conditions influence biomass and alkali-insoluble cell-wall polysaccharide production in indigenous Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains
Article.Authors: Mosallaie F.; Falah F.; Rahimi A.; Khabiri Noghani M.; Kashaninejad M.; Alizadeh Behbahani B.; Vasiee A.
Article.Abstract: AbstractSaccharomyces cerevisiaeis an important source of yeast biomass and alkali–insoluble cell–wall polysaccharide fractions (AICWP), which may contain substantial β–glucan. In the present study, indigenous yeast isolates from diverse natural sources were screened for biomass formation and AICWP accumulation. FourS. cerevisiaestrains, selected from 54 previously isolated yeasts, were evaluated for growth performance under the investigated culture conditions. Yeast isolates were obtained through selective cultivation and characterized morphologically and microscopically. High biomass–producing isolates were identified through growth–based screening, and the effects of glucose, ammonium sulfate, and inoculum size on biomass accumulation were assessed using a Plackett–Burman (PB) design and further examined by Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Under one set of selected cultivation conditions, biomass concentration reached 250.01 g/L wet weight (100.04 g/L dry weight), and the alkali–insoluble cell–wall fraction contained 7.01 g/L total carbohydrate expressed as glucose equivalents. Because the phenol–sulfuric acid assay is non–specific, this value represents total carbohydrate equivalents in the extracted alkali–insoluble fraction and does not constitute a direct measurement of purified β–glucan. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed dense aggregation of yeast cells with predominantly oval–to–round morphology and generally intact surfaces, consistent with the typical morphology ofS. cerevisiae. Biomass concentration declined by approximately 18% under 5% sorbitol and by 36% under 0.005% SDS; viable counts were 8.83 and 8.20 Log CFU/mL, respectively, compared with 9.07 Log CFU/mL in the control. Evaluation in a 3–L stirred–tank bioreactor with a 1–L working volume revealed that spray drying yielded a higher recovered dry powder concentration (144.75 ± 2.90 g/L) than freeze drying (125.12 ± 2.50 g/L), whereas freeze drying yielded higher viable–cell recovery after rehydration and 24 h incubation (0.2 × 109vs. 0.9 × 108CFU/mL). These findings provide preliminary feasibility evidence under the tested bioreactor conditions; further studies are required to evaluate oxygen transfer, hydrodynamics, reproducibility, and scalability.

Article.Title: Social influence under uncertainty: decision-making in anonymous crowds
Article.Authors: Konya K.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUncertainty and limited access to information may trigger unpredictable group dynamics and unsafe movements in urban crowds. Although such situations are common in everyday life, the socio-psychological mechanisms that guide decision making in crowds have scarcely been explored, apart from the controversially discussed concept of contagion. This experimental study aims to make an initial empirical approximation of this issue by examining how (non-)communication and group size affect the duration and homogeneity of group-level decisions in an anonymous setting. The results show that communication does not affect the duration of finding final solutions, but it can lead to both polarized or homogeneous outcomes. The absence of communication, on the other hand, may activate self-presentational concerns and lowers the possibility of highly homogeneous outcomes. These findings are discussed in light of mechanisms of social influence and conformity that could be identified through the videographic analysis of the experiments.

Article.Title: Integrated seismic and petrophysical characterization of the Kharita Formation in the SELKIT and SETHOS fields, Western Desert, Egypt
Article.Authors: Sarhan M.; Abdel-Fattah M.; Hamdan H.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe Kharita Formation represents one of the principal Lower Cretaceous clastic reservoirs in the Shushan Basin, Western Desert, Egypt. This study integrates seismic interpretation and petrophysical analysis to evaluate the reservoir characteristics, structural controls, and hydrocarbon potential of the Kharita Formation in the SELKIT and SETHOS fields, South Umbaraka Area. The investigation was based on the interpretation of thirty 2D seismic profiles and conventional well-log data from the SELK-6, SELK-7, and SETHOS-16 wells. Seismic interpretation was conducted to delineate the structural framework, fault architecture, and trapping configurations, while petrophysical analysis was performed to determine lithology, shale volume, porosity, fluid saturation, and net-pay distribution. Neutron-density crossplots were also utilized to identify lithological variations and potential gas-bearing intervals. The seismic interpretation reveals that the study area is structurally controlled by a series of major normal faults and fault-bounded anticlinal closures that significantly influence reservoir distribution and hydrocarbon accumulation. Time- and depth-structure maps of the Kharita Formation indicate that both the SELKIT and SETHOS fields occupy structurally elevated four-way dip closures, providing favorable trapping conditions. Correlation of the Cretaceous succession further demonstrates the influence of fault-controlled compartmentalization and differential subsidence on reservoir geometry and thickness distribution. Petrophysical analysis indicates that the Kharita Formation consists predominantly of sandstone reservoirs with variable shale content and favorable reservoir properties. Seven hydrocarbon-bearing zones were identified, with net-pay thicknesses ranging from 11 to 63 ft. Shale volume values vary between 4 and 20%, total porosity ranges from 8 to 18%, and effective porosity ranges from 6 to 17%. Water saturation values range from 20 to 45%, corresponding to hydrocarbon saturation values of 55% to 80%. The most prospective reservoir intervals occur in Zone D of SELK-6 and Zone F of SETHOS-16, which exhibit favorable combinations of net-pay thickness, porosity, and hydrocarbon saturation. The integrated results demonstrate that hydrocarbon accumulation within the Kharita Formation is controlled by the combined influence of depositional architecture, reservoir quality, and fault-related structural trapping. This study highlights the value of integrating seismic and petrophysical datasets for reducing exploration uncertainty and improving reservoir characterization in the Shushan Basin and analogous Lower Cretaceous reservoirs of the Western Desert.

Article.Title: Structure-based mechanical properties of human carotid arteries and their effect on stress-strain response
Article.Authors: Hrubanová A.; Bednařík Z.; Staffa R.; Johnston R.; Thomková B.; Lally C.; Burša J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractMechanical properties and structure of components of an atherosclerotic arterial wall are important for computational prediction of atheroma vulnerability. In this study, a total of 36 specimens harvested during standard carotid endarterectomies were tested under uniaxial tension, followed by histological examination to distinguish their tissue types. The structural composition of the specimens was found to have a significant impact on their mechanical properties, more specifically the extensibility. Specimens with severe atherosclerotic changes exhibited lower extensibility compared with those less impacted by the disease (p-value < 0.005), while no difference was observed in strength. These findings suggest that deformation-related parameters (strains) may be more sensitive to tissue-level disease changes than stress-based measures. A total of 64 computational simulations was performed using patient-specific geometry with isotropic and anisotropic models of individual arterial layers. These models demonstrate that local collagen fibre distribution in the fibrous cap where rupture can occur, is necessary for accurate assessment of strains and stresses. In contrast, population-specific data, such as those obtained in this study, may be sufficient for modelling the outer artery layers where the collagen fibre orientation did not have a significant impact on the strains and stresses in the fibrous cap.

Article.Title: Mitigating common-mode noise in high frequency LLC resonant converters: a parallel interleaved approach
Article.Authors: Zahraei M.; Tahami F.; Rezazadeh G.
Article.Abstract: AbstractThe increasing demands for efficiency and power density in modern applications such as electric vehicles, 5G infrastructure, and data centers have accelerated the adoption of high-frequency DC-DC converters. The use of wide-bandgap semiconductors enables switching frequencies in the megahertz range facilitating the miniaturization of passive components. However, these benefits come with challenges: high dv/dt transitions and parasitic capacitances in planar transformers often result in significant common-mode (CM) noise, leading to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Although conventional mitigation techniques such as structural symmetry, winding balance, and shielding offer partial relief, they frequently necessitate large CM filters. This paper presents an alternative approach by optimizing the magnetic structure and circuit layout of matrix planar transformers to intrinsically suppress CM noise. The proposed methodology is validated through comprehensive high-frequency transformer modeling, circuit-level optimization, and experimental evaluation of a 1 kW GaN-based LLC converter with an input voltage range of 375–405 V and a 48 V output. Results confirm that the proposed design achieves effective CM noise reduction, significantly minimizing the required filter size.

Article.Title: Acclimatization effects on partial pressure of arterial oxygen at high altitude: A systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Fischer H.; Gaisl T.; Forrer A.; Orler N.; Lichtblau M.; Ulrich S.; Furian M.
Article.Abstract: AbstractDuring acclimatization to high altitude with reduced barometric pressure, the rate of increase in PaO2after its initial drop has not been quantitatively described in healthy lowlanders. We therefore performed a systematic search on PubMed and Embase up to 4 October 2025, identifying 39 prospective studies that reported at least two PaO2measurements at > 1500 m in initially unacclimatized healthy adults. Additionally, changes in other blood gas parameters were investigated. The primary outcome was the mean effect and 95%CI for changes in PaO2during high altitude exposure in healthy, unacclimatized lowlanders. Data from 490 participants (mean[SD] age 30.5[5.4] years; 76.1% male), comprising 1109 measurements at a mean altitude of 4140 m (range 1600–5334 m), were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. PaO2showed an increase of 0.1 kPa/day (95%CI − 0.02;0.22;p= 0.10). Across all studies with the first measurement not restricted to day one, the increase was 0.06 kPa/day (95%CI − 0.02;0.15;p= 0.14). Neither altitude nor duration of exposure significantly influenced these estimates. Concurrently, SaO2increased, PaCO2decreased, and pH remained unchanged. Although not reaching statistical significance, the PaO2showed a clear trend of increasing by 0.06 to 0.1 kPa/day at high altitude over an observation period of several weeks. These values may serve as reference estimates for physiological acclimatization in healthy individuals at high altitude.

Article.Title: Urban building change detection with satellite imagery: a temporospatial attention Siamese SNUNet-ECAM framework
Article.Authors: Tiwari V.; Singhal R.; Gangrade S.; R. M.; Gangrade J.
Article.Abstract: AbstractUrban building change monitoring on bi-temporal Very High Resolution (VHR) satellite imagery is critical for land-use monitoring, post-disaster assessment, and urban planning. We use LEVIR-CD, a public benchmark of 637 bi-temporal 1024$$\times$$1024-pixel image pairs at 0.5 m/pixel resolution, collected from Google Earth imagery of 20 regions in Texas, USA, with a 5–14-year interval between acquisitions and a$$\sim$$4.6% building-change pixel ratio. Rather than proposing a new architectural module, this paper presents a systematic integration of a Siamese ResNet50 encoder, the Temporospatial Interactive Attention Module (TIAM), and the SNUNet dense nested decoder with Ensemble Channel Attention (ECAM) — into a single end-to-end trainable pipeline, evaluated on the official LEVIR-CD split. The central empirical finding, based on a controlled ablation, is that full-resolution image tiling (versus resizing) is the dominant driver of performance on this benchmark, improving F1 by 17.11 percentage points (73.24%$$\rightarrow$$90.35%) — an effect several times larger than the combined, measured contribution of the three architectural modules (TIAM +6.83 SNUNet +5.31, ECAM +3.87 F1%). We additionally document three previously unreported training instabilities (NaN propagation from Lovász-Hinge loss, silent fp16 overflow in TIAM’s attention computation, and catastrophic forgetting without progressive unfreezing) along with the engineering fixes that resolve them. Using the decision threshold selected on the validation set (0.56, avoiding test-set threshold tuning and test-set augmentation), the system reaches F1 90.35%, IoU 82.40%, Precision 91.70%, Recall 89.04%, and Overall Accuracy 99.03% on the official LEVIR-CD test split—essentially matching, rather than exceeding, a simpler ResNet-50 U-Net baseline (90.38% F1) and remaining below ChangeFormer (90.40% F1). Notably, our model achieves this comparable performance with substantially fewer parameters than ChangeFormer, demonstrating a more parameter-efficient architecture without sacrificing predictive performance. We report this honestly as evidence that, on this benchmark, correct preprocessing can be as important as architectural sophistication.

Article.Title: Prediction model for complex venous malformation complete remission after sirolimus using clinicopathological and CEUS parameters
Article.Authors: Sun B.; Lei H.; Li M.; Zhang B.; Dong C.
Article.Abstract: AbstractTo develop and validate a machine learning model incorporating clinicopathological features and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) parameters for predicting complete remission (CR) following sirolimus therapy in patients with complex venous malformations (CVM), thereby supporting individualized treatment decisions. A retrospective cohort of 260 CVM patients treated with sirolimus (January 2014-December 2024) was enrolled. Patients were randomly allocated to training (n = 182) and validation (n = 78) sets (7:3 ratio). Baseline clinicopathological (e.g., maximum lesion diameter, volume), CEUS (time-to-peak [TTP], peak intensity [PI]), and laboratory (D-dimer, hemoglobin) data were collected. Univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression were performed to identify independent predictors. Subsequently, random forest, logistic regression, and K-nearest neighbors models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. SHAP values and a nomogram enhanced interpretability. The training set CR rate was 30.77% (56/182). Maximum lesion diameter, volume, TTP, PI, hemoglobin, and D-dimer were significantly associated with CR on univariate analysis (P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified maximum lesion diameter (OR = 0.800), lesion volume (OR = 0.987), TTP (OR = 1.189), PI (OR = 0.815), and D-dimer (per 0.1 mg/L FEU increase: OR = 0.415) as independent predictors (P < 0.05). The RF model yielded an AUC of 0.869 (95%CI: 0.809–0.929) in the training set and 0.766 (95%CI: 0.629–0.902) in the validation set, with satisfactory calibration with satisfactory calibration (calibration intercept and slope close to 0 and 1; Hosmer-Lemeshow P > 0.05), supported by bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit. SHAP value ranking was D-dimer > TTP > PI > maximum lesion diameter > lesion volume. The nomogram enabled individualized CR risk visualization. A random forest model and nomogram based on clinicopathological and CEUS parameters accurately predict sirolimus‑induced CR in CVM patients. Maximum lesion diameter, volume, TTP, PI, and D-dimer are independent predictors. This model offers an effective tool for candidate selection and personalized treatment planning.

Article.Title: Application of depth migration velocity modeling technology based on multi-information constraint in deep seismic imaging
Article.Authors: Cao L.; Gu G.; Wu Y.; Sun S.; Wang S.; Wang Y.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: AbstractAccurate seismic imaging of deep, low signal-to-noise ratio zones in faulted basins remains a persistent challenge. To address this, we propose a pre-stack depth migration (PSDM) velocity modeling workflow that integrates multiple information constraints. Shallow velocities are derived from micro-logging constrained first-arrival inversion, while intermediate and deep interval velocities are converted from root-mean-square velocities using horizon-constrained constrained velocity inversion in the depth domain. Horizon-guided residual velocity analysis is iteratively applied from top to bottom, generating a low-frequency velocity model that captures the structural trends of the faulted basin. Multi-attribute constrained grid tomography—incorporating logging curves, azimuth, dip, continuity, and other seismic attributes—iteratively updates interval velocities through PSDM. The workflow combines model-based tomography for macroscopic along-horizon velocity trend control with multi-attribute constrained grid tomography for high-resolution interval characterization, enabling robust delineation of the faulted basin's velocity architecture and improved interval velocity accuracy. Application to 3-D data from Block H in an eastern China oilfield demonstrates clear sequence contacts, abundant interval details, a well-defined deep basement boundary, and improved imaging quality.

Article.Title: Reboxetine blocks NMDA receptors in a voltage-, use-, and activity-dependent manner
Article.Authors: Föhr K.; Jungwirth B.; Schrezenmeier H.; Messerer D.
Article.Abstract: AbstractReboxetine is a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor which has initially been approved as an antidepressant. In addition, it has been used off label for panic disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, particularly when methylphenidate is ineffective. As the action of other known monoamine reuptake inhibitors, including fluoxetine and atomoxetine, turned out to be effective blockers of NMDA receptors, we analyzed whether reboxetine similarly inhibits NMDA receptors. The whole-cell configuration of the patch-clamp technique was used to analyze the effect of reboxetine on recombinant NMDA receptors transiently expressed in tsA201 cells. Reboxetine reversibly blocked NMDA receptors in a concentration-dependent manner with a half-maximal inhibition of 20.4 ± 3.6 µM, when NMDA (50 µM) and glycine (10 µM) were used to activate GluN2A containing receptors. For GluN2B a corresponding value of 12.6 ± 3.1 µM was estimated. Inhibition increased at higher agonist concentrations, consistent with an uncompetitive, activity-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, the block occurred in a voltage- and use-dependent manner, indicating an open-channel blocking mechanism with an interaction site located deep within the channel pore (zδ = 0.94). In addition, a modest subunit dependence was observed, with greater inhibition of GluN2B- than GluN2A-containing receptors. Finally, Reboxetine belongs to a rare group of NMDA receptor antagonists whose efficacy increases with the concentration of the agonist. This activity-dependent profile is therapeutically attractive because it predicts preferential suppression of pathological NMDA-receptor over-activation while leaving low-frequency physiological signaling comparatively unaffected.
